payload.statement:
For every \(n\ge256\) and \(0<\Delta\le\Delta_0\), the handle \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}\) admits one same-class baseline--alternative realization with both difficulties present.  Specifically, put \(\kappa=c_L/4\), \(b_h(r)=(h_n-r)_+\),
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf 1\{0\le r<\Delta\},
 \qquad
 g_{n,\Delta}(r)=\kappa\{b_h(r)+a_\Delta(r)\}.
\]
There are \(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta}\in\mathcal P_L\) with \(m_{0,0}=m_{0,1}=1/2\), \(m_{1,0}=1/2\), and \(m_{1,1}=1/2+g_{n,\Delta}\), for which
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\!\left(\mathcal L_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n),
 \mathcal L_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n)\right)
 \le\frac14<1-2\alpha
\]
and
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)
 =\kappa(h_n+\Delta).
\]
payload.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\ge256\) and \(0<\Delta\le\Delta_0\), and let \(P_{0,n,\Delta}\) and \(P_{1,n,\Delta}\) be the baseline and alternative laws named by \(\mathrm{def:joint\text{-}lower\text{-}handle}\).  Write \(h=h_n=n^{-1/4}\) and \(\kappa=c_L/4\).  Since \(n\ge256\) and \(\Delta\le\Delta_0\le1/4\),
\[
 0<h\le\frac14,
 \qquad 0<\Delta\le\frac14.
\]
Under either law, \(X\) is uniform on the unit disc \(\mathcal D\), and the two assignment regions are half-discs.  Therefore polar integration gives, for \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(0<H\le1/2\),
\[
 \mathbb P(T=t,R<H)
 =\frac{(\pi H^2)/2}{\pi}
 =\frac{H^2}{2}
 \ge c_0H^2,
\]
where the last inequality uses \(c_0\le1/2\).  Thus the support and two-sided local-mass requirements in \(\mathrm{def:half\text{-}disc\text{-}class}\) hold.  The sharp-assignment, consistency, and conditional Bernoulli requirements hold by the construction and \(\mathrm{ass:sharp\text{-}boundary\text{-}assignment}\), \(\mathrm{ass:consistency}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:radial\text{-}bernoulli}\).

It remains to verify the range and point-anchor requirements.  On \([0,1]\),
\[
 |\phi(u)|=|(1-u)(1-2u)|\le1,
 \qquad
 \phi'(u)=-3+4u,
 \qquad
 |\phi'(u)|\le3.
\]
Because \(\phi(1)=0\), the function \(a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf1\{0\le r<\Delta\}\), extended by zero for \(r\ge\Delta\), is continuous and \(3\)-Lipschitz on \([0,\infty)\).  The function \(b_h(r)=(h-r)_+\) is \(1\)-Lipschitz.  Hence \(g_{n,\Delta}=\kappa(b_h+a_\Delta)\) is \(4\kappa=c_L\)-Lipschitz.  Since \(c_L\le L/8\le L\),
\[
 |g_{n,\Delta}(r)-g_{n,\Delta}(0)|\le Lr.
\]
Moreover, \(c_L\le1/16\), so \(\kappa\le1/64\), and
\[
 |g_{n,\Delta}(r)|
 \le\kappa(h+\Delta)
 \le\frac{1}{128}.
\]
Consequently the alternative treated mean lies in \([0,1]\), and its anchor is
\[
 \theta_{1,1}=\frac12+g_{n,\Delta}(0)
 =\frac12+\kappa(h+\Delta).
\]
The other three side-by-law means are constantly \(1/2\), so their anchors equal \(1/2\) and satisfy the envelope.  This proves
\[
 P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta}\in\mathcal P_L.
\]
By the definition of \(\tau_P(b)\), the common control anchor cancels and therefore
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)
 =g_{n,\Delta}(0)
 =\kappa(h_n+\Delta).
\]

We next bound the distance between the released laws.  Put \(W=(T,Q_\Delta(R))\).  Its law is the same under the two constructions.  Conditional on a positive-probability value of \(W\), \(Y\) is Bernoulli with its conditional average success probability by \(\mathrm{lem:conditional\text{-}local\text{-}binomial\text{-}law}\).  On a control value of \(W\), that probability is \(1/2\) under both laws.  On a treated value, write the alternative-minus-baseline conditional success probability as
\[
 \delta(W)=\kappa\,\mathbb E[b_h(R)+a_\Delta(R)\mid W].
\]
The alias component is zero outside the first bin.  In the first treated bin, uniform-disc polar density is proportional to \(r\), and \(\mathrm{lem:first\text{-}bin\text{-}alias}\) gives \(\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du=0\).  Thus
\[
 \int_0^\Delta r a_\Delta(r)\,dr
 =\Delta^3\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du
 =0.
\]
It follows that, on treated values of \(W\),
\[
 \delta(W)=\kappa\,\mathbb E[b_h(R)\mid W].
\]

Let \(Q_0\) and \(Q_1\) be the one-unit released laws under \(P_{0,n,\Delta}\) and \(P_{1,n,\Delta}\), respectively.  They have the same marginal law of \(W\), and under \(Q_0\), \(Y\mid W\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\).  Hence the likelihood ratio \(L_1=dQ_1/dQ_0\) equals \(1+2\delta(W)\) when \(Y=1\), equals \(1-2\delta(W)\) when \(Y=0\), and equals one on the control side.  Therefore, using conditional Jensen's inequality,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \chi^2(Q_1,Q_0)
 &=\mathbb E_{Q_0}[(L_1-1)^2]\\
 &=4\mathbb E[\mathbf1\{T=1\}\delta(W)^2]\\
 &\le4\kappa^2\mathbb E[\mathbf1\{T=1\}b_h(R)^2].
 \end{aligned}
\]
Uniform-disc polar integration on the treated half-disc now yields
\[
 \mathbb E[\mathbf1\{T=1\}b_h(R)^2]
 =\int_0^h r(h-r)^2\,dr
 =\frac{h^4}{12},
\]
and hence
\[
 \chi^2(Q_1,Q_0)\le\frac{\kappa^2h^4}{3}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\), the product likelihood ratio is \(L_n=\prod_{i=1}^nL_{1,i}\).  Independence gives the exact identity
\[
 1+\chi^2(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 =\mathbb E_{Q_0^{\otimes n}}[L_n^2]
 =\{\mathbb E_{Q_0}[L_1^2]\}^n
 =\{1+\chi^2(Q_1,Q_0)\}^n.
\]
Using \(1+x\le e^x\) and \(nh^4=1\),
\[
 \chi^2(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \le e^{\kappa^2/3}-1.
\]
The defining likelihood-ratio formula for total variation and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 =\frac12\mathbb E_{Q_0^{\otimes n}}|L_n-1|
 \le\frac12\sqrt{e^{\kappa^2/3}-1}.
\]
Since \(0\le\kappa^2/3\le1\), convexity of the exponential on \([0,1]\) implies \(e^x-1\le(e-1)x<2x\) there.  Consequently,
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \le\frac{\kappa}{\sqrt6}
 \le\frac{1}{64\sqrt6}
 <\frac14.
\]
Finally \(\alpha<1/4\) implies \(1-2\alpha>1/2>1/4\), proving the asserted uniform testing bound and completing the construction.

carrier.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\ge256\), \(0<\Delta\le\Delta_0\), and \(C\in\mathcal C_{n,\Delta}(\alpha)\).  Apply \(\mathrm{thm:single\text{-}joint\text{-}pair}\), the resolution of \(\mathrm{oeq:single\text{-}joint\text{-}pair}\), and abbreviate its two released product laws by \(Q_0,Q_1\), its two targets by \(\vartheta_j=\tau_{P_{j,n,\Delta}}(b)\), and their separation by
\[
 d=\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0
 =\kappa(h_n+\Delta),
 \qquad \kappa=\frac{c_L}{4}>0.
\]
Both laws belong to \(\mathcal P_L\), and \(C\) is honest over that class by \(\mathrm{def:honest\text{-}class}\).  Hence
\[
 Q_0\{\vartheta_0\in C\}\ge1-\alpha,
 \qquad
 Q_1\{\vartheta_1\in C\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
The defining supremum characterization of total variation and the joint-pair bound imply
\[
 Q_0\{\vartheta_1\in C\}
 \ge Q_1\{\vartheta_1\in C\}-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)
 \ge1-\alpha-\frac14.
\]
The union bound, applied under \(Q_0\), therefore gives
\[
 Q_0\{\vartheta_0\in C,\ \vartheta_1\in C\}
 \ge1-2\alpha-\frac14
 =\frac34-2\alpha>0.
\]
On this event the interval \(C\) contains both endpoints, so its length is at least \(d\).  It follows equation by equation that
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C)]
 &\ge \mathbb E_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}[\operatorname{length}(C)]\\
 &\ge d\left(\frac34-2\alpha\right)\\
 &=\kappa\left(\frac34-2\alpha\right)(h_n+\Delta)\\
 &\ge\kappa\left(\frac34-2\alpha\right)\rho_{n,\Delta},
 \end{aligned}
\]
where the last line uses \(h_n+\Delta\ge\max\{h_n,\Delta\}=\rho_{n,\Delta}\).  Thus the claimed lower bound holds with
\[
 c_{L,\alpha,\Delta_0}
 =\frac{c_L}{4}\left(\frac34-2\alpha\right)>0;
\]
the notation permits dependence on \(\Delta_0\), although this displayed valid choice does not require it.  Taking the infimum over \(C\in\mathcal C_{n,\Delta}(\alpha)\) proves
\[
 \mathfrak W_{n,\Delta}(\alpha)
 \ge c_{L,\alpha,\Delta_0}\rho_{n,\Delta}.
\]
For the reverse inequality, \(\mathrm{thm:total\text{-}honest\text{-}interval}\) states that the released-sample interval \(C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}\) is everywhere defined, is honest over \(\mathcal P_L\), and has worst-case expected length at most \(C_{L,c_0,\alpha,\Delta_0}\rho_{n,\Delta}\).  By \(\mathrm{def:total\text{-}honest\text{-}interval}\) it is a closed bounded, released-sample measurable interval, hence it belongs to \(\mathcal C_{n,\Delta}(\alpha)\).  The infimum in \(\mathrm{def:honest\text{-}width}\) is therefore no larger than its worst-case expected length. semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), and write
\[
 h=h_n=n^{-1/4},\qquad H=H_{n,\Delta},\qquad B=LH.
\]
The aligned-bandwidth definition gives
\[
 h\leq H<h+\Delta\leq\frac12,
\]
because \(h\leq1/4\) and \(\Delta\leq\Delta_0\leq1/4\).

For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(\mathrm{lem:conditional\text{-}local\text{-}binomial\text{-}law}\) gives
\[
 q_t:=\mathbb P_P(T=t,R<H)\geq c_0H^2>0,
 \qquad
 \nu_t:=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid T=t,R<H],
\]
\[
 |\nu_t-\theta_t|=|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|\leq LH=B,
 \qquad
 N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t),
\]
and, for every count value \(k\) having positive probability,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}\mid\{N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\}
 \sim\operatorname{Binomial}(k,\nu_t).
\]
The equality between rounded and unrounded localization used here is exact because
\[
 \{Q_\Delta(R)<H\}
 =\{\Delta\lfloor R/\Delta\rfloor<K_{n,\Delta}\Delta\}
 =\{R<K_{n,\Delta}\Delta\}
 =\{R<H\}.
\]

If \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=0\), the side interval is \([0,1]\) and contains \(\nu_t\).  If the count is \(k>0\), the revalidated cited leaf \(\mathrm{lem:clopper\text{-}pearson\text{-}conditional\text{-}coverage}\), applied to the conditional binomial law, gives conditional coverage at least \(1-\alpha/2\).  Averaging over the count gives
\[
 \mathbb P_P\{\nu_t\in[\ell_t,u_t]\}\geq1-\alpha/2.
\]
By a union bound there is an event \(E\) of probability at least \(1-\alpha\) on which both side inclusions hold.  On \(E\),
\[
 \nu_1-\nu_0\in[\ell_1-u_0,u_1-\ell_0]
\]
and the two point-anchor bias inequalities imply
\[
 |\tau_P(b)-(\nu_1-\nu_0)|
 =|(\theta_1-\nu_1)-(\theta_0-\nu_0)|
 \leq2B.
\]
Thus \(\tau_P(b)\in C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}\) on \(E\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_L\).

The counts and successes are measurable functions of \(Z_\Delta^n\); the Clopper--Pearson endpoints are functions on a finite count-success state space; and the zero-count branch is explicit.  Since \(0\leq\ell_t\leq u_t\leq1\) and \(B<\infty\), the endpoints in \(\mathrm{def:total\text{-}honest\text{-}interval}\) form an ordered, closed, bounded, \(\sigma(Z_\Delta^n)\)-measurable interval on every sample.  This proves totality and honesty.

For expected length, put \(\beta=\alpha/4>0\).  Fix \(k\geq1\), \(s\in\{0,\ldots,k\}\), set \(\widehat p=s/k\), and write
\[
 I^{\mathrm{CP}}_{k,\alpha/2}(s)=[\ell,u].
\]
For a nontrivial upper endpoint, let \(d=u-\widehat p>0\) and \(W\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(k,u)\).  On \(\{W\leq s\}\), \(|W-ku|\geq kd\), so the upper endpoint equation in the cited leaf and the binomial variance identity yield
\[
 \beta=\mathbb P_u(W\leq s)
 \leq\frac{u(1-u)}{kd^2}
 \leq\frac{\widehat p+d}{kd^2}.
\]
Thus \(d^2\leq \widehat p/(k\beta)+d/(k\beta)\).  If nonnegative numbers satisfy \(d^2\leq A+Dd\), then either \(d\leq D\), or \((d-D)^2\leq d(d-D)\leq A\); in both cases \(d\leq\sqrt A+D\).  Therefore
\[
 u-\widehat p\leq\sqrt{\frac{\widehat p}{k\beta}}+\frac1{k\beta}.
\]
For a nontrivial lower endpoint, set \(d_-=\widehat p-\ell>0\) and take \(W\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(k,\ell)\).  On \(\{W\geq s\}\), \(|W-k\ell|\geq kd_-\).  The lower endpoint equation and \(\ell(1-\ell)\leq\ell\leq\widehat p\) give
\[
 \beta\leq\frac{\ell(1-\ell)}{kd_-^2}
 \leq\frac{\widehat p}{kd_-^2},
 \qquad
 \widehat p-\ell\leq\sqrt{\frac{\widehat p}{k\beta}}.
\]
The cited boundary conventions cover \(s=0\) and \(s=k\), so for every \(s\),
\[
 u-\ell\leq2\sqrt{\frac{\widehat p}{k\beta}}+\frac1{k\beta}.
\]
Conditionally on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k>0\), Jensen's inequality and \(0\leq S_{t,n,\Delta}/k\leq1\) imply
\[
 \mathbb E_P[u_t-\ell_t\mid N_{t,n,\Delta}=k]
 \leq\frac2{\sqrt{k\beta}}+\frac1{k\beta}.
\]

For \(N\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q)\), \(q>0\),
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac1{N+1}\right]
 =\int_0^1(1-q+qx)^n\,dx
 \leq\frac1{(n+1)q}.
\]
Using \(k^{-1}\leq2(k+1)^{-1}\), Cauchy--Schwarz, and \((1-q)^n\leq e^{-nq}\leq(nq)^{-1}\), one obtains
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{N>0\}}N\right]\leq\frac2{nq},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{N>0\}}{\sqrt N}\right]\leq\sqrt{\frac2{nq}},
 \qquad
 \mathbb P(N=0)\leq\frac1{nq}.
\]
The zero-count side interval has length one.  Consequently
\[
 \mathbb E_P[u_t-\ell_t]
 \leq\frac{2\sqrt2}{\sqrt{\beta nq_t}}
 +\left(1+\frac2\beta\right)\frac1{nq_t}
 \leq\frac{2\sqrt2}{\sqrt{\beta c_0nH^2}}
 +\left(1+\frac2\beta\right)\frac1{c_0nH^2}.
\]

The constructed interval has exact length
\[
 \operatorname{length}(C_{n,\Delta,\alpha})
 =(u_1-\ell_1)+(u_0-\ell_0)+4LH.
\]
Finally,
\[
 H<h+\Delta\leq2\rho_{n,\Delta},
 \qquad
 \frac1{\sqrt nH}\leq h\leq\rho_{n,\Delta},
 \qquad
 \frac1{nH^2}\leq h^2\leq\rho_{n,\Delta}.
\]
Summing the two side bounds gives, with \(\beta=\alpha/4\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_{n,\Delta,\alpha})]
 \leq
 \left\{
 \frac{4\sqrt2}{\sqrt{\beta c_0}}
 +\frac{2(1+2/\beta)}{c_0}+8L
 \right\}\rho_{n,\Delta}.
\]
This finite constant has the permitted dependence on \(L,c_0,\alpha,\Delta_0\) and is uniform in every allowed \(n\) and \(\Delta\).

\[
 |\mu_t(x)-\theta_t|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
\]
holds for every \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every side-\(t\) point \(x\) of radius at most \(1/2\), where \(\theta_t\in[0,1]\) and \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\).  The sampling condition \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) is imposed on the sample and is not a member property of a one-unit law.

semantic_closure.name: Embedded uniform-half-disc joint lower handle
semantic_closure.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}=(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta})\) denote the following pair.  Under both laws, \(X\) is uniform on \(\mathcal D\), \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assignment is sharp, and the control mean is \(1/2\).  Under \(P_{0,n,\Delta}\) the treated mean is \(1/2\); under \(P_{1,n,\Delta}\) it is
\[
 \frac12+\frac{c_L}{4}\left\{(h_n-\lVert x-b\rVert_2)_+
 +\Delta\phi\!\left(\frac{\lVert x-b\rVert_2}{\Delta}\right)
 \mathbf1\{\lVert x-b\rVert_2<\Delta\}\right\}.
\]
Given \(X\), the potential outcomes are conditionally independent Bernoulli variables with these means, and \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\).

semantic_closure.statement: For every \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), \(\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du=0\), both \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}\) and \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}\) belong to \(\mathcal P_L\), their released one-unit laws of \(Z_\Delta\) are identical, and \(\tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}}(b)=2c_L\Delta\).
semantic_closure.justification: This certifies an exact order-\(\Delta\) alias in a legal uniform-half-disc subclass of the unknown-design point-anchored model, without asserting design-wide orthogonality.
semantic_closure.gap: Scalar rounding results do not furnish the radial-Jacobian null direction for a release that hides bivariate coordinates within annuli.
semantic_closure.consumer: Data stewards using released radial bins can see that no sample size removes the first-bin resolution floor.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
The polynomial specified in \(\mathrm{def:first\text{-}bin\text{-}alias}\) is
\[
 \phi(u)=1-3u+2u^2,
 \qquad
 \int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du
 =\int_0^1(u-3u^2+2u^3)\,du
 =\frac12-1+\frac12=0.
\]
Furthermore, \(\phi(1)=0\), \(|\phi(u)|\leq1\) for \(u\in[0,1]\), and \(\phi'(u)=-3+4u\), whence \(\sup_{u\in[0,1]}|\phi'(u)|=3\).  Define
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf1\{0\leq r<\Delta\}.
\]
Because the two pieces agree at \(r=\Delta\), the preceding derivative bound shows that \(a_\Delta\) is continuous and \(3\)-Lipschitz on \([0,1]\).  The radius map is \(1\)-Lipschitz, since
\[
 \bigl|\lVert x-b\rVert_2-\lVert x'-b\rVert_2\bigr|
 \leq\lVert x-x'\rVert_2.
\]

Consider either law in \(\mathrm{def:first\text{-}bin\text{-}alias}\).  Choose the control anchor \(\theta_0=1/2\) and the treated anchor
\[
 \theta_{1,\pm}=\frac12\pm c_L\Delta
 =\frac12\pm c_La_\Delta(0).
\]
For every treated point \(x\) with radius \(r\leq1/2\), the point-anchor deviation is
\[
 |\mu_{1,\pm}(x)-\theta_{1,\pm}|
 =c_L|a_\Delta(r)-a_\Delta(0)|
 \leq3c_Lr\leq Lr,
\]
where the last inequality follows from \(c_L\leq L/8\).  The corresponding control deviation is zero.  Also
\[
 |c_La_\Delta(r)|\leq c_L\Delta
 \leq\frac1{16}\frac14=\frac1{64},
\]
using \(c_L\leq1/16\) and \(\Delta\leq\Delta_0\leq1/4\); hence all constructed Bernoulli means lie in \([0,1]\).  Thus the Bernoulli and point-anchor member conditions hold.

The construction supplies the known half-plane partition, sharp assignment, consistency, and conditionally Bernoulli potential outcomes.  Uniformity of \(X\) on the unit disc and polar integration give, for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(0<H\leq1/2\),
\[
 \mathbb P(T=t,R<H)
 =\frac1\pi\int_{\Theta_t}\int_0^H r\,dr\,d\vartheta
 =\frac{H^2}{2}
 \geq c_0H^2,
 \qquad |\Theta_t|=\pi,
\]
by \(c_0\leq1/2\).  Consequently both constructed laws are members of the unknown-design point-anchored class \(\mathcal P_L\).  This verifies membership through an embedded uniform-half-disc subclass only; it does not assert the alias identity for an arbitrary design in \(\mathcal P_L\).

The distribution of \((T,Q_\Delta(R))\) is common to the two signs.  Within the treated first bin, the difference of their joint success masses is
\[
 \frac1\pi\int_{\Theta_1}\int_0^\Delta
 2c_L\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)r\,dr\,d\vartheta
 =2c_L\Delta^3\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du=0.
\]
Outside this bin the perturbation vanishes, and every control cell is unchanged.  Since \(Y\) is binary, equality of each released cell's total mass and success mass also gives equality of its failure mass.  Hence the entire one-unit laws of \(Z_\Delta=(Y,T,Q_\Delta(R))\) coincide.  Finally, by \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\) and \(\phi(0)=1\),
\[
 \tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}}(b)=c_L\Delta,
 \qquad
 \tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}}(b)=-c_L\Delta,
\]
so their difference is \(2c_L\Delta\), as claimed.

semantic_closure.name: Bias-enlarged conditional-count exact-binomial interval
semantic_closure.construction:
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), set \([\ell_t,u_t]=[0,1]\) when \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=0\), and set \([\ell_t,u_t]=I^{\mathrm{CP}}_{N_{t,n,\Delta},\alpha/2}(S_{t,n,\Delta})\) when \(N_{t,n,\Delta}>0\).  With \(B_{n,\Delta}=LH_{n,\Delta}\), define the closed bounded interval
\[
 C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}
 =\bigl[\ell_1-u_0-2B_{n,\Delta},\ u_1-\ell_0+2B_{n,\Delta}\bigr].
\]

semantic_closure.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  For every event \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) with \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\),
\[
 Y\mid B\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}\!\left(\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B]\right).
\]
In particular, put \(A_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Then \(A_t=\{T=t,R<H_{n,\Delta}\}\), its probability \(q_t\) is at least \(c_0H_{n,\Delta}^2>0\), and, with
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t],
\]
one has \(|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|\leq LH_{n,\Delta}\), \(N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\), and
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}\mid N_{t,n,\Delta}=k
 \sim\operatorname{Binomial}(k,\nu_t)
 \quad\text{for every }k\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\text{ with }\mathbb P_P(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k)>0.
\]
semantic_closure.justification: This lemma supplies the conditional-count likelihood and the explicit point-anchor bias uniformly over unknown bivariate designs.
semantic_closure.gap: Exact-radius and scalar-running-variable analyses do not state the conditional Bernoulli law after retaining only side and quantized radius under an unknown bivariate design.
semantic_closure.consumer: The count law is the implementation contract for the bin-aware estimator and the total confidence interval.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Let \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) satisfy \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\).  Consistency gives \(Y=Y(t)\) on \(B\).  The conditional Bernoulli member condition and iterated conditioning therefore imply
\[
 \mathbb P_P(Y=1\mid B)
 =\mathbb E_P\!\left[\mathbb P_P(Y(t)=1\mid X)\mid B\right]
 =\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
As \(Y\in\{0,1\}\), its conditional law is determined by this success probability, proving the first assertion.

Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:boundary\text{-}anchor\text{-}uniqueness}\) ensures that the declared \(\theta_t=\mu_t(b)\) is a well-defined functional of the law rather than a choice of regression version.

Put \(h=h_n\), \(H=H_{n,\Delta}\), and \(K=K_{n,\Delta}\).  Since \(H=K\Delta\), the floor quantizer satisfies, pointwise on \([0,1]\),
\[
 Q_\Delta(R)<H
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \lfloor R/\Delta\rfloor<K
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad R<K\Delta=H.
\]
Moreover, \(n\geq256\) and \(\Delta\leq\Delta_0\leq1/4\) give
\[
 0<h=n^{-1/4}\leq\frac14,
 \qquad h\leq H<h+\Delta\leq\frac12.
\]
Thus the two-sided local-mass member condition applies and yields
\[
 q_t:=\mathbb P_P(A_t)
 =\mathbb P_P(T=t,R<H)
 \geq c_0H^2>0.
\]
The first part of the proof with \(B=A_t\) shows that \(Y\mid A_t\) is Bernoulli with parameter
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t].
\]
The point-anchored envelope applies \(P_X\)-almost surely throughout \(A_t\).  Using \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\), conditional Jensen's inequality for absolute value, and \(R<H\) on \(A_t\), one obtains
\[
 |\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|
 =|\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)-\theta_t\mid A_t]|
 \leq\mathbb E_P[|\mu_t(X)-\theta_t|\mid A_t]
 \leq L\mathbb E_P[R\mid A_t]
 \leq LH.
\]

By independent identical sampling, the pairs
\[
 \left(\mathbf1\{A_{t,i}\},\mathbf1\{A_{t,i}\}Y_i\right),
 \qquad i=1,\ldots,n,
\]
are iid.  Hence \(N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\).  Their one-unit joint probability generating function, with \(w\) marking local membership and \(z\) marking a success, is
\[
 1-q_t+q_t(1-\nu_t)w+q_t\nu_twz.
\]
After taking the \(n\)-th power, the coefficient of \(w^k\) is proportional to \((1-\nu_t+\nu_tz)^k\).  Conditional on every count value \(k\) of positive probability, this is the probability generating function of \(\operatorname{Binomial}(k,\nu_t)\), proving the final assertion, including the degenerate case \(k=0\).

semantic_closure.statement: For every integer \(k\geq1\), if \(S\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(k,p)\), then the equal-tailed Clopper--Pearson interval \(I^{\mathrm{CP}}_{k,\alpha/2}(S)\) covers \(p\) with probability at least \(1-\alpha/2\). semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Put \(h=h_n\), \(H=H_{n,\Delta}\), and \(\rho=\rho_{n,\Delta}\).  From \(H=\Delta\lceil h/\Delta\rceil\), \(n\geq256\), and \(\Delta\leq\Delta_0\leq1/4\),
\[
 h\leq H<h+\Delta\leq2\rho,
 \qquad 0<H\leq\frac12.
\]
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  Use \(A_t,q_t,\nu_t,N_t,S_t\) from \(\mathrm{lem:conditional\text{-}local\text{-}binomial\text{-}law}\).  That lemma and the definition \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\) give
\[
 q_t\geq c_0H^2,
 \qquad |\nu_t-\theta_t|\leq LH,
 \qquad N_t\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t),
 \qquad S_t\mid N_t=k\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(k,\nu_t).
\]
In particular, \(0\leq\nu_t\leq1\).

For \(N\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q)\) with \(q>0\), integrating its probability generating function gives
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac1{N+1}\right]
 =\int_0^1(1-q+qx)^n\,dx
 =\frac{1-(1-q)^{n+1}}{(n+1)q}
 \leq\frac1{(n+1)q}.
\]
Since \(k^{-1}\leq2(k+1)^{-1}\) for \(k\geq1\), and then by Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{N>0\}}N\right]\leq\frac2{nq},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{N>0\}}{\sqrt N}\right]
 \leq\sqrt{\frac2{nq}}.
\]
Also \((1-q)^n\leq e^{-nq}\).  The elementary inequalities \(x^{1/2}e^{-x}\leq1\) and \(xe^{-x}\leq1\) for \(x>0\) imply
\[
 \mathbb P(N=0)\leq(nq)^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 \mathbb P(N=0)\leq(nq)^{-1}.
\]

On \(N_t=k>0\), clipping does nothing because \(0\leq S_t/k\leq1\).  The ratio has conditional mean \(\nu_t\) and variance \(\nu_t(1-\nu_t)/k\leq1/(4k)\).  On \(N_t=0\), the fixed fallback obeys
\[
 |1/2-\nu_t|\leq\frac12,
 \qquad (1/2-\nu_t)^2\leq\frac14,
\]
which uses only the full Bernoulli range \([0,1]\).  Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz and the inverse-count bounds therefore give
\[
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}-\nu_t|
 \leq\frac12\sqrt{\frac2{nq_t}}
      +\frac1{2\sqrt{nq_t}}
 =\left(\frac1{\sqrt2}+\frac12\right)\frac1{\sqrt{nq_t}},
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[(\widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}-\nu_t)^2]
 \leq\frac14\frac2{nq_t}+\frac14\frac1{nq_t}
 =\frac3{4nq_t}.
\]
Adding the point-anchor bias and using \((a+b)^2\leq2a^2+2b^2\) yield
\[
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}-\theta_t|
 \leq LH+\left(\frac1{\sqrt2}+\frac12\right)
              \frac1{\sqrt{c_0nH^2}},
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[(\widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}-\theta_t)^2]
 \leq2L^2H^2+\frac3{2c_0nH^2}.
\]
Since \(H\geq h=n^{-1/4}\),
\[
 \frac1{\sqrt nH}\leq h\leq\rho,
 \qquad
 \frac1{nH^2}\leq h^2\leq\rho^2.
\]
The identity \(\tau_P(b)=\theta_1-\theta_0\), the triangle inequality, and \((x-y)^2\leq2x^2+2y^2\) now imply constants \(C_1,C_2<\infty\), depending only on \(L\) and \(c_0\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}-\tau_P(b)|\leq C_1\rho,
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}
 \mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}-\tau_P(b))^2]\leq C_2\rho^2.
\]
The counts and successes are measurable functions of \(Z_\Delta^n\), and the zero-count branch is fixed, so \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}\) is one law-independent member of \(\mathcal T_{n,\Delta}\).  Taking the infima in \(\mathrm{def:minimax\text{-}risks}\) proves both upper bounds.

For the converse, use the pair in \(\mathrm{thm:single\text{-}joint\text{-}pair}\).  Its two laws belong to the embedded uniform-half-disc subclass and hence to the unknown-design point-anchored superclass.  Let \(Q_0,Q_1\) be their released product laws, let \(\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1\) be their targets, and set \(\delta=|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|\).  The theorem gives
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\leq\frac14,
 \qquad
 \delta=\kappa(h+\Delta)\geq\kappa\rho,
 \qquad \kappa=\frac{c_L}{4}>0.
\]
For any released-data estimator \(a\), take densities \(q_0,q_1\) with respect to \(Q_0+Q_1\).  Pointwise,
\[
 |a-\vartheta_0|+|a-\vartheta_1|\geq\delta,
 \qquad
 (a-\vartheta_0)^2+(a-\vartheta_1)^2\geq\frac{\delta^2}{2},
\]
and \(\int\min(q_0,q_1)=1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\).  Multiplying by the minimum density, integrating, and bounding a maximum below by half the sum give
\[
 \max_{j\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_{Q_j}|a-\vartheta_j|
 \geq\frac\delta2\{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\}
 \geq\frac{3\kappa}{8}\rho,
\]
and
\[
 \max_{j\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_{Q_j}(a-\vartheta_j)^2
 \geq\frac{\delta^2}{4}\{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\}
 \geq\frac{3\kappa^2}{16}\rho^2.
\]
The supremum over \(\mathcal P_L\) dominates the maximum over this pair.  Taking the infimum over estimators proves the lower bounds.  Choose \(c\) as the smaller of the two displayed lower constants and choose \(C\) larger than \(c\), \(C_1\), and \(C_2\).  This proves the simultaneous assertion with the allowed dependence on \(L,c_0,\Delta_0\).

semantic_closure.statement:
For every \(n\ge256\) and \(0<\Delta\le\Delta_0\), the handle \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}\) admits one same-class baseline--alternative realization with both difficulties present.  Specifically, put \(\kappa=c_L/4\), \(b_h(r)=(h_n-r)_+\),
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf 1\{0\le r<\Delta\},
 \qquad
 g_{n,\Delta}(r)=\kappa\{b_h(r)+a_\Delta(r)\}.
\]
There are \(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta}\in\mathcal P_L\) with \(m_{0,0}=m_{0,1}=1/2\), \(m_{1,0}=1/2\), and \(m_{1,1}=1/2+g_{n,\Delta}\), for which
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\!\left(\mathcal L_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n),
 \mathcal L_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n)\right)
 \le\frac14<1-2\alpha
\]
and
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)
 =\kappa(h_n+\Delta).
\]
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\ge256\) and \(0<\Delta\le\Delta_0\), and let \(P_{0,n,\Delta}\) and \(P_{1,n,\Delta}\) be the baseline and alternative laws named by \(\mathrm{def:joint\text{-}lower\text{-}handle}\).  Write \(h=h_n=n^{-1/4}\) and \(\kappa=c_L/4\).  Since \(n\ge256\) and \(\Delta\le\Delta_0\le1/4\),
\[
 0<h\le\frac14,
 \qquad 0<\Delta\le\frac14.
\]
Under either law, \(X\) is uniform on the unit disc \(\mathcal D\), and the two assignment regions are half-discs.  Therefore polar integration gives, for \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(0<H\le1/2\),
\[
 \mathbb P(T=t,R<H)
 =\frac{(\pi H^2)/2}{\pi}
 =\frac{H^2}{2}
 \ge c_0H^2,
\]
where the last inequality uses \(c_0\le1/2\).  Thus the support and two-sided local-mass requirements in \(\mathrm{def:half\text{-}disc\text{-}class}\) hold.  The sharp-assignment, consistency, and conditional Bernoulli requirements hold by the construction and \(\mathrm{ass:sharp\text{-}boundary\text{-}assignment}\), \(\mathrm{ass:consistency}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:radial\text{-}bernoulli}\).

It remains to verify the range and point-anchor requirements.  On \([0,1]\),
\[
 |\phi(u)|=|(1-u)(1-2u)|\le1,
 \qquad
 \phi'(u)=-3+4u,
 \qquad
 |\phi'(u)|\le3.
\]
Because \(\phi(1)=0\), the function \(a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf1\{0\le r<\Delta\}\), extended by zero for \(r\ge\Delta\), is continuous and \(3\)-Lipschitz on \([0,\infty)\).  The function \(b_h(r)=(h-r)_+\) is \(1\)-Lipschitz.  Hence \(g_{n,\Delta}=\kappa(b_h+a_\Delta)\) is \(4\kappa=c_L\)-Lipschitz.  Since \(c_L\le L/8\le L\),
\[
 |g_{n,\Delta}(r)-g_{n,\Delta}(0)|\le Lr.
\]
Moreover, \(c_L\le1/16\), so \(\kappa\le1/64\), and
\[
 |g_{n,\Delta}(r)|
 \le\kappa(h+\Delta)
 \le\frac{1}{128}.
\]
Consequently the alternative treated mean lies in \([0,1]\), and its anchor is
\[
 \theta_{1,1}=\frac12+g_{n,\Delta}(0)
 =\frac12+\kappa(h+\Delta).
\]
The other three side-by-law means are constantly \(1/2\), so their anchors equal \(1/2\) and satisfy the envelope.  This proves
\[
 P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta}\in\mathcal P_L.
\]
By the definition of \(\tau_P(b)\), the common control anchor cancels and therefore
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)
 =g_{n,\Delta}(0)
 =\kappa(h_n+\Delta).
\]

We next bound the distance between the released laws.  Put \(W=(T,Q_\Delta(R))\).  Its law is the same under the two constructions.  Conditional on a positive-probability value of \(W\), \(Y\) is Bernoulli with its conditional average success probability by \(\mathrm{lem:conditional\text{-}local\text{-}binomial\text{-}law}\).  On a control value of \(W\), that probability is \(1/2\) under both laws.  On a treated value, write the alternative-minus-baseline conditional success probability as
\[
 \delta(W)=\kappa\,\mathbb E[b_h(R)+a_\Delta(R)\mid W].
\]
The alias component is zero outside the first bin.  In the first treated bin, uniform-disc polar density is proportional to \(r\), and \(\mathrm{lem:first\text{-}bin\text{-}alias}\) gives \(\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du=0\).  Thus
\[
 \int_0^\Delta r a_\Delta(r)\,dr
 =\Delta^3\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du
 =0.
\]
It follows that, on treated values of \(W\),
\[
 \delta(W)=\kappa\,\mathbb E[b_h(R)\mid W].
\]

Let \(Q_0\) and \(Q_1\) be the one-unit released laws under \(P_{0,n,\Delta}\) and \(P_{1,n,\Delta}\), respectively.  They have the same marginal law of \(W\), and under \(Q_0\), \(Y\mid W\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\).  Hence the likelihood ratio \(L_1=dQ_1/dQ_0\) equals \(1+2\delta(W)\) when \(Y=1\), equals \(1-2\delta(W)\) when \(Y=0\), and equals one on the control side.  Therefore, using conditional Jensen's inequality,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \chi^2(Q_1,Q_0)
 &=\mathbb E_{Q_0}[(L_1-1)^2]\\
 &=4\mathbb E[\mathbf1\{T=1\}\delta(W)^2]\\
 &\le4\kappa^2\mathbb E[\mathbf1\{T=1\}b_h(R)^2].
 \end{aligned}
\]
Uniform-disc polar integration on the treated half-disc now yields
\[
 \mathbb E[\mathbf1\{T=1\}b_h(R)^2]
 =\int_0^h r(h-r)^2\,dr
 =\frac{h^4}{12},
\]
and hence
\[
 \chi^2(Q_1,Q_0)\le\frac{\kappa^2h^4}{3}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\), the product likelihood ratio is \(L_n=\prod_{i=1}^nL_{1,i}\).  Independence gives the exact identity
\[
 1+\chi^2(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 =\mathbb E_{Q_0^{\otimes n}}[L_n^2]
 =\{\mathbb E_{Q_0}[L_1^2]\}^n
 =\{1+\chi^2(Q_1,Q_0)\}^n.
\]
Using \(1+x\le e^x\) and \(nh^4=1\),
\[
 \chi^2(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \le e^{\kappa^2/3}-1.
\]
The defining likelihood-ratio formula for total variation and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 =\frac12\mathbb E_{Q_0^{\otimes n}}|L_n-1|
 \le\frac12\sqrt{e^{\kappa^2/3}-1}.
\]
Since \(0\le\kappa^2/3\le1\), convexity of the exponential on \([0,1]\) implies \(e^x-1\le(e-1)x<2x\) there.  Consequently,
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \le\frac{\kappa}{\sqrt6}
 \le\frac{1}{64\sqrt6}
 <\frac14.
\]
Finally \(\alpha<1/4\) implies \(1-2\alpha>1/2>1/4\), proving the asserted uniform testing bound and completing the construction.

semantic_closure.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_L\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), there is at most one \(a\in[0,1]\) such that \(|\mu_t(x)-a|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) with \(\lVert x-b\rVert_2\leq1/2\). semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  Suppose \(a,a'\in[0,1]\) each satisfies the displayed point-anchor envelope.  For any \(H\in(0,1/2]\), the local-mass member condition gives
\[
 \mathbb P_P(T=t,R<H)\geq c_0H^2>0.
\]
Each candidate envelope holds outside a \(P_X\)-null subset of the side-\(t\), radius-at-most-\(1/2\) region.  Removing the union of those two null sets from \(\{T=t,R<H\}\) leaves a nonempty set.  At any \(x\) in that set,
\[
 |a-a'|
 \leq|a-\mu_t(x)|+|\mu_t(x)-a'|
 \leq2L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
 <2LH.
\]
This holds for every \(H\in(0,1/2]\).  Taking \(H\downarrow0\) gives \(|a-a'|=0\), hence \(a=a'\).  Existence of the declared anchor is part of the class construction, so it is unique for each side.  Therefore \(\theta_t\), and hence \(\tau_P(b)=\theta_1-\theta_0\), is a well-defined functional of \(P\).

There is a known Borel side partition \((\mathcal X_{0,P},\mathcal X_{1,P})\) of \(\mathcal D\) such that \(T=\mathbf 1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\) almost surely under \(P\).

semantic_closure.name: Embedded uniform-half-disc exact first-bin alias pair
semantic_closure.construction:
For each sign, construct \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{\pm,\Delta}\) by drawing \(X\) uniformly on \(\mathcal D\), taking \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assigning \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\), and drawing conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes given \(X\) with
\[
 \mu_{0,\pm}(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mu_{1,\pm}(x)=\frac12\pm c_L\Delta\phi\!\left(\frac{\lVert x-b\rVert_2}{\Delta}\right)
 \mathbf1\{\lVert x-b\rVert_2<\Delta\}.
\]
Finally set \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\), where \(\phi(u)=(1-u)(1-2u)\) and \(c_L=\min\{L/8,1/16\}\).

semantic_closure.def: The observed-count ratio with fixed zero-count fallback constructed in \(\mathrm{def:bin\text{-}aware\text{-}estimator}\).

semantic_closure.name: \mathcal T_{n,\Delta}
semantic_closure.def: All law-independent estimators measurable with respect to the released sample only.

carrier.proof_tex:
Recall from the definition of the sampling--aliasing frontier that
\[
 \rho_{n,\Delta}=\max\{n^{-1/4},\Delta\}.
\]
Along any sequence satisfying \(0<\Delta\le n^{-1/4}\), this identity gives \(\rho_{n,\Delta}=n^{-1/4}\) and \(\rho_{n,\Delta}^2=n^{-1/2}\).  Substitution into the two uniform equivalences of \(\mathrm{thm:minimax\text{-}frontier}\) yields minimax absolute-error order \(n^{-1/4}\) and squared-risk order \(n^{-1/2}\); substitution into \(\mathrm{thm:honest\text{-}length\text{-}lower}\), whose proof also supplies the matching upper bound, yields honest expected-length order \(n^{-1/4}\).

Along any sequence satisfying \(n^{-1/4}=o(\Delta)\), the ratio \(n^{-1/4}/\Delta\) tends to zero.  Hence \(n^{-1/4}<\Delta\) eventually, so eventually
\[
 \rho_{n,\Delta}=\Delta,
 \qquad
 \rho_{n,\Delta}^2=\Delta^2.
\]
The same substitutions into \(\mathrm{thm:minimax\text{-}frontier}\) and \(\mathrm{thm:honest\text{-}length\text{-}lower}\) give, respectively, minimax absolute-error and honest expected-length order \(\Delta\), and minimax squared-risk order \(\Delta^2\), as asserted.

target_declaration.statement: Along every sequence with \(0<\Delta\leq n^{-1/4}\), the unknown-design frontier has minimax absolute-error and honest expected-length order \(n^{-1/4}\) and squared-risk order \(n^{-1/2}\).  Along every sequence with \(n^{-1/4}=o(\Delta)\), the corresponding orders are \(\Delta\) and \(\Delta^2\), respectively.
target_declaration.justification: This separates the fine-quantization sampling regime from the coarsening-dominated regime without claiming equivalence to an exact-score theorem.
target_declaration.gap: The exact-score literature is a rate sanity check only; it does not imply the latent-annular experiment proved here.
target_declaration.consumer: Applied users can diagnose whether sample size or released radial precision is the active constraint.

semantic_closure.statement: There exist constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \(L\), \(c_0\), and \(\Delta_0\), such that for every \(n\geq256\) and \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), \(c\rho_{n,\Delta}\leq\mathfrak R^{(1)}_{n,\Delta}\leq C\rho_{n,\Delta}\) and \(c\rho_{n,\Delta}^2\leq\mathfrak R^{(2)}_{n,\Delta}\leq C\rho_{n,\Delta}^2\). The upper bounds are attained, up to \(C\), by \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}\).
semantic_closure.justification: This is the sampling--quantization minimax frontier over the unknown-design bivariate Lipschitz boundary class.
semantic_closure.gap: Exact-radius boundary methods and ordinary scalar rounding methods do not derive the latent-annular rate \(\max\{n^{-1/4},\Delta\}\) over this superclass.
semantic_closure.consumer: The result tells users of the \(\texttt{rd2d}\) R, Python, and Stata workflows when the Ser Pilo Paga analysis is sample-limited or release-precision-limited.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Put \(h=h_n\), \(H=H_{n,\Delta}\), and \(\rho=\rho_{n,\Delta}\).  From \(H=\Delta\lceil h/\Delta\rceil\), \(n\geq256\), and \(\Delta\leq\Delta_0\leq1/4\),
\[
 h\leq H<h+\Delta\leq2\rho,
 \qquad 0<H\leq\frac12.
\]
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  Use \(A_t,q_t,\nu_t,N_t,S_t\) from \(\mathrm{lem:conditional\text{-}local\text{-}binomial\text{-}law}\).  That lemma and the definition \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\) give
\[
 q_t\geq c_0H^2,
 \qquad |\nu_t-\theta_t|\leq LH,
 \qquad N_t\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t),
 \qquad S_t\mid N_t=k\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(k,\nu_t).
\]
In particular, \(0\leq\nu_t\leq1\).

For \(N\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q)\) with \(q>0\), integrating its probability generating function gives
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac1{N+1}\right]
 =\int_0^1(1-q+qx)^n\,dx
 =\frac{1-(1-q)^{n+1}}{(n+1)q}
 \leq\frac1{(n+1)q}.
\]
Since \(k^{-1}\leq2(k+1)^{-1}\) for \(k\geq1\), and then by Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{N>0\}}N\right]\leq\frac2{nq},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{N>0\}}{\sqrt N}\right]
 \leq\sqrt{\frac2{nq}}.
\]
Also \((1-q)^n\leq e^{-nq}\).  The elementary inequalities \(x^{1/2}e^{-x}\leq1\) and \(xe^{-x}\leq1\) for \(x>0\) imply
\[
 \mathbb P(N=0)\leq(nq)^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 \mathbb P(N=0)\leq(nq)^{-1}.
\]

On \(N_t=k>0\), clipping does nothing because \(0\leq S_t/k\leq1\).  The ratio has conditional mean \(\nu_t\) and variance \(\nu_t(1-\nu_t)/k\leq1/(4k)\).  On \(N_t=0\), the fixed fallback obeys
\[
 |1/2-\nu_t|\leq\frac12,
 \qquad (1/2-\nu_t)^2\leq\frac14,
\]
which uses only the full Bernoulli range \([0,1]\).  Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz and the inverse-count bounds therefore give
\[
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}-\nu_t|
 \leq\frac12\sqrt{\frac2{nq_t}}
      +\frac1{2\sqrt{nq_t}}
 =\left(\frac1{\sqrt2}+\frac12\right)\frac1{\sqrt{nq_t}},
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[(\widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}-\nu_t)^2]
 \leq\frac14\frac2{nq_t}+\frac14\frac1{nq_t}
 =\frac3{4nq_t}.
\]
Adding the point-anchor bias and using \((a+b)^2\leq2a^2+2b^2\) yield
\[
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}-\theta_t|
 \leq LH+\left(\frac1{\sqrt2}+\frac12\right)
              \frac1{\sqrt{c_0nH^2}},
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[(\widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}-\theta_t)^2]
 \leq2L^2H^2+\frac3{2c_0nH^2}.
\]
Since \(H\geq h=n^{-1/4}\),
\[
 \frac1{\sqrt nH}\leq h\leq\rho,
 \qquad
 \frac1{nH^2}\leq h^2\leq\rho^2.
\]
The identity \(\tau_P(b)=\theta_1-\theta_0\), the triangle inequality, and \((x-y)^2\leq2x^2+2y^2\) now imply constants \(C_1,C_2<\infty\), depending only on \(L\) and \(c_0\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}-\tau_P(b)|\leq C_1\rho,
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}
 \mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}-\tau_P(b))^2]\leq C_2\rho^2.
\]
The counts and successes are measurable functions of \(Z_\Delta^n\), and the zero-count branch is fixed, so \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}\) is one law-independent member of \(\mathcal T_{n,\Delta}\).  Taking the infima in \(\mathrm{def:minimax\text{-}risks}\) proves both upper bounds.

For the converse, use the pair in \(\mathrm{thm:single\text{-}joint\text{-}pair}\).  Its two laws belong to the embedded uniform-half-disc subclass and hence to the unknown-design point-anchored superclass.  Let \(Q_0,Q_1\) be their released product laws, let \(\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1\) be their targets, and set \(\delta=|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|\).  The theorem gives
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\leq\frac14,
 \qquad
 \delta=\kappa(h+\Delta)\geq\kappa\rho,
 \qquad \kappa=\frac{c_L}{4}>0.
\]
For any released-data estimator \(a\), take densities \(q_0,q_1\) with respect to \(Q_0+Q_1\).  Pointwise,
\[
 |a-\vartheta_0|+|a-\vartheta_1|\geq\delta,
 \qquad
 (a-\vartheta_0)^2+(a-\vartheta_1)^2\geq\frac{\delta^2}{2},
\]
and \(\int\min(q_0,q_1)=1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\).  Multiplying by the minimum density, integrating, and bounding a maximum below by half the sum give
\[
 \max_{j\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_{Q_j}|a-\vartheta_j|
 \geq\frac\delta2\{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\}
 \geq\frac{3\kappa}{8}\rho,
\]
and
\[
 \max_{j\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_{Q_j}(a-\vartheta_j)^2
 \geq\frac{\delta^2}{4}\{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\}
 \geq\frac{3\kappa^2}{16}\rho^2.
\]
The supremum over \(\mathcal P_L\) dominates the maximum over this pair.  Taking the infimum over estimators proves the lower bounds.  Choose \(c\) as the smaller of the two displayed lower constants and choose \(C\) larger than \(c\), \(C_1\), and \(C_2\).  This proves the simultaneous assertion with the allowed dependence on \(L,c_0,\Delta_0\).

semantic_closure.statement: There is a constant \(c_{L,\alpha,\Delta_0}>0\) such that, for every \(n\geq256\) and \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), every \(C\in\mathcal C_{n,\Delta}(\alpha)\) satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C)]\geq c_{L,\alpha,\Delta_0}\rho_{n,\Delta}\); hence \(\mathfrak W_{n,\Delta}(\alpha)\asymp\rho_{n,\Delta}\).
semantic_closure.justification: The expected-length lower bound certifies that the total interval pays exactly the information loss forced by the release protocol.
semantic_closure.gap: ArmstrongKolesar2018Optimal gives general modulus lower bounds and KolesarRothe2018Discrete gives discrete-RD intervals, but neither evaluates the rounded radial modulus or its \(n^{-1/4}\)-to-\(\Delta\) transition.
semantic_closure.consumer: The lower bound provides a performance certificate for software defaults and prevents misleading interval comparisons that ignore impossible within-bin recovery.

semantic_closure.name: Unknown-design bivariate Bernoulli point-anchored boundary class
semantic_closure.construction:
\(\mathcal P_L\) is the set of one-unit laws \(P\) such that \(P_X(\mathcal D)=1\); for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(H\in(0,1/2]\), \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\); \((\mathcal X_{0,P},\mathcal X_{1,P})\) is a known Borel partition of \(\mathcal D\) and \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\) almost surely; \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\) almost surely; for each \(t\), \(Y(t)\mid X=x\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\mu_t(x))\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\); and the point-anchored envelope
\[
 |\mu_t(x)-\theta_t|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
\]
holds for every \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every side-\(t\) point \(x\) of radius at most \(1/2\), where \(\theta_t\in[0,1]\) and \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\).  The sampling condition \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) is imposed on the sample and is not a member property of a one-unit law.

semantic_closure.name: Rounded-radius observation experiment
semantic_closure.construction: \(\mathcal E_{n,\Delta}(P)=\mathcal L_P(Z_{\Delta,1},\ldots,Z_{\Delta,n})\),\quad Z_{\Delta,i}=(Y_i,T_i,\Delta\lfloor R_i/\Delta\rfloor)\). The observation \(\sigma\)-field is exactly \(\sigma(Z_{\Delta,1},\ldots,Z_{\Delta,n})\); it excludes \(X_i\), angle, and raw \(R_i\).

semantic_closure.name: Total bin-aware local-constant estimator
semantic_closure.construction:
For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), let \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{T_i=t,Q_\Delta(R_i)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Define
\[
 \widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}=
 \begin{cases}
 \Pi_{[0,1]}\!\left(S_{t,n,\Delta}/N_{t,n,\Delta}\right),&N_{t,n,\Delta}>0,\\
 1/2,&N_{t,n,\Delta}=0,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 H_{n,\Delta}=\Delta\left\lceil n^{-1/4}/\Delta\right\rceil,
\]
where \(\Pi_{[0,1]}\) is Euclidean clipping, and set \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}=\widehat m_{1,n,\Delta}-\widehat m_{0,n,\Delta}\).

semantic_closure.name: Rounded-radius minimax risks
semantic_closure.construction: \(\mathfrak R^{(1)}_{n,\Delta}=\inf_{\widetilde\tau\in\mathcal T_{n,\Delta}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P|\widetilde\tau-\tau_P(b)|\) and \(\mathfrak R^{(2)}_{n,\Delta}=\inf_{\widetilde\tau\in\mathcal T_{n,\Delta}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau_P(b))^2]\).

semantic_closure.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  For every event \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) with \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\),
\[
 Y\mid B\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}\!\left(\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B]\right).
\]
In particular, put \(A_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Then \(A_t=\{T=t,R<H_{n,\Delta}\}\), its probability \(q_t\) is at least \(c_0H_{n,\Delta}^2>0\), and, with
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t],
\]
one has \(|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|\leq LH_{n,\Delta}\), \(N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\), and
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}\mid N_{t,n,\Delta}=k
 \sim\operatorname{Binomial}(k,\nu_t)
 \quad\text{for every }k\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\text{ with }\mathbb P_P(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k)>0.
\]
semantic_closure.justification: This lemma supplies the conditional-count likelihood and the explicit point-anchor bias uniformly over unknown bivariate designs.
semantic_closure.gap: Exact-radius and scalar-running-variable analyses do not state the conditional Bernoulli law after retaining only side and quantized radius under an unknown bivariate design.
semantic_closure.consumer: The count law is the implementation contract for the bin-aware estimator and the total confidence interval.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Let \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) satisfy \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\).  Consistency gives \(Y=Y(t)\) on \(B\).  The conditional Bernoulli member condition and iterated conditioning therefore imply
\[
 \mathbb P_P(Y=1\mid B)
 =\mathbb E_P\!\left[\mathbb P_P(Y(t)=1\mid X)\mid B\right]
 =\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
As \(Y\in\{0,1\}\), its conditional law is determined by this success probability, proving the first assertion.

Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:boundary\text{-}anchor\text{-}uniqueness}\) ensures that the declared \(\theta_t=\mu_t(b)\) is a well-defined functional of the law rather than a choice of regression version.

Put \(h=h_n\), \(H=H_{n,\Delta}\), and \(K=K_{n,\Delta}\).  Since \(H=K\Delta\), the floor quantizer satisfies, pointwise on \([0,1]\),
\[
 Q_\Delta(R)<H
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \lfloor R/\Delta\rfloor<K
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad R<K\Delta=H.
\]
Moreover, \(n\geq256\) and \(\Delta\leq\Delta_0\leq1/4\) give
\[
 0<h=n^{-1/4}\leq\frac14,
 \qquad h\leq H<h+\Delta\leq\frac12.
\]
Thus the two-sided local-mass member condition applies and yields
\[
 q_t:=\mathbb P_P(A_t)
 =\mathbb P_P(T=t,R<H)
 \geq c_0H^2>0.
\]
The first part of the proof with \(B=A_t\) shows that \(Y\mid A_t\) is Bernoulli with parameter
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t].
\]
The point-anchored envelope applies \(P_X\)-almost surely throughout \(A_t\).  Using \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\), conditional Jensen's inequality for absolute value, and \(R<H\) on \(A_t\), one obtains
\[
 |\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|
 =|\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)-\theta_t\mid A_t]|
 \leq\mathbb E_P[|\mu_t(X)-\theta_t|\mid A_t]
 \leq L\mathbb E_P[R\mid A_t]
 \leq LH.
\]

By independent identical sampling, the pairs
\[
 \left(\mathbf1\{A_{t,i}\},\mathbf1\{A_{t,i}\}Y_i\right),
 \qquad i=1,\ldots,n,
\]
are iid.  Hence \(N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\).  Their one-unit joint probability generating function, with \(w\) marking local membership and \(z\) marking a success, is
\[
 1-q_t+q_t(1-\nu_t)w+q_t\nu_twz.
\]
After taking the \(n\)-th power, the coefficient of \(w^k\) is proportional to \((1-\nu_t+\nu_tz)^k\).  Conditional on every count value \(k\) of positive probability, this is the probability generating function of \(\operatorname{Binomial}(k,\nu_t)\), proving the final assertion, including the degenerate case \(k=0\).

semantic_closure.statement:
For every \(n\ge256\) and \(0<\Delta\le\Delta_0\), the handle \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}\) admits one same-class baseline--alternative realization with both difficulties present.  Specifically, put \(\kappa=c_L/4\), \(b_h(r)=(h_n-r)_+\),
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf 1\{0\le r<\Delta\},
 \qquad
 g_{n,\Delta}(r)=\kappa\{b_h(r)+a_\Delta(r)\}.
\]
There are \(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta}\in\mathcal P_L\) with \(m_{0,0}=m_{0,1}=1/2\), \(m_{1,0}=1/2\), and \(m_{1,1}=1/2+g_{n,\Delta}\), for which
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\!\left(\mathcal L_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n),
 \mathcal L_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n)\right)
 \le\frac14<1-2\alpha
\]
and
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)
 =\kappa(h_n+\Delta).
\]
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\ge256\) and \(0<\Delta\le\Delta_0\), and let \(P_{0,n,\Delta}\) and \(P_{1,n,\Delta}\) be the baseline and alternative laws named by \(\mathrm{def:joint\text{-}lower\text{-}handle}\).  Write \(h=h_n=n^{-1/4}\) and \(\kappa=c_L/4\).  Since \(n\ge256\) and \(\Delta\le\Delta_0\le1/4\),
\[
 0<h\le\frac14,
 \qquad 0<\Delta\le\frac14.
\]
Under either law, \(X\) is uniform on the unit disc \(\mathcal D\), and the two assignment regions are half-discs.  Therefore polar integration gives, for \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(0<H\le1/2\),
\[
 \mathbb P(T=t,R<H)
 =\frac{(\pi H^2)/2}{\pi}
 =\frac{H^2}{2}
 \ge c_0H^2,
\]
where the last inequality uses \(c_0\le1/2\).  Thus the support and two-sided local-mass requirements in \(\mathrm{def:half\text{-}disc\text{-}class}\) hold.  The sharp-assignment, consistency, and conditional Bernoulli requirements hold by the construction and \(\mathrm{ass:sharp\text{-}boundary\text{-}assignment}\), \(\mathrm{ass:consistency}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:radial\text{-}bernoulli}\).

It remains to verify the range and point-anchor requirements.  On \([0,1]\),
\[
 |\phi(u)|=|(1-u)(1-2u)|\le1,
 \qquad
 \phi'(u)=-3+4u,
 \qquad
 |\phi'(u)|\le3.
\]
Because \(\phi(1)=0\), the function \(a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf1\{0\le r<\Delta\}\), extended by zero for \(r\ge\Delta\), is continuous and \(3\)-Lipschitz on \([0,\infty)\).  The function \(b_h(r)=(h-r)_+\) is \(1\)-Lipschitz.  Hence \(g_{n,\Delta}=\kappa(b_h+a_\Delta)\) is \(4\kappa=c_L\)-Lipschitz.  Since \(c_L\le L/8\le L\),
\[
 |g_{n,\Delta}(r)-g_{n,\Delta}(0)|\le Lr.
\]
Moreover, \(c_L\le1/16\), so \(\kappa\le1/64\), and
\[
 |g_{n,\Delta}(r)|
 \le\kappa(h+\Delta)
 \le\frac{1}{128}.
\]
Consequently the alternative treated mean lies in \([0,1]\), and its anchor is
\[
 \theta_{1,1}=\frac12+g_{n,\Delta}(0)
 =\frac12+\kappa(h+\Delta).
\]
The other three side-by-law means are constantly \(1/2\), so their anchors equal \(1/2\) and satisfy the envelope.  This proves
\[
 P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta}\in\mathcal P_L.
\]
By the definition of \(\tau_P(b)\), the common control anchor cancels and therefore
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)
 =g_{n,\Delta}(0)
 =\kappa(h_n+\Delta).
\]

We next bound the distance between the released laws.  Put \(W=(T,Q_\Delta(R))\).  Its law is the same under the two constructions.  Conditional on a positive-probability value of \(W\), \(Y\) is Bernoulli with its conditional average success probability by \(\mathrm{lem:conditional\text{-}local\text{-}binomial\text{-}law}\).  On a control value of \(W\), that probability is \(1/2\) under both laws.  On a treated value, write the alternative-minus-baseline conditional success probability as
\[
 \delta(W)=\kappa\,\mathbb E[b_h(R)+a_\Delta(R)\mid W].
\]
The alias component is zero outside the first bin.  In the first treated bin, uniform-disc polar density is proportional to \(r\), and \(\mathrm{lem:first\text{-}bin\text{-}alias}\) gives \(\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du=0\).  Thus
\[
 \int_0^\Delta r a_\Delta(r)\,dr
 =\Delta^3\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du
 =0.
\]
It follows that, on treated values of \(W\),
\[
 \delta(W)=\kappa\,\mathbb E[b_h(R)\mid W].
\]

Let \(Q_0\) and \(Q_1\) be the one-unit released laws under \(P_{0,n,\Delta}\) and \(P_{1,n,\Delta}\), respectively.  They have the same marginal law of \(W\), and under \(Q_0\), \(Y\mid W\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\).  Hence the likelihood ratio \(L_1=dQ_1/dQ_0\) equals \(1+2\delta(W)\) when \(Y=1\), equals \(1-2\delta(W)\) when \(Y=0\), and equals one on the control side.  Therefore, using conditional Jensen's inequality,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \chi^2(Q_1,Q_0)
 &=\mathbb E_{Q_0}[(L_1-1)^2]\\
 &=4\mathbb E[\mathbf1\{T=1\}\delta(W)^2]\\
 &\le4\kappa^2\mathbb E[\mathbf1\{T=1\}b_h(R)^2].
 \end{aligned}
\]
Uniform-disc polar integration on the treated half-disc now yields
\[
 \mathbb E[\mathbf1\{T=1\}b_h(R)^2]
 =\int_0^h r(h-r)^2\,dr
 =\frac{h^4}{12},
\]
and hence
\[
 \chi^2(Q_1,Q_0)\le\frac{\kappa^2h^4}{3}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\), the product likelihood ratio is \(L_n=\prod_{i=1}^nL_{1,i}\).  Independence gives the exact identity
\[
 1+\chi^2(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 =\mathbb E_{Q_0^{\otimes n}}[L_n^2]
 =\{\mathbb E_{Q_0}[L_1^2]\}^n
 =\{1+\chi^2(Q_1,Q_0)\}^n.
\]
Using \(1+x\le e^x\) and \(nh^4=1\),
\[
 \chi^2(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \le e^{\kappa^2/3}-1.
\]
The defining likelihood-ratio formula for total variation and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 =\frac12\mathbb E_{Q_0^{\otimes n}}|L_n-1|
 \le\frac12\sqrt{e^{\kappa^2/3}-1}.
\]
Since \(0\le\kappa^2/3\le1\), convexity of the exponential on \([0,1]\) implies \(e^x-1\le(e-1)x<2x\) there.  Consequently,
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \le\frac{\kappa}{\sqrt6}
 \le\frac{1}{64\sqrt6}
 <\frac14.
\]
Finally \(\alpha<1/4\) implies \(1-2\alpha>1/2>1/4\), proving the asserted uniform testing bound and completing the construction.

semantic_closure.gap: Existing ordinary-running-variable intervals do not handle latent annuli, quadratic local mass, or empty random side counts in this release field.
semantic_closure.consumer: The interval is directly implementable as a safe fallback in quantized \(\texttt{rd2d.dist}\) workflows.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), and write
\[
 h=h_n=n^{-1/4},\qquad H=H_{n,\Delta},\qquad B=LH.
\]
The aligned-bandwidth definition gives
\[
 h\leq H<h+\Delta\leq\frac12,
\]
because \(h\leq1/4\) and \(\Delta\leq\Delta_0\leq1/4\).

For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(\mathrm{lem:conditional\text{-}local\text{-}binomial\text{-}law}\) gives
\[
 q_t:=\mathbb P_P(T=t,R<H)\geq c_0H^2>0,
 \qquad
 \nu_t:=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid T=t,R<H],
\]
\[
 |\nu_t-\theta_t|=|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|\leq LH=B,
 \qquad
 N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t),
\]
and, for every count value \(k\) having positive probability,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}\mid\{N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\}
 \sim\operatorname{Binomial}(k,\nu_t).
\]
The equality between rounded and unrounded localization used here is exact because
\[
 \{Q_\Delta(R)<H\}
 =\{\Delta\lfloor R/\Delta\rfloor<K_{n,\Delta}\Delta\}
 =\{R<K_{n,\Delta}\Delta\}
 =\{R<H\}.
\]

If \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=0\), the side interval is \([0,1]\) and contains \(\nu_t\).  If the count is \(k>0\), the revalidated cited leaf \(\mathrm{lem:clopper\text{-}pearson\text{-}conditional\text{-}coverage}\), applied to the conditional binomial law, gives conditional coverage at least \(1-\alpha/2\).  Averaging over the count gives
\[
 \mathbb P_P\{\nu_t\in[\ell_t,u_t]\}\geq1-\alpha/2.
\]
By a union bound there is an event \(E\) of probability at least \(1-\alpha\) on which both side inclusions hold.  On \(E\),
\[
 \nu_1-\nu_0\in[\ell_1-u_0,u_1-\ell_0]
\]
and the two point-anchor bias inequalities imply
\[
 |\tau_P(b)-(\nu_1-\nu_0)|
 =|(\theta_1-\nu_1)-(\theta_0-\nu_0)|
 \leq2B.
\]
Thus \(\tau_P(b)\in C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}\) on \(E\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_L\).

The counts and successes are measurable functions of \(Z_\Delta^n\); the Clopper--Pearson endpoints are functions on a finite count-success state space; and the zero-count branch is explicit.  Since \(0\leq\ell_t\leq u_t\leq1\) and \(B<\infty\), the endpoints in \(\mathrm{def:total\text{-}honest\text{-}interval}\) form an ordered, closed, bounded, \(\sigma(Z_\Delta^n)\)-measurable interval on every sample.  This proves totality and honesty.

For expected length, put \(\beta=\alpha/4>0\).  Fix \(k\geq1\), \(s\in\{0,\ldots,k\}\), set \(\widehat p=s/k\), and write
\[
 I^{\mathrm{CP}}_{k,\alpha/2}(s)=[\ell,u].
\]
For a nontrivial upper endpoint, let \(d=u-\widehat p>0\) and \(W\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(k,u)\).  On \(\{W\leq s\}\), \(|W-ku|\geq kd\), so the upper endpoint equation in the cited leaf and the binomial variance identity yield
\[
 \beta=\mathbb P_u(W\leq s)
 \leq\frac{u(1-u)}{kd^2}
 \leq\frac{\widehat p+d}{kd^2}.
\]
Thus \(d^2\leq \widehat p/(k\beta)+d/(k\beta)\).  If nonnegative numbers satisfy \(d^2\leq A+Dd\), then either \(d\leq D\), or \((d-D)^2\leq d(d-D)\leq A\); in both cases \(d\leq\sqrt A+D\).  Therefore
\[
 u-\widehat p\leq\sqrt{\frac{\widehat p}{k\beta}}+\frac1{k\beta}.
\]
For a nontrivial lower endpoint, set \(d_-=\widehat p-\ell>0\) and take \(W\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(k,\ell)\).  On \(\{W\geq s\}\), \(|W-k\ell|\geq kd_-\).  The lower endpoint equation and \(\ell(1-\ell)\leq\ell\leq\widehat p\) give
\[
 \beta\leq\frac{\ell(1-\ell)}{kd_-^2}
 \leq\frac{\widehat p}{kd_-^2},
 \qquad
 \widehat p-\ell\leq\sqrt{\frac{\widehat p}{k\beta}}.
\]
The cited boundary conventions cover \(s=0\) and \(s=k\), so for every \(s\),
\[
 u-\ell\leq2\sqrt{\frac{\widehat p}{k\beta}}+\frac1{k\beta}.
\]
Conditionally on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k>0\), Jensen's inequality and \(0\leq S_{t,n,\Delta}/k\leq1\) imply
\[
 \mathbb E_P[u_t-\ell_t\mid N_{t,n,\Delta}=k]
 \leq\frac2{\sqrt{k\beta}}+\frac1{k\beta}.
\]

For \(N\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q)\), \(q>0\),
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac1{N+1}\right]
 =\int_0^1(1-q+qx)^n\,dx
 \leq\frac1{(n+1)q}.
\]
Using \(k^{-1}\leq2(k+1)^{-1}\), Cauchy--Schwarz, and \((1-q)^n\leq e^{-nq}\leq(nq)^{-1}\), one obtains
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{N>0\}}N\right]\leq\frac2{nq},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{N>0\}}{\sqrt N}\right]\leq\sqrt{\frac2{nq}},
 \qquad
 \mathbb P(N=0)\leq\frac1{nq}.
\]
The zero-count side interval has length one.  Consequently
\[
 \mathbb E_P[u_t-\ell_t]
 \leq\frac{2\sqrt2}{\sqrt{\beta nq_t}}
 +\left(1+\frac2\beta\right)\frac1{nq_t}
 \leq\frac{2\sqrt2}{\sqrt{\beta c_0nH^2}}
 +\left(1+\frac2\beta\right)\frac1{c_0nH^2}.
\]

The constructed interval has exact length
\[
 \operatorname{length}(C_{n,\Delta,\alpha})
 =(u_1-\ell_1)+(u_0-\ell_0)+4LH.
\]
Finally,
\[
 H<h+\Delta\leq2\rho_{n,\Delta},
 \qquad
 \frac1{\sqrt nH}\leq h\leq\rho_{n,\Delta},
 \qquad
 \frac1{nH^2}\leq h^2\leq\rho_{n,\Delta}.
\]
Summing the two side bounds gives, with \(\beta=\alpha/4\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_{n,\Delta,\alpha})]
 \leq
 \left\{
 \frac{4\sqrt2}{\sqrt{\beta c_0}}
 +\frac{2(1+2/\beta)}{c_0}+8L
 \right\}\rho_{n,\Delta}.
\]
This finite constant has the permitted dependence on \(L,c_0,\alpha,\Delta_0\) and is uniform in every allowed \(n\) and \(\Delta\).

semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  Suppose \(a,a'\in[0,1]\) each satisfies the displayed point-anchor envelope.  For any \(H\in(0,1/2]\), the local-mass member condition gives
\[
 \mathbb P_P(T=t,R<H)\geq c_0H^2>0.
\]
Each candidate envelope holds outside a \(P_X\)-null subset of the side-\(t\), radius-at-most-\(1/2\) region.  Removing the union of those two null sets from \(\{T=t,R<H\}\) leaves a nonempty set.  At any \(x\) in that set,
\[
 |a-a'|
 \leq|a-\mu_t(x)|+|\mu_t(x)-a'|
 \leq2L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
 <2LH.
\]
This holds for every \(H\in(0,1/2]\).  Taking \(H\downarrow0\) gives \(|a-a'|=0\), hence \(a=a'\).  Existence of the declared anchor is part of the class construction, so it is unique for each side.  Therefore \(\theta_t\), and hence \(\tau_P(b)=\theta_1-\theta_0\), is a well-defined functional of \(P\).

semantic_closure.name: Embedded uniform-half-disc joint lower handle
semantic_closure.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}=(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta})\) denote the following pair.  Under both laws, \(X\) is uniform on \(\mathcal D\), \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assignment is sharp, and the control mean is \(1/2\).  Under \(P_{0,n,\Delta}\) the treated mean is \(1/2\); under \(P_{1,n,\Delta}\) it is
\[
 \frac12+\frac{c_L}{4}\left\{(h_n-\lVert x-b\rVert_2)_+
 +\Delta\phi\!\left(\frac{\lVert x-b\rVert_2}{\Delta}\right)
 \mathbf1\{\lVert x-b\rVert_2<\Delta\}\right\}.
\]
Given \(X\), the potential outcomes are conditionally independent Bernoulli variables with these means, and \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\).

semantic_closure.statement: For every \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), \(\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du=0\), both \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}\) and \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}\) belong to \(\mathcal P_L\), their released one-unit laws of \(Z_\Delta\) are identical, and \(\tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}}(b)=2c_L\Delta\).
semantic_closure.justification: This certifies an exact order-\(\Delta\) alias in a legal uniform-half-disc subclass of the unknown-design point-anchored model, without asserting design-wide orthogonality.
semantic_closure.gap: Scalar rounding results do not furnish the radial-Jacobian null direction for a release that hides bivariate coordinates within annuli.
semantic_closure.consumer: Data stewards using released radial bins can see that no sample size removes the first-bin resolution floor.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
The polynomial specified in \(\mathrm{def:first\text{-}bin\text{-}alias}\) is
\[
 \phi(u)=1-3u+2u^2,
 \qquad
 \int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du
 =\int_0^1(u-3u^2+2u^3)\,du
 =\frac12-1+\frac12=0.
\]
Furthermore, \(\phi(1)=0\), \(|\phi(u)|\leq1\) for \(u\in[0,1]\), and \(\phi'(u)=-3+4u\), whence \(\sup_{u\in[0,1]}|\phi'(u)|=3\).  Define
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf1\{0\leq r<\Delta\}.
\]
Because the two pieces agree at \(r=\Delta\), the preceding derivative bound shows that \(a_\Delta\) is continuous and \(3\)-Lipschitz on \([0,1]\).  The radius map is \(1\)-Lipschitz, since
\[
 \bigl|\lVert x-b\rVert_2-\lVert x'-b\rVert_2\bigr|
 \leq\lVert x-x'\rVert_2.
\]

Consider either law in \(\mathrm{def:first\text{-}bin\text{-}alias}\).  Choose the control anchor \(\theta_0=1/2\) and the treated anchor
\[
 \theta_{1,\pm}=\frac12\pm c_L\Delta
 =\frac12\pm c_La_\Delta(0).
\]
For every treated point \(x\) with radius \(r\leq1/2\), the point-anchor deviation is
\[
 |\mu_{1,\pm}(x)-\theta_{1,\pm}|
 =c_L|a_\Delta(r)-a_\Delta(0)|
 \leq3c_Lr\leq Lr,
\]
where the last inequality follows from \(c_L\leq L/8\).  The corresponding control deviation is zero.  Also
\[
 |c_La_\Delta(r)|\leq c_L\Delta
 \leq\frac1{16}\frac14=\frac1{64},
\]
using \(c_L\leq1/16\) and \(\Delta\leq\Delta_0\leq1/4\); hence all constructed Bernoulli means lie in \([0,1]\).  Thus the Bernoulli and point-anchor member conditions hold.

The construction supplies the known half-plane partition, sharp assignment, consistency, and conditionally Bernoulli potential outcomes.  Uniformity of \(X\) on the unit disc and polar integration give, for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(0<H\leq1/2\),
\[
 \mathbb P(T=t,R<H)
 =\frac1\pi\int_{\Theta_t}\int_0^H r\,dr\,d\vartheta
 =\frac{H^2}{2}
 \geq c_0H^2,
 \qquad |\Theta_t|=\pi,
\]
by \(c_0\leq1/2\).  Consequently both constructed laws are members of the unknown-design point-anchored class \(\mathcal P_L\).  This verifies membership through an embedded uniform-half-disc subclass only; it does not assert the alias identity for an arbitrary design in \(\mathcal P_L\).

The distribution of \((T,Q_\Delta(R))\) is common to the two signs.  Within the treated first bin, the difference of their joint success masses is
\[
 \frac1\pi\int_{\Theta_1}\int_0^\Delta
 2c_L\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)r\,dr\,d\vartheta
 =2c_L\Delta^3\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du=0.
\]
Outside this bin the perturbation vanishes, and every control cell is unchanged.  Since \(Y\) is binary, equality of each released cell's total mass and success mass also gives equality of its failure mass.  Hence the entire one-unit laws of \(Z_\Delta=(Y,T,Q_\Delta(R))\) coincide.  Finally, by \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\) and \(\phi(0)=1\),
\[
 \tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}}(b)=c_L\Delta,
 \qquad
 \tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}}(b)=-c_L\Delta,
\]
so their difference is \(2c_L\Delta\), as claimed.

semantic_closure.construction:
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), set \([\ell_t,u_t]=[0,1]\) when \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=0\), and set \([\ell_t,u_t]=I^{\mathrm{CP}}_{N_{t,n,\Delta},\alpha/2}(S_{t,n,\Delta})\) when \(N_{t,n,\Delta}>0\).  With \(B_{n,\Delta}=LH_{n,\Delta}\), define the closed bounded interval
\[

 =\bigl[\ell_1-u_0-2B_{n,\Delta},\ u_1-\ell_0+2B_{n,\Delta}\bigr].
\]

semantic_closure.statement: For every integer \(k\geq1\), if \(S\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(k,p)\), then the equal-tailed Clopper--Pearson interval \(I^{\mathrm{CP}}_{k,\alpha/2}(S)\) covers \(p\) with probability at least \(1-\alpha/2\). semantic_closure.construction:
For each sign, construct \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{\pm,\Delta}\) by drawing \(X\) uniformly on \(\mathcal D\), taking \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assigning \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\), and drawing conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes given \(X\) with
\[
 \mu_{0,\pm}(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mu_{1,\pm}(x)=\frac12\pm c_L\Delta\phi\!\left(\frac{\lVert x-b\rVert_2}{\Delta}\right)
 \mathbf1\{\lVert x-b\rVert_2<\Delta\}.
\]
Finally set \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\), where \(\phi(u)=(1-u)(1-2u)\) and \(c_L=\min\{L/8,1/16\}\).

payload.statement:
Let \(k\geq1\), and let \(W_1,\ldots,W_k\) be independent random variables satisfying \(0\leq W_j\leq1\) almost surely and \(\mathbb E[W_j]=p\) for every \(j\).  Then, for every \(r>0\),
\[
 \mathbb P\!\left(\frac1k\sum_{j=1}^kW_j-p\geq r\right)\leq\exp(-2kr^2).
\]

attestation.note: The original published scan was checked: Theorem 1, equation (2.3), p. 15 gives the direct \([0,1]\)-bounded one-sided average bound used here; it is distinct from Theorem 2, equation (2.6), p. 16.

payload.justification: This classical one-sided inequality supplies finite-sample concentration for a selected average of independent bounded outcomes.
payload.gap: The cited result is only the fixed-count concentration leaf; conditioning on a random spatial count and adding point-anchor bias are proved in this note.
payload.consumer: The total conditional-Hoeffding interval invokes the bound on each side and on complemented outcomes.

carrier.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  Suppose \(a,a'\in[0,1]\) both satisfy the point-anchor envelope in the statement.  For every \(H\in(0,1/2]\), the local-mass condition in \(\mathrm{def:half\text{-}disc\text{-}class}\) gives
\[
 \mathbb P_P(T=t,R<H)\geq c_0H^2>0.
\]
Each candidate envelope holds outside a \(P_X\)-null subset of the side-\(t\), radius-at-most-\(1/2\) region.  Removing the union of these two null sets from \(\{T=t,R<H\}\) leaves a set of positive probability.  At every \(x\) in that remaining set,
\[
 |a-a'|
 \leq |a-\mu_t(x)|+|\mu_t(x)-a'|
 \leq 2L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
 <2LH.
\]
This inequality holds for every \(H\in(0,1/2]\).  Letting \(H\downarrow0\) yields \(|a-a'|=0\), so \(a=a'\).

Existence of the declared anchor \(\theta_t\) is part of \(\mathrm{def:half\text{-}disc\text{-}class}\).  Moreover, any two versions of the conditional mean \(x\mapsto\mathbb E_P[Y(t)\mid X=x]\) agree \(P_X\)-almost everywhere by the definition of a conditional expectation.  Intersecting that full-measure equality set with the two full-measure envelope sets and repeating the preceding argument shows that the anchor is invariant to the chosen version.  Hence \(\theta_t\), and therefore \(\tau_P(b)=\theta_1-\theta_0\), is a well-defined functional of \(P\).

target_declaration.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_L\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), there is at most one \(a\in[0,1]\) such that \(|\mu_t(x)-a|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) with \(\lVert x-b\rVert_2\leq1/2\). Consequently, the declared \(\theta_t\) and \(\tau_P(b)=\theta_1-\theta_0\) are well-defined functionals of \(P\).
target_declaration.justification: The point anchor must be a functional of the law, not an arbitrary version choice, for the boundary contrast to be a well-defined causal estimand.
target_declaration.gap: The uniqueness step is specific to combining an almost-everywhere point envelope with positive side mass at every shrinking radius.
target_declaration.consumer: All risk and coverage statements use the uniquely determined boundary anchor contrast.

semantic_closure.name: Unknown-design bivariate bounded-outcome point-anchored boundary class
semantic_closure.construction:
\(\mathcal P_L\) is the set of one-unit laws \(P\) such that \(P_X(\mathcal D)=1\); for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(H\in(0,1/2]\), \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\); \((\mathcal X_{0,P},\mathcal X_{1,P})\) is a known Borel partition of \(\mathcal D\) and \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\) almost surely; \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\) almost surely; for each \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the conditional law of \(Y(t)\) given \(X=x\) is supported on \([0,1]\) and has mean \(\mu_t(x)\); and the point-anchored envelope
\[
 |\mu_t(x)-\theta_t|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
\]
holds for every \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every side-\(t\) point \(x\) of radius at most \(1/2\), where \(\theta_t\in[0,1]\) and \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\).  The sampling condition \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) is imposed on the sample and is not a member property of a one-unit law.

semantic_closure.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  For every event \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) with \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\), the conditional outcome is supported on \([0,1]\) and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid B]=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
In particular, put \(A_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Then \(A_t=\{T=t,R<H_{n,\Delta}\}\), its probability \(q_t\) is at least \(c_0H_{n,\Delta}^2>0\), and, with
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t],
\]
one has \(|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|\leq LH_{n,\Delta}\) and \(N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\).  Conditional on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\geq1\), list the selected outcomes in increasing sample-index order as \(Y_{t,1}^{\star},\ldots,Y_{t,k}^{\star}\).  They are independent and identically distributed, supported on \([0,1]\), and have common mean \(\nu_t\); moreover,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{j=1}^kY_{t,j}^{\star},\qquad
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right]=\nu_t,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right)\leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
Outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass, the conditional sum need not be binomial.
semantic_closure.justification: This lemma supplies the conditional selected-sample law, random-count likelihood, bounded variance, and explicit point-anchor bias under the unknown bivariate design.
semantic_closure.gap: Exact-radius and scalar-running-variable analyses do not state the conditional iid selected-outcome law after retaining only side and quantized radius under an unknown bivariate design.
semantic_closure.consumer: The count and selected-average laws are the implementation contract for the bin-aware estimator and total conditional-Hoeffding interval.

semantic_closure.statement:
For every \(n\ge256\) and \(0<\Delta\le\Delta_0\), the handle \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}\) admits one same-class baseline--alternative realization with both difficulties present.  Specifically, put \(\kappa=c_L/4\), \(b_h(r)=(h_n-r)_+\),
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf 1\{0\le r<\Delta\},
 \qquad
 g_{n,\Delta}(r)=\kappa\{b_h(r)+a_\Delta(r)\}.
\]
There are \(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta}\in\mathcal P_L\) with \(m_{0,0}=m_{0,1}=1/2\), \(m_{1,0}=1/2\), and \(m_{1,1}=1/2+g_{n,\Delta}\), for which
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\!\left(\mathcal L_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n),
 \mathcal L_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n)\right)
 \le\frac14<1-2\alpha
\]
and
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)
 =\kappa(h_n+\Delta).
\]
semantic_closure.justification: One legal uniform-half-disc pair combines the sampling bump and exact first-bin alias while charging released divergence only for the sampling component.
semantic_closure.gap: No cited comparator supplies a single pair for the latent annular experiment with both order-\(n^{-1/4}\) and order-\(\Delta\) displacement.
semantic_closure.consumer: The pair is the common lower certificate for absolute risk, squared risk, and honest expected interval length over the point-anchored superclass.

semantic_closure.construction:

semantic_closure.name: Total bin-aware local-constant estimator
semantic_closure.construction:
For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), let \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{T_i=t,Q_\Delta(R_i)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Define
\[
 \widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}=
 \begin{cases}
 \Pi_{[0,1]}\!\left(S_{t,n,\Delta}/N_{t,n,\Delta}\right),&N_{t,n,\Delta}>0,\\
 1/2,&N_{t,n,\Delta}=0,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 H_{n,\Delta}=\Delta\left\lceil n^{-1/4}/\Delta\right\rceil,
\]
where \(\Pi_{[0,1]}\) is Euclidean clipping, and set \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}=\widehat m_{1,n,\Delta}-\widehat m_{0,n,\Delta}\).

semantic_closure.name: Bias-enlarged conditional-Hoeffding interval
semantic_closure.construction:
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), set \([\ell_t,u_t]=[0,1]\) when \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=0\).  When \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k>0\), put
\[
 \overline Y_t=\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k,
 \qquad
 r_{k,\alpha}=\sqrt{\frac{\log(4/\alpha)}{2k}},
 \qquad
 [\ell_t,u_t]=\bigl[\max\{0,\overline Y_t-r_{k,\alpha}\},\min\{1,\overline Y_t+r_{k,\alpha}\}\bigr].
\]
With \(B_{n,\Delta}=LH_{n,\Delta}\), define the closed bounded interval
\[
 C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}
 =\bigl[\ell_1-u_0-2B_{n,\Delta},\ u_1-\ell_0+2B_{n,\Delta}\bigr].
\]
