carrier.proof_tex:
Let \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) satisfy \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:sharp\text{-}boundary\text{-}assignment}\), \(T\) is a measurable function of \(X\), and the definitions of \(R\) and \(Q_\Delta\) make \(Q_\Delta(R)\) a measurable function of \(X\).  Thus \(B\in\sigma(X)\), up to completion by a \(P\)-null event.  By \(\mathrm{ass:consistency}\), \(Y=Y(t)\) on \(B\).  The bounded-outcome conditional-mean condition \(\mathrm{ass:radial\text{-}bernoulli}\) and iterated conditioning therefore give
\[
 0\leq Y\leq1\quad\text{on }B,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid B]
 =\mathbb E_P[Y(t)\mid B]
 =\mathbb E_P\!\left[\mathbb E_P[Y(t)\mid X]\,\middle|\,B\right]
 =\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
This proves the first assertion without requiring a mixture of bounded outcome laws to be Bernoulli.

Put \(h=h_n\), \(H=H_{n,\Delta}\), and \(K=K_{n,\Delta}\).  The definitions give \(H=K\Delta\), where \(K\geq1\) is an integer.  Hence, pointwise for \(R\in[0,1]\),
\[
 Q_\Delta(R)<H
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \Delta\lfloor R/\Delta\rfloor<K\Delta
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 R<K\Delta=H.
\]
Since \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\leq1/4\), and \(\lceil x\rceil<x+1\),
\[
 0<h=n^{-1/4}\leq\frac14,
 \qquad
 h\leq H=\Delta\left\lceil\frac h\Delta\right\rceil<h+\Delta\leq\frac12.
\]
Thus the local-mass condition applies to \(A_t=\{T=t,R<H\}\), and
\[
 q_t:=\mathbb P_P(A_t)\geq c_0H^2>0.
\]
Using the first part with \(B=A_t\), define
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A_t]
      =\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t].
\]
On \(A_t\), \(R<H\leq1/2\).  The point-anchor envelope \(\mathrm{ass:radial\text{-}lipschitz}\), the equality \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\), and conditional Jensen's inequality yield
\[
 |\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|
 =\left|\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)-\theta_t\mid A_t]\right|
 \leq\mathbb E_P[|\mu_t(X)-\theta_t|\mid A_t]
 \leq L\mathbb E_P[R\mid A_t]
 \leq LH.
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:boundary\text{-}anchor\text{-}uniqueness}\) ensures that the anchor appearing here is a well-defined functional of \(P\).

For unit \(i\), let \(I_i=\mathbf1\{A_{t,i}\}\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) makes the pairs \((I_i,Y_i)\) independent and identically distributed, with \(\mathbb P_P(I_i=1)=q_t\).  Therefore
\[
 N_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{i=1}^n I_i\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t).
\]
Fix \(k\geq1\) with \(\mathbb P_P(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k)>0\).  Conditional on any indicator configuration \((I_1,\ldots,I_n)\) having exactly \(k\) ones, independence across units makes the outcomes at the selected indices independent, and identical sampling gives each selected outcome the common conditional law \(\mathcal L_P(Y\mid A_t)\).  This product law is the same for every such indicator configuration.  Mixing over the configurations conditional on their sum therefore leaves that product law unchanged.  Consequently \(Y_{t,1}^{\star},\ldots,Y_{t,k}^{\star}\) are conditionally independent and identically distributed, are supported on \([0,1]\), and have common mean \(\nu_t\).  By the definition of the localized sum,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{j=1}^kY_{t,j}^{\star}
 \quad\text{on }\{N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right]=\nu_t.
\]
If \(0\leq W\leq1\) and \(\mathbb E[W]=\nu\), then \(W^2\leq W\), whence
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(W)=\mathbb E[W^2]-\nu^2
 \leq\nu-\nu^2\leq\frac14.
\]
Conditional independence now implies
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\frac1k\sum_{j=1}^kY_{t,j}^{\star}\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right)
 =\frac1{k^2}\sum_{j=1}^k\operatorname{Var}_P(Y_{t,j}^{\star}\mid N_{t,n,\Delta}=k)
 \leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
All claims follow.  In particular, no binomial law is asserted for the sum outside the explicitly Bernoulli lower-bound subclass.

target_declaration.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  For every event \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) with \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\), the conditional outcome is supported on \([0,1]\) and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid B]=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
In particular, put \(A_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Then \(A_t=\{T=t,R<H_{n,\Delta}\}\), its probability \(q_t\) is at least \(c_0H_{n,\Delta}^2>0\), and, with
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t],
\]
one has \(|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|\leq LH_{n,\Delta}\) and \(N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\).  Conditional on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\geq1\), list the selected outcomes in increasing sample-index order as \(Y_{t,1}^{\star},\ldots,Y_{t,k}^{\star}\).  They are independent and identically distributed, supported on \([0,1]\), and have common mean \(\nu_t\); moreover,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{j=1}^kY_{t,j}^{\star},\qquad
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right]=\nu_t,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right)\leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
Outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass, the conditional sum need not be binomial.

semantic_closure.name: Unknown-design bivariate bounded-outcome point-anchored boundary class
semantic_closure.construction:
\(\mathcal P_L\) is the set of one-unit laws \(P\) such that \(P_X(\mathcal D)=1\); for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(H\in(0,1/2]\), \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\); \((\mathcal X_{0,P},\mathcal X_{1,P})\) is a known Borel partition of \(\mathcal D\) and \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\) almost surely; \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\) almost surely; for each \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the conditional law of \(Y(t)\) given \(X=x\) is supported on \([0,1]\) and has mean \(\mu_t(x)\); and the point-anchored envelope
\[
 |\mu_t(x)-\theta_t|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
\]
holds for every \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every side-\(t\) point \(x\) of radius at most \(1/2\), where \(\theta_t\in[0,1]\) and \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\).  The sampling condition \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) is imposed on the sample and is not a member property of a one-unit law.

semantic_closure.construction:
For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), let \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{T_i=t,Q_\Delta(R_i)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Define
\[
 \widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}=
 \begin{cases}
 \Pi_{[0,1]}\!\left(S_{t,n,\Delta}/N_{t,n,\Delta}\right),&N_{t,n,\Delta}>0,\\
 1/2,&N_{t,n,\Delta}=0,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 H_{n,\Delta}=\Delta\left\lceil n^{-1/4}/\Delta\right\rceil,
\]
where \(\Pi_{[0,1]}\) is Euclidean clipping, and set \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}=\widehat m_{1,n,\Delta}-\widehat m_{0,n,\Delta}\).

semantic_closure.name: Bias-enlarged conditional-Hoeffding interval
semantic_closure.construction:
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), set \([\ell_t,u_t]=[0,1]\) when \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=0\).  When \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k>0\), put
\[
 \overline Y_t=\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k,
 \qquad
 r_{k,\alpha}=\sqrt{\frac{\log(4/\alpha)}{2k}},
 \qquad
 [\ell_t,u_t]=\bigl[\max\{0,\overline Y_t-r_{k,\alpha}\},\min\{1,\overline Y_t+r_{k,\alpha}\}\bigr].
\]
With \(B_{n,\Delta}=LH_{n,\Delta}\), define the closed bounded interval
\[
 C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}
 =\bigl[\ell_1-u_0-2B_{n,\Delta},\ u_1-\ell_0+2B_{n,\Delta}\bigr].
\]

semantic_closure.statement:
Let \(k\geq1\), and let \(W_1,\ldots,W_k\) be independent random variables satisfying \(0\leq W_j\leq1\) almost surely and \(\mathbb E[W_j]=p\) for every \(j\).  Then, for every \(r>0\),
\[
 \mathbb P\!\left(\frac1k\sum_{j=1}^kW_j-p\geq r\right)\leq\exp(-2kr^2).
\]

carrier.proof_tex:
The polynomial in \(\mathrm{def:first\text{-}bin\text{-}alias}\) is
\[
 \phi(u)=1-3u+2u^2,
 \qquad
 \int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du
 =\int_0^1(u-3u^2+2u^3)\,du
 =\frac12-1+\frac12=0.
\]
Also \(\phi(1)=0\), \(|\phi(u)|\leq1\) on \([0,1]\), and \(\phi'(u)=-3+4u\), so \(\sup_{u\in[0,1]}|\phi'(u)|=3\).  Define
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf1\{0\leq r<\Delta\}.
\]
The two pieces meet at \(r=\Delta\) because \(\phi(1)=0\); hence the derivative bound shows that \(a_\Delta\) is continuous and \(3\)-Lipschitz on \([0,1]\).  The reverse triangle inequality gives
\[
 \bigl|\lVert x-b\rVert_2-\lVert x'-b\rVert_2\bigr|
 \leq\lVert x-x'\rVert_2.
\]

Consider either sign in \(\mathrm{def:first\text{-}bin\text{-}alias}\).  Choose \(\theta_0=1/2\) and
\[
 \theta_{1,\pm}=\frac12\pm c_L\Delta
 =\frac12\pm c_La_\Delta(0).
\]
For every treated point \(x\) of radius \(r\leq1/2\),
\[
 |\mu_{1,\pm}(x)-\theta_{1,\pm}|
 =c_L|a_\Delta(r)-a_\Delta(0)|
 \leq3c_Lr
 \leq Lr,
\]
where \(3c_L\leq3L/8\leq L\).  The control deviation is zero.  Furthermore,
\[
 |c_La_\Delta(r)|\leq c_L\Delta
 \leq\frac1{16}\frac14=\frac1{64},
\]
so the constructed Bernoulli means lie in \([31/64,33/64]\subset[0,1]\).  Thus the bounded-outcome conditional-mean and point-anchor conditions hold.

The construction supplies the known half-plane partition, sharp assignment, consistency, and conditionally Bernoulli potential outcomes.  Uniformity of \(X\) on the unit disc and polar integration give, for \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(0<H\leq1/2\),
\[
 \mathbb P(T=t,R<H)
 =\frac1\pi\int_{\Theta_t}\int_0^H r\,dr\,d\vartheta
 =\frac{H^2}{2}
 \geq c_0H^2,
 \qquad |\Theta_t|=\pi,
\]
because \(c_0\leq1/2\).  Hence both constructed laws belong to \(\mathcal P_L\).  This is membership through an embedded uniform-half-disc subclass, not a claim of design-wide orthogonality.

The distribution of \((T,Q_\Delta(R))\) is common to the two signs.  In the treated first bin, the difference of their joint success masses is
\[
 \frac1\pi\int_{\Theta_1}\int_0^\Delta
 2c_L\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)r\,dr\,d\vartheta
 =2c_L\Delta^3\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du=0.
\]
Outside that bin the perturbation vanishes, and all control cells are unchanged.  Because \(Y\) is binary in these two constructed laws, equality of a released cell's total mass and success mass also gives equality of its failure mass.  Therefore the complete one-unit laws of \(Z_\Delta=(Y,T,Q_\Delta(R))\) coincide.  Finally, \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\) and \(\phi(0)=1\) give
\[
 \tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}}(b)=c_L\Delta,
 \qquad
 \tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}}(b)=-c_L\Delta,
\]
whose difference is \(2c_L\Delta\).

target_declaration.statement: For every \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), \(\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du=0\), both \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}\) and \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}\) belong to \(\mathcal P_L\), their released one-unit laws of \(Z_\Delta\) are identical, and \(\tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}}(b)=2c_L\Delta\).
target_declaration.justification: This certifies an exact order-\(\Delta\) alias in a legal uniform-half-disc subclass of the unknown-design point-anchored model, without asserting design-wide orthogonality.
target_declaration.gap: Scalar rounding results do not furnish the radial-Jacobian null direction for a release that hides bivariate coordinates within annuli.
target_declaration.consumer: Data stewards using released radial bins can see that no sample size removes the first-bin resolution floor.

semantic_closure.condition:
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\),
\[
 \mathcal L_P(Y(t)\mid X=x)
 \in\left\{F:F([0,1])=1\ \text{ and }\ \int_{[0,1]}y\,dF(y)=\mu_t(x)\right\}.
\]

For every \(t\in\{0,1\}\), for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) satisfying \(\lVert x-b\rVert_2\leq1/2\),
\[

\]
\(Y=T Y(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\) almost surely under \(P\).

semantic_closure.name: Unknown-design bivariate bounded-outcome point-anchored boundary class
semantic_closure.construction:
\(\mathcal P_L\) is the set of one-unit laws \(P\) such that \(P_X(\mathcal D)=1\); for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(H\in(0,1/2]\), \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\); \((\mathcal X_{0,P},\mathcal X_{1,P})\) is a known Borel partition of \(\mathcal D\) and \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\) almost surely; \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\) almost surely; for each \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the conditional law of \(Y(t)\) given \(X=x\) is supported on \([0,1]\) and has mean \(\mu_t(x)\); and the point-anchored envelope
\[
 |\mu_t(x)-\theta_t|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
\]
holds for every \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every side-\(t\) point \(x\) of radius at most \(1/2\), where \(\theta_t\in[0,1]\) and \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\).  The sampling condition \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) is imposed on the sample and is not a member property of a one-unit law.

semantic_closure.name: Rounded-radius observation experiment
semantic_closure.construction: \(\mathcal E_{n,\Delta}(P)=\mathcal L_P(Z_{\Delta,1},\ldots,Z_{\Delta,n})\),\quad Z_{\Delta,i}=(Y_i,T_i,\Delta\lfloor R_i/\Delta\rfloor)\). The observation \(\sigma\)-field is exactly \(\sigma(Z_{\Delta,1},\ldots,Z_{\Delta,n})\); it excludes \(X_i\), angle, and raw \(R_i\).

semantic_closure.name: Embedded uniform-half-disc exact first-bin alias pair
semantic_closure.construction:
For each sign, construct \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{\pm,\Delta}\) by drawing \(X\) uniformly on \(\mathcal D\), taking \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assigning \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\), and drawing conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes given \(X\) with
\[
 \mu_{0,\pm}(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mu_{1,\pm}(x)=\frac12\pm c_L\Delta\phi\!\left(\frac{\lVert x-b\rVert_2}{\Delta}\right)
 \mathbf1\{\lVert x-b\rVert_2<\Delta\}.
\]
Finally set \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\), where \(\phi(u)=(1-u)(1-2u)\) and \(c_L=\min\{L/8,1/16\}\).

semantic_closure.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  For every event \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) with \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\), the conditional outcome is supported on \([0,1]\) and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid B]=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
In particular, put \(A_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Then \(A_t=\{T=t,R<H_{n,\Delta}\}\), its probability \(q_t\) is at least \(c_0H_{n,\Delta}^2>0\), and, with
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t],
\]
one has \(|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|\leq LH_{n,\Delta}\) and \(N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\).  Conditional on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\geq1\), list the selected outcomes in increasing sample-index order as \(Y_{t,1}^{\star},\ldots,Y_{t,k}^{\star}\).  They are independent and identically distributed, supported on \([0,1]\), and have common mean \(\nu_t\); moreover,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{j=1}^kY_{t,j}^{\star},\qquad
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right]=\nu_t,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right)\leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
Outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass, the conditional sum need not be binomial.
semantic_closure.justification: This lemma supplies the conditional selected-sample law, random-count likelihood, bounded variance, and explicit point-anchor bias under the unknown bivariate design.
semantic_closure.gap: Exact-radius and scalar-running-variable analyses do not state the conditional iid selected-outcome law after retaining only side and quantized radius under an unknown bivariate design.
semantic_closure.consumer: The count and selected-average laws are the implementation contract for the bin-aware estimator and total conditional-Hoeffding interval.

semantic_closure.statement:
For every \(n\ge256\) and \(0<\Delta\le\Delta_0\), the handle \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}\) admits one same-class baseline--alternative realization with both difficulties present.  Specifically, put \(\kappa=c_L/4\), \(b_h(r)=(h_n-r)_+\),
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf 1\{0\le r<\Delta\},
 \qquad
 g_{n,\Delta}(r)=\kappa\{b_h(r)+a_\Delta(r)\}.
\]
There are \(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta}\in\mathcal P_L\) with \(m_{0,0}=m_{0,1}=1/2\), \(m_{1,0}=1/2\), and \(m_{1,1}=1/2+g_{n,\Delta}\), for which
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\!\left(\mathcal L_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n),
 \mathcal L_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n)\right)
 \le\frac14<1-2\alpha
\]
and
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)
 =\kappa(h_n+\Delta).
\]
semantic_closure.justification: One legal uniform-half-disc pair combines the sampling bump and exact first-bin alias while charging released divergence only for the sampling component.
semantic_closure.gap: No cited comparator supplies a single pair for the latent annular experiment with both order-\(n^{-1/4}\) and order-\(\Delta\) displacement.
semantic_closure.consumer: The pair is the common lower certificate for absolute risk, squared risk, and honest expected interval length over the point-anchored superclass.

semantic_closure.name: Total bin-aware local-constant estimator
semantic_closure.construction:
For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), let \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{T_i=t,Q_\Delta(R_i)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Define
\[

 1/2,&N_{t,n,\Delta}=0,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 H_{n,\Delta}=\Delta\left\lceil n^{-1/4}/\Delta\right\rceil,
\]
where \(\Pi_{[0,1]}\) is Euclidean clipping, and set \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}=\widehat m_{1,n,\Delta}-\widehat m_{0,n,\Delta}\).

carrier.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\geq256\) and \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and abbreviate \(h=h_n\) and \(\kappa=c_L/4\).  Then \(h\leq1/4\) and \(\Delta\leq1/4\).  Since \(\phi(1)=0\) and \(\phi'(u)=-3+4u\), the function
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf1\{0\leq r<\Delta\}
\]
is continuous and \(3\)-Lipschitz on \([0,1]\), and it satisfies \(a_\Delta(0)=\Delta\).  The moment identity in \(\mathrm{lem:first\text{-}bin\text{-}alias}\) gives
\[
 \int_0^\Delta ra_\Delta(r)\,dr
 =\Delta^3\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du=0.
\]
The function \(b_h(r)=(h-r)_+\) is \(1\)-Lipschitz and satisfies \(b_h(0)=h\).  Thus
\[
 g_{n,\Delta}(r)=\kappa\{b_h(r)+a_\Delta(r)\}
\]
is \(4\kappa=c_L\leq L\)-Lipschitz, and
\[
 |g_{n,\Delta}(r)|
 \leq\kappa(h+\Delta)
 \leq\frac{c_L}{8}
 \leq\frac1{128}<\frac12.
\]

Take the laws in \(\mathrm{def:joint\text{-}lower\text{-}handle}\).  Under \(P_{0,n,\Delta}\), choose both anchors equal to \(1/2\).  Under \(P_{1,n,\Delta}\), choose \(\theta_0=1/2\) and
\[
 \theta_1=\frac12+g_{n,\Delta}(0)
 =\frac12+\kappa(h+\Delta).
\]
The range bound puts every conditional Bernoulli mean in \([0,1]\).  For a treated point of radius \(r\leq1/2\),
\[
 |\mu_1(x)-\theta_1|
 =|g_{n,\Delta}(r)-g_{n,\Delta}(0)|
 \leq c_Lr\leq Lr,
\]
and every other point-anchor deviation is zero.  The construction supplies the known sharp half-plane partition, consistency, and conditional Bernoulli laws.  Uniform polar integration gives, on either side and for \(0<H\leq1/2\),
\[
 \mathbb P(T=t,R<H)=\frac{H^2}{2}\geq c_0H^2
\]
because \(c_0\leq1/2\).  Both laws therefore belong to the bounded-outcome point-anchored class \(\mathcal P_L\).  Their target separation is
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)
 =g_{n,\Delta}(0)=\kappa(h+\Delta).
\]

It remains to bound the distance between the released laws.  Partition \([0,1]\) into the positive-mass quantizer cells \(A_j=[j\Delta,\min\{(j+1)\Delta,1\})\), and set
\[
 w_j=\int_{A_j}r\,dr,
 \qquad
 \overline b_j=w_j^{-1}\int_{A_j}rb_h(r)\,dr.
\]
For the uniform disc split into half-discs,
\[
 w_j=\mathbb P(T=1,Q_\Delta(R)=j\Delta).
\]
The alias term is supported in the complete first cell \([0,\Delta)\), where its \(r\)-weighted integral is zero, and vanishes in every other cell.  Thus the treated conditional success probability in cell \(j\) is \(1/2\) under \(P_0\) and \(1/2+\kappa\overline b_j\) under \(P_1\); every control cell agrees.

Let \(Q_k=\mathcal L_{P_k}(Z_\Delta)\).  Direct summation over the two Bernoulli outcomes gives
\[
 \chi^2\!\left(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2+x),
                    \operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\right)=4x^2.
\]
Consequently, Jensen's inequality within every quantizer cell gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 d:=\chi^2(Q_1,Q_0)
 &=4\kappa^2\sum_jw_j\overline b_j^{,2}\\
 &\leq4\kappa^2\int_0^1rb_h(r)^2\,dr
 =4\kappa^2\int_0^h r(h-r)^2\,dr
 =\frac{\kappa^2h^4}{3}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) makes the likelihood ratio a product.  Expanding its second moment and using \(nh^4=1\),
\[
 1+\chi^2(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 =(1+d)^n
 \leq\exp(nd)
 \leq\exp(\kappa^2/3).
\]
Since \(\kappa=c_L/4\leq1/64\), the elementary bound \(e^x-1\leq2x\) for \(0\leq x\leq1\) yields
\[
 \chi^2(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \leq\frac{2\kappa^2}{3}.
\]
Writing \(M=dQ_1^{\otimes n}/dQ_0^{\otimes n}\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 =\frac12\mathbb E_{Q_0^{\otimes n}}|M-1|
 \leq\frac12\{\mathbb E_{Q_0^{\otimes n}}(M-1)^2\}^{1/2}
 \leq\frac{\kappa}{\sqrt6}<\frac14.
\]
Finally \(\alpha<1/4\) implies \(1/4<1-2\alpha\).  The same pair therefore has both the order-\(h\) sampling displacement and the exact order-\(\Delta\) alias displacement, while released divergence is charged only for the sampling bump, as claimed.

target_declaration.statement:
For every \(n\ge256\) and \(0<\Delta\le\Delta_0\), the handle \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}\) admits one same-class baseline--alternative realization with both difficulties present.  Specifically, put \(\kappa=c_L/4\), \(b_h(r)=(h_n-r)_+\),
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf 1\{0\le r<\Delta\},
 \qquad
 g_{n,\Delta}(r)=\kappa\{b_h(r)+a_\Delta(r)\}.
\]
There are \(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta}\in\mathcal P_L\) with \(m_{0,0}=m_{0,1}=1/2\), \(m_{1,0}=1/2\), and \(m_{1,1}=1/2+g_{n,\Delta}\), for which
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\!\left(\mathcal L_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n),
 \mathcal L_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n)\right)
 \le\frac14<1-2\alpha
\]
and
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)
 =\kappa(h_n+\Delta).
\]
target_declaration.justification: One legal uniform-half-disc pair combines the sampling bump and exact first-bin alias while charging released divergence only for the sampling component.
target_declaration.gap: No cited comparator supplies a single pair for the latent annular experiment with both order-\(n^{-1/4}\) and order-\(\Delta\) displacement.
target_declaration.consumer: The pair is the common lower certificate for absolute risk, squared risk, and honest expected interval length over the point-anchored superclass.

semantic_closure.condition: \(Y=T Y(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\) almost surely under \(P\).

For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\),
\[
 \mathcal L_P(Y(t)\mid X=x)
 \in\left\{F:F([0,1])=1\ \text{ and }\ \int_{[0,1]}y\,dF(y)=\mu_t(x)\right\}.
\]

For every \(t\in\{0,1\}\), for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) satisfying \(\lVert x-b\rVert_2\leq1/2\),
\[

\]
For the fixed class constant \(c_0\in(0,1/2]\), \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\) for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and every \(H\in(0,1/2]\).

semantic_closure.name: Unknown-design bivariate bounded-outcome point-anchored boundary class
semantic_closure.construction:
\(\mathcal P_L\) is the set of one-unit laws \(P\) such that \(P_X(\mathcal D)=1\); for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(H\in(0,1/2]\), \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\); \((\mathcal X_{0,P},\mathcal X_{1,P})\) is a known Borel partition of \(\mathcal D\) and \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\) almost surely; \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\) almost surely; for each \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the conditional law of \(Y(t)\) given \(X=x\) is supported on \([0,1]\) and has mean \(\mu_t(x)\); and the point-anchored envelope
\[
 |\mu_t(x)-\theta_t|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
\]
holds for every \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every side-\(t\) point \(x\) of radius at most \(1/2\), where \(\theta_t\in[0,1]\) and \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\).  The sampling condition \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) is imposed on the sample and is not a member property of a one-unit law.

semantic_closure.construction: \(\mathcal E_{n,\Delta}(P)=\mathcal L_P(Z_{\Delta,1},\ldots,Z_{\Delta,n})\),\quad Z_{\Delta,i}=(Y_i,T_i,\Delta\lfloor R_i/\Delta\rfloor)\). The observation \(\sigma\)-field is exactly \(\sigma(Z_{\Delta,1},\ldots,Z_{\Delta,n})\); it excludes \(X_i\), angle, and raw \(R_i\).

semantic_closure.name: Embedded uniform-half-disc joint lower handle
semantic_closure.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}=(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta})\) denote the following pair.  Under both laws, \(X\) is uniform on \(\mathcal D\), \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assignment is sharp, and the control mean is \(1/2\).  Under \(P_{0,n,\Delta}\) the treated mean is \(1/2\); under \(P_{1,n,\Delta}\) it is
\[
 \frac12+\frac{c_L}{4}\left\{(h_n-\lVert x-b\rVert_2)_+
 +\Delta\phi\!\left(\frac{\lVert x-b\rVert_2}{\Delta}\right)
 \mathbf1\{\lVert x-b\rVert_2<\Delta\}\right\}.
\]
Given \(X\), the potential outcomes are conditionally independent Bernoulli variables with these means, and \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\).

semantic_closure.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  For every event \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) with \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\), the conditional outcome is supported on \([0,1]\) and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid B]=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
In particular, put \(A_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Then \(A_t=\{T=t,R<H_{n,\Delta}\}\), its probability \(q_t\) is at least \(c_0H_{n,\Delta}^2>0\), and, with
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t],
\]
one has \(|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|\leq LH_{n,\Delta}\) and \(N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\).  Conditional on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\geq1\), list the selected outcomes in increasing sample-index order as \(Y_{t,1}^{\star},\ldots,Y_{t,k}^{\star}\).  They are independent and identically distributed, supported on \([0,1]\), and have common mean \(\nu_t\); moreover,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{j=1}^kY_{t,j}^{\star},\qquad
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right]=\nu_t,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right)\leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
Outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass, the conditional sum need not be binomial.
semantic_closure.justification: This lemma supplies the conditional selected-sample law, random-count likelihood, bounded variance, and explicit point-anchor bias under the unknown bivariate design.

semantic_closure.consumer: The count and selected-average laws are the implementation contract for the bin-aware estimator and total conditional-Hoeffding interval.

semantic_closure.name: Embedded uniform-half-disc exact first-bin alias pair
semantic_closure.construction:
For each sign, construct \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{\pm,\Delta}\) by drawing \(X\) uniformly on \(\mathcal D\), taking \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assigning \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\), and drawing conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes given \(X\) with
\[
 \mu_{0,\pm}(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mu_{1,\pm}(x)=\frac12\pm c_L\Delta\phi\!\left(\frac{\lVert x-b\rVert_2}{\Delta}\right)
 \mathbf1\{\lVert x-b\rVert_2<\Delta\}.
\]
Finally set \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\), where \(\phi(u)=(1-u)(1-2u)\) and \(c_L=\min\{L/8,1/16\}\).

semantic_closure.name: Total bin-aware local-constant estimator
semantic_closure.construction:
For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), let \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{T_i=t,Q_\Delta(R_i)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Define
\[
 \widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}=
 \begin{cases}
 \Pi_{[0,1]}\!\left(S_{t,n,\Delta}/N_{t,n,\Delta}\right),&N_{t,n,\Delta}>0,\\
 1/2,&N_{t,n,\Delta}=0,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 H_{n,\Delta}=\Delta\left\lceil n^{-1/4}/\Delta\right\rceil,
\]
where \(\Pi_{[0,1]}\) is Euclidean clipping, and set \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}=\widehat m_{1,n,\Delta}-\widehat m_{0,n,\Delta}\).

semantic_closure.name: Bias-enlarged conditional-Hoeffding interval
semantic_closure.construction:
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), set \([\ell_t,u_t]=[0,1]\) when \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=0\).  When \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k>0\), put
\[
 \overline Y_t=\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k,
 \qquad
 r_{k,\alpha}=\sqrt{\frac{\log(4/\alpha)}{2k}},
 \qquad
 [\ell_t,u_t]=\bigl[\max\{0,\overline Y_t-r_{k,\alpha}\},\min\{1,\overline Y_t+r_{k,\alpha}\}\bigr].
\]
With \(B_{n,\Delta}=LH_{n,\Delta}\), define the closed bounded interval
\[
 C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}
 =\bigl[\ell_1-u_0-2B_{n,\Delta},\ u_1-\ell_0+2B_{n,\Delta}\bigr].
\]

semantic_closure.statement:
Let \(k\geq1\), and let \(W_1,\ldots,W_k\) be independent random variables satisfying \(0\leq W_j\leq1\) almost surely and \(\mathbb E[W_j]=p\) for every \(j\).  Then, for every \(r>0\),
\[
 \mathbb P\!\left(\frac1k\sum_{j=1}^kW_j-p\geq r\right)\leq\exp(-2kr^2).
\]

carrier.proof_tex:
Put \(h=h_n\), \(H=H_{n,\Delta}\), and \(\rho=\rho_{n,\Delta}\).  The aligned bandwidth, \(n\geq256\), and \(\Delta\leq\Delta_0\leq1/4\) imply
\[
 h\leq H<h+\Delta\leq2\rho,
 \qquad 0<H<\frac12.
\]
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  Apply \(\mathrm{lem:conditional\text{-}local\text{-}binomial\text{-}law}\) and abbreviate its quantities by \(q_t,\nu_t,N_t,S_t\).  It gives
\[
 q_t\geq c_0H^2,
 \qquad |\nu_t-\theta_t|\leq LH,
 \qquad N_t\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t),
\]
and, conditional on \(N_t=k\geq1\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P[S_t/k\mid N_t=k]=\nu_t,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P(S_t/k\mid N_t=k)\leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
The conditional support gives \(0\leq S_t/k\leq1\), so clipping in \(\mathrm{def:bin\text{-}aware\text{-}estimator}\) does not alter the ratio.

If \(N\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q)\) with \(q>0\), integration of its probability generating function yields
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac1{N+1}\right]
 =\int_0^1(1-q+qx)^n\,dx
 =\frac{1-(1-q)^{n+1}}{(n+1)q}
 \leq\frac1{(n+1)q}.
\]
Because \(k^{-1}\leq2(k+1)^{-1}\) for \(k\geq1\), and by Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{N>0\}}N\right]\leq\frac2{nq},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{N>0\}}{\sqrt N}\right]
 \leq\sqrt{\frac2{nq}}.
\]
Also \(\mathbb P(N=0)=(1-q)^n\leq e^{-nq}\).  Since \(x^{1/2}e^{-x}\leq1\) and \(xe^{-x}\leq1\) for \(x>0\),
\[
 \mathbb P(N=0)\leq(nq)^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 \mathbb P(N=0)\leq(nq)^{-1}.
\]

On \(N_t=k>0\), conditional Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[|S_t/k-\nu_t|\mid N_t=k]\leq\frac1{2\sqrt k}.
\]
On \(N_t=0\), the fixed fallback obeys \(|1/2-\nu_t|\leq1/2\) and \((1/2-\nu_t)^2\leq1/4\), because \(\nu_t\in[0,1]\).  Averaging over the count gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}-\nu_t|
 \leq\left(\frac1{\sqrt2}+\frac12\right)\frac1{\sqrt{nq_t}},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_P[(\widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}-\nu_t)^2]
 \leq\frac3{4nq_t}.
\]
Adding the point-anchor bias and using \((a+b)^2\leq2a^2+2b^2\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}-\theta_t|
 \leq LH+\left(\frac1{\sqrt2}+\frac12\right)\frac1{\sqrt{c_0nH^2}},
\]
\[
 \mathbb E_P[(\widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}-\theta_t)^2]
 \leq2L^2H^2+\frac3{2c_0nH^2}.
\]
Since \(H\geq h=n^{-1/4}\),
\[
 \frac1{\sqrt nH}\leq h\leq\rho,
 \qquad
 \frac1{nH^2}\leq h^2\leq\rho^2.
\]
Using \(\tau_P(b)=\theta_1-\theta_0\), the triangle inequality, and \((x-y)^2\leq2x^2+2y^2\), there are finite constants \(C_1,C_2\), depending only on \(L\) and \(c_0\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P|\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}-\tau_P(b)|\leq C_1\rho,
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}-\tau_P(b))^2]\leq C_2\rho^2.
\]
The counts and localized sums are measurable functions of \(Z_\Delta^n\), and the zero-count branch is fixed.  Hence \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}\) is one law-independent element of \(\mathcal T_{n,\Delta}\).  Taking the infima in \(\mathrm{def:minimax\text{-}risks}\) proves both upper bounds over the bounded-outcome superclass.

For the converse, use the pair from \(\mathrm{thm:single\text{-}joint\text{-}pair}\).  Let \(Q_0,Q_1\) be its released product laws, let \(\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1\) be its targets, and put \(\delta=|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|\).  With \(\kappa=c_L/4>0\), that theorem gives
\[
 P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta}\in\mathcal P_L,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\leq\frac14,
 \qquad
 \delta=\kappa(h+\Delta)\geq\kappa\rho.
\]
For any released-data estimator \(a\), take densities \(q_0,q_1\) with respect to \(Q_0+Q_1\).  Pointwise,
\[
 |a-\vartheta_0|+|a-\vartheta_1|\geq\delta,
 \qquad
 (a-\vartheta_0)^2+(a-\vartheta_1)^2\geq\frac{\delta^2}{2},
\]
the second inequality following by minimizing its left-hand side over \(a\).  Since
\[
 \int\min(q_0,q_1)=1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1),
\]
multiplying by the minimum density, integrating, and using that a maximum is at least half a sum give
\[
 \max_{j\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_{Q_j}|a-\vartheta_j|
 \geq\frac\delta2\{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\}
 \geq\frac{3\kappa}{8}\rho,
\]
\[
 \max_{j\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_{Q_j}(a-\vartheta_j)^2
 \geq\frac{\delta^2}{4}\{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\}
 \geq\frac{3\kappa^2}{16}\rho^2.
\]
The supremum over \(\mathcal P_L\) dominates this same-class pair.  Taking the infimum over all released-data estimators proves the lower bounds.  Choose \(c\) no larger than both lower constants and \(C\) no smaller than \(C_1,C_2\).  These constants have only the dependence allowed in the statement, completing the proof.

target_declaration.statement: There exist constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \(L\), \(c_0\), and \(\Delta_0\), such that for every \(n\geq256\) and \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), \(c\rho_{n,\Delta}\leq\mathfrak R^{(1)}_{n,\Delta}\leq C\rho_{n,\Delta}\) and \(c\rho_{n,\Delta}^2\leq\mathfrak R^{(2)}_{n,\Delta}\leq C\rho_{n,\Delta}^2\). The upper bounds are attained, up to \(C\), by \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}\).
target_declaration.justification: This is the sampling--quantization minimax frontier over the unknown-design bivariate Lipschitz boundary class.
target_declaration.gap: Exact-radius boundary methods and ordinary scalar rounding methods do not derive the latent-annular rate \(\max\{n^{-1/4},\Delta\}\) over this superclass.
target_declaration.consumer: The result tells users of the \(\texttt{rd2d}\) R, Python, and Stata workflows when the Ser Pilo Paga analysis is sample-limited or release-precision-limited.

semantic_closure.name: Unknown-design bivariate bounded-outcome point-anchored boundary class
semantic_closure.construction:
\(\mathcal P_L\) is the set of one-unit laws \(P\) such that \(P_X(\mathcal D)=1\); for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(H\in(0,1/2]\), \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\); \((\mathcal X_{0,P},\mathcal X_{1,P})\) is a known Borel partition of \(\mathcal D\) and \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\) almost surely; \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\) almost surely; for each \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the conditional law of \(Y(t)\) given \(X=x\) is supported on \([0,1]\) and has mean \(\mu_t(x)\); and the point-anchored envelope
\[
 |\mu_t(x)-\theta_t|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
\]
holds for every \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every side-\(t\) point \(x\) of radius at most \(1/2\), where \(\theta_t\in[0,1]\) and \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\).  The sampling condition \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) is imposed on the sample and is not a member property of a one-unit law.

semantic_closure.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  For every event \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) with \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\), the conditional outcome is supported on \([0,1]\) and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid B]=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
In particular, put \(A_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Then \(A_t=\{T=t,R<H_{n,\Delta}\}\), its probability \(q_t\) is at least \(c_0H_{n,\Delta}^2>0\), and, with
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t],
\]
one has \(|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|\leq LH_{n,\Delta}\) and \(N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\).  Conditional on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\geq1\), list the selected outcomes in increasing sample-index order as \(Y_{t,1}^{\star},\ldots,Y_{t,k}^{\star}\).  They are independent and identically distributed, supported on \([0,1]\), and have common mean \(\nu_t\); moreover,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{j=1}^kY_{t,j}^{\star},\qquad
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right]=\nu_t,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right)\leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
Outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass, the conditional sum need not be binomial.
semantic_closure.justification: This lemma supplies the conditional selected-sample law, random-count likelihood, bounded variance, and explicit point-anchor bias under the unknown bivariate design.
semantic_closure.gap: Exact-radius and scalar-running-variable analyses do not state the conditional iid selected-outcome law after retaining only side and quantized radius under an unknown bivariate design.
semantic_closure.consumer: The count and selected-average laws are the implementation contract for the bin-aware estimator and total conditional-Hoeffding interval.

semantic_closure.statement:
For every \(n\ge256\) and \(0<\Delta\le\Delta_0\), the handle \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}\) admits one same-class baseline--alternative realization with both difficulties present.  Specifically, put \(\kappa=c_L/4\), \(b_h(r)=(h_n-r)_+\),
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf 1\{0\le r<\Delta\},
 \qquad
 g_{n,\Delta}(r)=\kappa\{b_h(r)+a_\Delta(r)\}.
\]
There are \(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta}\in\mathcal P_L\) with \(m_{0,0}=m_{0,1}=1/2\), \(m_{1,0}=1/2\), and \(m_{1,1}=1/2+g_{n,\Delta}\), for which
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\!\left(\mathcal L_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n),
 \mathcal L_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n)\right)
 \le\frac14<1-2\alpha
\]
and
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)
 =\kappa(h_n+\Delta).
\]

semantic_closure.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}=(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta})\) denote the following pair.  Under both laws, \(X\) is uniform on \(\mathcal D\), \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assignment is sharp, and the control mean is \(1/2\).  Under \(P_{0,n,\Delta}\) the treated mean is \(1/2\); under \(P_{1,n,\Delta}\) it is
\[

 +\Delta\phi\!\left(\frac{\lVert x-b\rVert_2}{\Delta}\right)
 \mathbf1\{\lVert x-b\rVert_2<\Delta\}\right\}.
\]
Given \(X\), the potential outcomes are conditionally independent Bernoulli variables with these means, and \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\).

For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), set \([\ell_t,u_t]=[0,1]\) when \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=0\).  When \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k>0\), put
\[

\]
With \(B_{n,\Delta}=LH_{n,\Delta}\), define the closed bounded interval
\[
 C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}
 =\bigl[\ell_1-u_0-2B_{n,\Delta},\ u_1-\ell_0+2B_{n,\Delta}\bigr].
\]

semantic_closure.statement:
Let \(k\geq1\), and let \(W_1,\ldots,W_k\) be independent random variables satisfying \(0\leq W_j\leq1\) almost surely and \(\mathbb E[W_j]=p\) for every \(j\).  Then, for every \(r>0\),
\[
 \mathbb P\!\left(\frac1k\sum_{j=1}^kW_j-p\geq r\right)\leq\exp(-2kr^2).
\]

carrier.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), and write
\[
 h=h_n=n^{-1/4},\qquad H=H_{n,\Delta},\qquad B=LH.
\]
The aligned bandwidth satisfies
\[
 h\leq H<h+\Delta\leq\frac12.
\]
For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(\mathrm{lem:conditional\text{-}local\text{-}binomial\text{-}law}\) gives
\[
 q_t:=\mathbb P_P(T=t,R<H)\geq c_0H^2>0,
 \qquad
 \nu_t:=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid T=t,R<H],
\]
\[
 |\nu_t-\theta_t|\leq LH=B,
 \qquad
 N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t).
\]
It also gives, conditional on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\geq1\), independent selected outcomes in \([0,1]\) with common mean \(\nu_t\) and sum \(S_{t,n,\Delta}\).  The rounded and latent localization events agree exactly because
\[
 \{Q_\Delta(R)<H\}
 =\{\Delta\lfloor R/\Delta\rfloor<K_{n,\Delta}\Delta\}
 =\{R<K_{n,\Delta}\Delta\}
 =\{R<H\}.
\]

If \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=0\), the side interval in \(\mathrm{def:total\text{-}honest\text{-}interval}\) is \([0,1]\), which contains \(\nu_t\).  If the count is \(k>0\), apply the cited \(\mathrm{lem:hoeffding\text{-}bounded\text{-}average}\), conditionally on that count, first to the selected outcomes and then to their complements \(1-Y_{t,j}^{\star}\), with
\[
 r_{k,\alpha}=\sqrt{\frac{\log(4/\alpha)}{2k}}>0.
\]
The two one-sided bounds and a union bound yield
\[
 \mathbb P_P\!\left(\left|\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k-\nu_t\right|>r_{k,\alpha}\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right)
 \leq2e^{-2kr_{k,\alpha}^2}=\frac\alpha2.
\]
Because \(\nu_t\in[0,1]\), intersecting the untruncated interval with \([0,1]\) cannot remove \(\nu_t\).  Averaging over all counts, including the zero-count branch, gives
\[
 \mathbb P_P\{\nu_t\in[\ell_t,u_t]\}\geq1-\frac\alpha2.
\]
A union bound gives an event \(E\) of probability at least \(1-\alpha\) on which both side inclusions hold.  On \(E\),
\[
 \nu_1-\nu_0\in[\ell_1-u_0,u_1-\ell_0].
\]
The two point-anchor bias bounds imply
\[
 |\tau_P(b)-(\nu_1-\nu_0)|
 =| (\theta_1-\nu_1)-(\theta_0-\nu_0)|
 \leq2B.
\]
Thus \(\tau_P(b)\in C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}\) on \(E\).  Since \(P\) was arbitrary, coverage is uniform over \(\mathcal P_L\).

The counts and sums are measurable functions of \(Z_\Delta^n\), and every endpoint operation is Borel measurable.  For every sample, \(0\leq\ell_t\leq u_t\leq1\), and
\[
 (u_1-\ell_0+2B)-(\ell_1-u_0-2B)
 =(u_1-\ell_1)+(u_0-\ell_0)+4B\geq0.
\]
Hence the construction is an ordered, closed, bounded, \(\sigma(Z_\Delta^n)\)-measurable interval, including when either count is zero.

For expected length, put \(a_\alpha=\sqrt{\log(4/\alpha)/2}\).  For a positive count \(k\), clipping can only shorten the side interval, so
\[
 u_t-\ell_t\leq\frac{2a_\alpha}{\sqrt k};
\]
for a zero count its length is one.  If \(N\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q)\), then
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac1{N+1}\right]
 =\int_0^1(1-q+qx)^n\,dx
 =\frac{1-(1-q)^{n+1}}{(n+1)q}
 \leq\frac1{(n+1)q}.
\]
Using \(k^{-1}\leq2(k+1)^{-1}\) and Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{N>0\}}{\sqrt N}\right]
 \leq\sqrt{\mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{N>0\}}N\right]}
 \leq\sqrt{\frac2{nq}}.
\]
Also \(\mathbb P(N=0)=(1-q)^n\leq e^{-nq}\leq(nq)^{-1/2}\), because \(x^{1/2}e^{-x}\leq1\) for \(x>0\).  Therefore
\[
 \mathbb E_P[u_t-\ell_t]
 \leq\frac{1+2\sqrt2a_\alpha}{\sqrt{nq_t}}
 \leq\frac{1+2\sqrt{\log(4/\alpha)}}{\sqrt{c_0nH^2}}.
\]
The full interval has length
\[
 \operatorname{length}(C_{n,\Delta,\alpha})
 =(u_1-\ell_1)+(u_0-\ell_0)+4LH.
\]
Finally,
\[
 H<h+\Delta\leq2\rho_{n,\Delta},
 \qquad
 \frac1{\sqrt nH}\leq h\leq\rho_{n,\Delta}.
\]
Summing the two side bounds gives the explicit uniform inequality
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_{n,\Delta,\alpha})]
 \leq
 \left\{
 \frac{2+4\sqrt{\log(4/\alpha)}}{\sqrt{c_0}}+8L
 \right\}\rho_{n,\Delta}.
\]
This proves totality, honest coverage, and the asserted expected-length order over the bounded-outcome superclass.

semantic_closure.name: Unknown-design bivariate bounded-outcome point-anchored boundary class
semantic_closure.construction:
\(\mathcal P_L\) is the set of one-unit laws \(P\) such that \(P_X(\mathcal D)=1\); for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(H\in(0,1/2]\), \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\); \((\mathcal X_{0,P},\mathcal X_{1,P})\) is a known Borel partition of \(\mathcal D\) and \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\) almost surely; \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\) almost surely; for each \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the conditional law of \(Y(t)\) given \(X=x\) is supported on \([0,1]\) and has mean \(\mu_t(x)\); and the point-anchored envelope
\[
 |\mu_t(x)-\theta_t|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
\]
holds for every \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every side-\(t\) point \(x\) of radius at most \(1/2\), where \(\theta_t\in[0,1]\) and \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\).  The sampling condition \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) is imposed on the sample and is not a member property of a one-unit law.

semantic_closure.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  For every event \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) with \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\), the conditional outcome is supported on \([0,1]\) and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid B]=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
In particular, put \(A_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Then \(A_t=\{T=t,R<H_{n,\Delta}\}\), its probability \(q_t\) is at least \(c_0H_{n,\Delta}^2>0\), and, with
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t],
\]
one has \(|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|\leq LH_{n,\Delta}\) and \(N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\).  Conditional on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\geq1\), list the selected outcomes in increasing sample-index order as \(Y_{t,1}^{\star},\ldots,Y_{t,k}^{\star}\).  They are independent and identically distributed, supported on \([0,1]\), and have common mean \(\nu_t\); moreover,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{j=1}^kY_{t,j}^{\star},\qquad
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right]=\nu_t,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right)\leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
Outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass, the conditional sum need not be binomial.

semantic_closure.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}=(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta})\) denote the following pair.  Under both laws, \(X\) is uniform on \(\mathcal D\), \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assignment is sharp, and the control mean is \(1/2\).  Under \(P_{0,n,\Delta}\) the treated mean is \(1/2\); under \(P_{1,n,\Delta}\) it is

carrier.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(C\in\mathcal C_{n,\Delta}(\alpha)\).  Let \((P_0,P_1)\) be the Bernoulli pair supplied by \(\mathrm{thm:single\text{-}joint\text{-}pair}\), and define
\[
 Q_j=\mathcal L_{P_j}(Z_\Delta^n),
 \qquad
 \vartheta_j=\tau_{P_j}(b),
 \qquad
 \delta=|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|,
 \quad j\in\{0,1\}.
\]
The joint-pair theorem gives \(P_0,P_1\in\mathcal P_L\), and, with \(\kappa=c_L/4\),
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\leq\frac14,
 \qquad
 \delta=\kappa(h_n+\Delta).
\]
By \(\mathrm{def:honest\text{-}class}\), \(C\) is \(\sigma(Z_\Delta^n)\)-measurable and covers each target with probability at least \(1-\alpha\).  For \(A_j=\{\vartheta_j\in C\}\),
\[
 Q_j(A_j)\geq1-\alpha,
 \qquad j\in\{0,1\}.
\]
The variational characterization of total variation, applied to \(A_1\), gives
\[
 Q_0(A_1)\geq Q_1(A_1)-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)
 \geq1-\alpha-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1).
\]
Thus a union bound under \(Q_0\) yields
\[
 Q_0(A_0\cap A_1)
 \geq1-Q_0(A_0^c)-Q_0(A_1^c)
 \geq1-2\alpha-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)
 \geq\frac34-2\alpha>0,
\]
where positivity uses \(0<\alpha<1/4\).  On \(A_0\cap A_1\), the closed interval \(C\) contains both targets, so \(\operatorname{length}(C)\geq\delta\).  Nonnegativity of length therefore implies
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_0}[\operatorname{length}(C)]
 \geq\delta Q_0(A_0\cap A_1)
 \geq\frac{c_L}{4}\left(\frac34-2\alpha\right)(h_n+\Delta)
 \geq\frac{c_L}{4}\left(\frac34-2\alpha\right)\rho_{n,\Delta}.
\]
Since \(P_0\in\mathcal P_L\), the supremum over \(P\in\mathcal P_L\) is at least this expectation.  As the inequality holds for every \(C\in\mathcal C_{n,\Delta}(\alpha)\), \(\mathrm{def:honest\text{-}width}\) gives
\[
 \mathfrak W_{n,\Delta}(\alpha)
 \geq c_{L,\alpha,\Delta_0}\rho_{n,\Delta},
 \qquad
 c_{L,\alpha,\Delta_0}:=\frac{c_L}{4}\left(\frac34-2\alpha\right)>0.
\]
This constant is independent of \(n\) and \(\Delta\); permitting its label to include \(\Delta_0\) does not change the assertion.

For the matching upper bound, \(\mathrm{thm:total\text{-}honest\text{-}interval}\) proves that \(C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}\) is a total released-sample interval, uniformly honest over \(\mathcal P_L\), whose worst-case expected length is at most \(C_{L,c_0,\alpha,\Delta_0}\rho_{n,\Delta}\).  Thus \(C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}\in\mathcal C_{n,\Delta}(\alpha)\), and inserting it into the infimum in \(\mathrm{def:honest\text{-}width}\) gives
\[
 \mathfrak W_{n,\Delta}(\alpha)
 \leq C_{L,c_0,\alpha,\Delta_0}\rho_{n,\Delta}.
\]
The two inequalities establish \(\mathfrak W_{n,\Delta}(\alpha)\asymp\rho_{n,\Delta}\) uniformly over all allowed \(n\) and \(\Delta\).

\(\mathcal P_L\) is the set of one-unit laws \(P\) such that \(P_X(\mathcal D)=1\); for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(H\in(0,1/2]\), \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\); \((\mathcal X_{0,P},\mathcal X_{1,P})\) is a known Borel partition of \(\mathcal D\) and \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\) almost surely; \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\) almost surely; for each \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the conditional law of \(Y(t)\) given \(X=x\) is supported on \([0,1]\) and has mean \(\mu_t(x)\); and the point-anchored envelope
\[
 |\mu_t(x)-\theta_t|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
\]
holds for every \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every side-\(t\) point \(x\) of radius at most \(1/2\), where \(\theta_t\in[0,1]\) and \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\).  The sampling condition \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) is imposed on the sample and is not a member property of a one-unit law.

semantic_closure.construction: \(\mathcal E_{n,\Delta}(P)=\mathcal L_P(Z_{\Delta,1},\ldots,Z_{\Delta,n})\),\quad Z_{\Delta,i}=(Y_i,T_i,\Delta\lfloor R_i/\Delta\rfloor)\). The observation \(\sigma\)-field is exactly \(\sigma(Z_{\Delta,1},\ldots,Z_{\Delta,n})\); it excludes \(X_i\), angle, and raw \(R_i\).

semantic_closure.name: Embedded uniform-half-disc joint lower handle
semantic_closure.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}=(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta})\) denote the following pair.  Under both laws, \(X\) is uniform on \(\mathcal D\), \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assignment is sharp, and the control mean is \(1/2\).  Under \(P_{0,n,\Delta}\) the treated mean is \(1/2\); under \(P_{1,n,\Delta}\) it is
\[
 \frac12+\frac{c_L}{4}\left\{(h_n-\lVert x-b\rVert_2)_+
 +\Delta\phi\!\left(\frac{\lVert x-b\rVert_2}{\Delta}\right)
 \mathbf1\{\lVert x-b\rVert_2<\Delta\}\right\}.
\]
Given \(X\), the potential outcomes are conditionally independent Bernoulli variables with these means, and \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\).

semantic_closure.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  For every event \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) with \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\), the conditional outcome is supported on \([0,1]\) and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid B]=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
In particular, put \(A_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Then \(A_t=\{T=t,R<H_{n,\Delta}\}\), its probability \(q_t\) is at least \(c_0H_{n,\Delta}^2>0\), and, with
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t],
\]
one has \(|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|\leq LH_{n,\Delta}\) and \(N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\).  Conditional on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\geq1\), list the selected outcomes in increasing sample-index order as \(Y_{t,1}^{\star},\ldots,Y_{t,k}^{\star}\).  They are independent and identically distributed, supported on \([0,1]\), and have common mean \(\nu_t\); moreover,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{j=1}^kY_{t,j}^{\star},\qquad
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right]=\nu_t,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right)\leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
Outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass, the conditional sum need not be binomial.
semantic_closure.justification: This lemma supplies the conditional selected-sample law, random-count likelihood, bounded variance, and explicit point-anchor bias under the unknown bivariate design.
semantic_closure.gap: Exact-radius and scalar-running-variable analyses do not state the conditional iid selected-outcome law after retaining only side and quantized radius under an unknown bivariate design.
semantic_closure.consumer: The count and selected-average laws are the implementation contract for the bin-aware estimator and total conditional-Hoeffding interval.

semantic_closure.name: Bias-enlarged conditional-Hoeffding interval
semantic_closure.construction:
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), set \([\ell_t,u_t]=[0,1]\) when \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=0\).  When \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k>0\), put
\[
 \overline Y_t=\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k,
 \qquad
 r_{k,\alpha}=\sqrt{\frac{\log(4/\alpha)}{2k}},
 \qquad
 [\ell_t,u_t]=\bigl[\max\{0,\overline Y_t-r_{k,\alpha}\},\min\{1,\overline Y_t+r_{k,\alpha}\}\bigr].
\]
With \(B_{n,\Delta}=LH_{n,\Delta}\), define the closed bounded interval
\[
 C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}
 =\bigl[\ell_1-u_0-2B_{n,\Delta},\ u_1-\ell_0+2B_{n,\Delta}\bigr].
\]

semantic_closure.statement:
Let \(k\geq1\), and let \(W_1,\ldots,W_k\) be independent random variables satisfying \(0\leq W_j\leq1\) almost surely and \(\mathbb E[W_j]=p\) for every \(j\).  Then, for every \(r>0\),
\[
 \mathbb P\!\left(\frac1k\sum_{j=1}^kW_j-p\geq r\right)\leq\exp(-2kr^2).
\]

carrier.proof_tex:
By definition,
\[
 h_n=n^{-1/4},
 \qquad
 \rho_{n,\Delta}=\max\{h_n,\Delta\}.
\]
If \(0<\Delta\leq n^{-1/4}=h_n\), then \(\rho_{n,\Delta}=h_n=n^{-1/4}\).  Substitution into \(\mathrm{thm:minimax\text{-}frontier}\) gives minimax absolute-error order \(n^{-1/4}\) and squared-risk order
\[
 (n^{-1/4})^2=n^{-1/2}.
\]
Substitution into \(\mathrm{thm:honest\text{-}length\text{-}lower}\), including its matching upper conclusion, gives honest expected-length order \(n^{-1/4}\).

Along a sequence satisfying \(n^{-1/4}=o(\Delta)\), the definition of little-oh gives \(n^{-1/4}/\Delta\to0\), so \(n^{-1/4}<\Delta\) eventually.  Consequently \(\rho_{n,\Delta}=\Delta\) eventually.  The same two theorems then give minimax absolute-error and honest expected-length order \(\Delta\), and minimax squared-risk order \(\Delta^2\).  These are conclusions for the bounded-outcome point-anchored rounded-radius experiment; no equivalence to an exact-coordinate experiment is used or asserted.

target_declaration.statement: Along every sequence with \(0<\Delta\leq n^{-1/4}\), the unknown-design frontier has minimax absolute-error and honest expected-length order \(n^{-1/4}\) and squared-risk order \(n^{-1/2}\).  Along every sequence with \(n^{-1/4}=o(\Delta)\), the corresponding orders are \(\Delta\) and \(\Delta^2\), respectively.
target_declaration.justification: This separates the fine-quantization sampling regime from the coarsening-dominated regime without claiming equivalence to an exact-score theorem.
target_declaration.gap: The exact-score literature is a rate sanity check only; it does not imply the latent-annular experiment proved here.
target_declaration.consumer: Applied users can diagnose whether sample size or released radial precision is the active constraint.

Conditional on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\geq1\), list the selected outcomes in increasing sample-index order as \(Y_{t,1}^{\star},\ldots,Y_{t,k}^{\star}\).  They are independent and identically distributed, supported on \([0,1]\), and have common mean \(\nu_t\); moreover,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{j=1}^kY_{t,j}^{\star},\qquad
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right]=\nu_t,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right)\leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
Outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass, the conditional sum need not be binomial.

payload.statement:
For every \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), every release law \(Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta\) has positive probability on each first-bin side event \(\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)=0\}\), and
\[
 2c_L\Delta\leq\omega_\Delta\leq4L\Delta.
\]
Consequently, the full-data causal functional \(\tau_P(b)\) is generally not point identified from a fixed-\(\Delta\) released law, and its worst release-fiber diameter is of order \(\Delta\).
payload.proof_tex:
Fix \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\) and \(Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta\).  By \(\mathrm{def:released\text{-}identified\text{-}set}\), there is at least one \(P\in\mathcal P_L\) such that \(Q=\mathcal L_P(Z_\Delta)\).  For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), define the released first-bin side event
\[
 B_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)=0\}.
\]
Because \(R\in[0,1]\) and \(Q_\Delta(r)=\Delta\lfloor r/\Delta\rfloor\),
\[
 B_t=\{T=t,0\leq R<\Delta\}=\{T=t,R<\Delta\}.
\]
The inequalities \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\leq1/4<1/2\) permit use of the two-sided local-mass condition in \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}disc\text{-}design}\) and \(\mathrm{def:half\text{-}disc\text{-}class}\), giving
\[
 Q(B_t)=\mathbb P_P(B_t)\geq c_0\Delta^2>0.
\]
This proves the first assertion for every attainable \(Q\).

Since \(B_t\) has positive \(Q\)-probability, the released law determines the number
\[
 \zeta_t(Q)=\mathbb E_Q[Y\mid B_t]
 =\frac{\int y\mathbf1_{B_t}(y,t',q)\,dQ(y,t',q)}{Q(B_t)}.
\]
For any \(P'\in\mathcal P_L\) satisfying \(\mathcal L_{P'}(Z_\Delta)=Q\), the general event assertion of \(\mathrm{lem:conditional\text{-}local\text{-}binomial\text{-}law}\), which follows from sharp assignment, consistency, and the declared conditional means, yields
\[
 \zeta_t(Q)=\mathbb E_{P'}[Y\mid B_t]
 =\mathbb E_{P'}[\mu_t(X)\mid B_t].
\]
On \(B_t\), one has \(R<\Delta\leq1/2\).  The point-anchor envelope in \(\mathrm{ass:radial\text{-}lipschitz}\) therefore gives, using conditional Jensen's inequality for the absolute value,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\zeta_t(Q)-\theta_{t,P'}|
 &\leq \mathbb E_{P'}[|\mu_t(X)-\theta_{t,P'}|\mid B_t]\\
 &\leq L\mathbb E_{P'}[R\mid B_t]
 \leq L\Delta.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The anchor \(\theta_{t,P'}\) is unambiguous by \(\mathrm{lem:boundary\text{-}anchor\text{-}uniqueness}\).  Hence, if \(P',P''\in\mathcal P_L\) induce the same \(Q\), then
\[
 |\theta_{t,P'}-\theta_{t,P''}|
 \leq |\theta_{t,P'}-\zeta_t(Q)|+|\zeta_t(Q)-\theta_{t,P''}|
 \leq2L\Delta.
\]
Using \(\tau_P(b)=\theta_{1,P}-\theta_{0,P}\) and the triangle inequality,
\[
 |\tau_{P'}(b)-\tau_{P''}(b)|
 \leq |\theta_{1,P'}-\theta_{1,P''}|+|\theta_{0,P'}-\theta_{0,P''}|
 \leq4L\Delta.
\]
Taking the supremum first over all \(P',P''\) in a fixed release fiber and then over \(Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta\), as prescribed by \(\mathrm{def:released\text{-}identified\text{-}set}\), proves \(\omega_\Delta\leq4L\Delta\).

For the converse, \(\mathrm{lem:first\text{-}bin\text{-}alias}\) supplies \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta},P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}\in\mathcal P_L\) having a common released law, say \(Q^{\mathrm{alias}}\), and satisfying
\[
 \tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}}(b)
 -\tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}}(b)=2c_L\Delta.
\]
Both displayed target values consequently belong to \(I_\Delta(Q^{\mathrm{alias}})\), so
\[
 \omega_\Delta
 \geq\operatorname{diam}I_\Delta(Q^{\mathrm{alias}})
 \geq2c_L\Delta.
\]
Here \(c_L>0\) by its definition and \(L\geq1\).  Thus a fixed-width release has at least one fiber containing two distinct values of the structural causal target, which proves general failure of point identification.  The two positive finite constants \(2c_L\) and \(4L\) give the asserted order in \(\Delta\).
payload.justification: This proposition proves that fixed radial precision creates population ambiguity for the structural boundary effect before finite-sample error is considered.
payload.gap: Exact-coordinate theory has no such release fiber, and scalar discrete-score results do not calculate its radial two-sided diameter over this point-anchored class.
payload.consumer: The result quantifies the causal information lost by releasing only treatment side and floor-rounded radius.

carrier.proof_tex:
Put \(h=h_n\), \(H=H_{n,\Delta}\), and \(\rho=\rho_{n,\Delta}\).  By \(\mathrm{def:bin\text{-}aware\text{-}estimator}\),
\[
 H=\Delta\left\lceil\frac h\Delta\right\rceil,
 \qquad h=n^{-1/4}.
\]
The inequalities \(x\leq\lceil x\rceil<x+1\), together with \(n\geq256\) and \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\leq1/4\), imply
\[
 h\leq H<h+\Delta\leq2\rho,
 \qquad 0<H<\frac12.
\]

We first prove the upper bounds with the single law-independent estimator in \(\mathrm{def:bin\text{-}aware\text{-}estimator}\).  Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  Applying \(\mathrm{lem:conditional\text{-}local\text{-}binomial\text{-}law}\), abbreviate its quantities by \(q_t,\nu_t,N_t,S_t\).  The class conditions and \(0<H<1/2\) give
\[
 q_t\geq c_0H^2>0,
 \qquad |\nu_t-\theta_t|\leq LH,
 \qquad N_t\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t).
\]
For every \(k\geq1\) having positive count probability, the same lemma gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\frac{S_t}{k}\,\middle|\,N_t=k\right]=\nu_t,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\frac{S_t}{k}\,\middle|\,N_t=k\right)\leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
The selected outcomes lie in \([0,1]\), so \(S_t/k\in[0,1]\); the clipping operation therefore leaves the positive-count average unchanged.

We next derive the required random-denominator bounds.  If \(N\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q)\) with \(q>0\), finite expansion and \((k+1)^{-1}=\int_0^1x^k\,dx\) yield
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac1{N+1}\right]
 =\int_0^1(1-q+qx)^n\,dx
 =\frac{1-(1-q)^{n+1}}{(n+1)q}
 \leq\frac1{(n+1)q}.
\]
Since \(k^{-1}\leq2(k+1)^{-1}\) for \(k\geq1\), and since Cauchy--Schwarz applies to the bounded random variable \(\mathbf1\{N>0\}/\sqrt N\),
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{N>0\}}N\right]
 \leq\frac2{nq},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{N>0\}}{\sqrt N}\right]
 \leq\sqrt{\frac2{nq}}.
\]
Also, independence gives
\[
 \mathbb P(N=0)=(1-q)^n\leq e^{-nq}.
\]
For \(x>0\), \(x^{1/2}e^{-x}\leq1\) and \(xe^{-x}\leq1\), whence
\[
 \mathbb P(N=0)\leq(nq)^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 \mathbb P(N=0)\leq(nq)^{-1}.
\]

Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz and the conditional variance bound imply, on \(N_t=k>0\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\left|\frac{S_t}{k}-\nu_t\right|\,\middle|\,N_t=k\right]
 \leq\frac1{2\sqrt k},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\left(\frac{S_t}{k}-\nu_t\right)^2\,\middle|\,N_t=k\right]
 \leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
On \(N_t=0\), the fallback is \(1/2\), while \(\nu_t\in[0,1]\), so its absolute and squared deviations from \(\nu_t\) are at most \(1/2\) and \(1/4\), respectively.  Averaging over \(N_t\) and using the preceding bounds gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}-\nu_t|
 \leq\left(\frac1{\sqrt2}+\frac12\right)\frac1{\sqrt{nq_t}},
\]
\[
 \mathbb E_P[(\widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}-\nu_t)^2]
 \leq\frac3{4nq_t}.
\]
Writing \(A=1/\sqrt2+1/2\), using \(q_t\geq c_0H^2\), \(|\nu_t-\theta_t|\leq LH\), and \((a+b)^2\leq2a^2+2b^2\), we obtain
\[
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}-\theta_t|
 \leq LH+\frac{A}{\sqrt{c_0n}\,H},
\]
\[
 \mathbb E_P[(\widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}-\theta_t)^2]
 \leq2L^2H^2+\frac3{2c_0nH^2}.
\]
Since \(H\geq h=n^{-1/4}\),
\[
 \frac1{\sqrt nH}\leq h\leq\rho,
 \qquad
 \frac1{nH^2}\leq h^2\leq\rho^2.
\]
Combining these inequalities with \(H<2\rho\), \(\tau_P(b)=\theta_1-\theta_0\), the triangle inequality, and \((x-y)^2\leq2x^2+2y^2\), gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}-\tau_P(b)|
 \leq C_1\rho,
 \qquad C_1=4L+\frac{2A}{\sqrt{c_0}},
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}
 \mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}-\tau_P(b))^2]
 \leq C_2\rho^2,
 \qquad C_2=32L^2+\frac6{c_0}.
\]
The counts and sums are measurable functions of \(Z_\Delta^n\), the bandwidth is known, and the zero-count fallback is fixed.  Thus \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}\in\mathcal T_{n,\Delta}\).  Taking the two infima in \(\mathrm{def:minimax\text{-}risks}\) proves both upper bounds and their attainment by the displayed estimator up to constants.

The two components of the converse have distinct statistical meanings.  By \(\mathrm{prop:release\text{-}fiber\text{-}diameter}\),
\[
 2c_L\Delta\leq\omega_\Delta\leq4L\Delta.
\]
Thus the structural target is generally not point identified by a fixed-\(\Delta\) released law, and \(\Delta\) is a population release-fiber ambiguity cost.  This does not redefine \(\tau_P(b)\).  In contrast, \(h=n^{-1/4}\) is the local sampling-error scale.  We combine both scales with the single same-class certificate of \(\mathrm{thm:single\text{-}joint\text{-}pair}\).

Let \(P_j=P_{j,n,\Delta}\), \(Q_j=\mathcal L_{P_j}(Z_\Delta^n)\), and \(\vartheta_j=\tau_{P_j}(b)\) for \(j\in\{0,1\}\).  With \(\kappa=c_L/4>0\) and \(\delta=|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|\), that theorem gives
\[
 P_0,P_1\in\mathcal P_L,
 \qquad \operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\leq\frac14,
 \qquad \delta=\kappa(h+\Delta)\geq\kappa\rho.
\]
Fix any estimator \(a\in\mathcal T_{n,\Delta}\), let \(\lambda=Q_0+Q_1\), and write \(f_j=dQ_j/d\lambda\).  For every released sample \(z\),
\[
 |a(z)-\vartheta_0|+|a(z)-\vartheta_1|\geq\delta,
\]
and completion of the square gives
\[
 (a(z)-\vartheta_0)^2+(a(z)-\vartheta_1)^2
 =2\left(a(z)-\frac{\vartheta_0+\vartheta_1}{2}\right)^2+\frac{\delta^2}{2}
 \geq\frac{\delta^2}{2}.
\]
Moreover, by the density formula for total variation,
\[
 \int\min(f_0,f_1)\,d\lambda
 =1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1).
\]
Because \(f_j\geq\min(f_0,f_1)\), multiplying the pointwise loss inequalities by \(\min(f_0,f_1)\), integrating, and using that a maximum is at least half a sum yields
\[
 \max_{j\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_{Q_j}|a-\vartheta_j|
 \geq\frac\delta2\{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\}
 \geq\frac{3\kappa}{8}\rho,
\]
and
\[
 \max_{j\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_{Q_j}(a-\vartheta_j)^2
 \geq\frac{\delta^2}{4}\{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\}
 \geq\frac{3\kappa^2}{16}\rho^2.
\]
The supremum over \(\mathcal P_L\) dominates the maximum over \(P_0,P_1\).  Taking the infimum over \(a\in\mathcal T_{n,\Delta}\) proves both lower bounds.  Finally, choose
\[
 c=\min\left\{\frac{3\kappa}{8},\frac{3\kappa^2}{16}\right\}>0,
 \qquad
 C=1+\max\{C_1,C_2,c\}.
\]
These constants are finite, satisfy \(c<C\), and depend only on the permitted class constants.  This proves every assertion uniformly over the stated ranges of \(n\) and \(\Delta\).

semantic_closure.name: Unknown-design bivariate bounded-outcome point-anchored boundary class
semantic_closure.construction:
\(\mathcal P_L\) is the set of one-unit laws \(P\) such that \(P_X(\mathcal D)=1\); for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(H\in(0,1/2]\), \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\); \((\mathcal X_{0,P},\mathcal X_{1,P})\) is a known Borel partition of \(\mathcal D\) and \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\) almost surely; \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\) almost surely; for each \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the conditional law of \(Y(t)\) given \(X=x\) is supported on \([0,1]\) and has mean \(\mu_t(x)\); and the point-anchored envelope
\[
 |\mu_t(x)-\theta_t|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
\]
holds for every \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every side-\(t\) point \(x\) of radius at most \(1/2\), where \(\theta_t\in[0,1]\) and \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\).  The sampling condition \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) is imposed on the sample and is not a member property of a one-unit law.

semantic_closure.construction:
For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), let \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{T_i=t,Q_\Delta(R_i)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Define
\[
 \widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}=
 \begin{cases}
 \Pi_{[0,1]}\!\left(S_{t,n,\Delta}/N_{t,n,\Delta}\right),&N_{t,n,\Delta}>0,\\
 1/2,&N_{t,n,\Delta}=0,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 H_{n,\Delta}=\Delta\left\lceil n^{-1/4}/\Delta\right\rceil,
\]
where \(\Pi_{[0,1]}\) is Euclidean clipping, and set \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}=\widehat m_{1,n,\Delta}-\widehat m_{0,n,\Delta}\).

semantic_closure.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  For every event \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) with \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\), the conditional outcome is supported on \([0,1]\) and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid B]=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
In particular, put \(A_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Then \(A_t=\{T=t,R<H_{n,\Delta}\}\), its probability \(q_t\) is at least \(c_0H_{n,\Delta}^2>0\), and, with
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t],
\]
one has \(|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|\leq LH_{n,\Delta}\) and \(N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\).  Conditional on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\geq1\), list the selected outcomes in increasing sample-index order as \(Y_{t,1}^{\star},\ldots,Y_{t,k}^{\star}\).  They are independent and identically distributed, supported on \([0,1]\), and have common mean \(\nu_t\); moreover,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{j=1}^kY_{t,j}^{\star},\qquad
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right]=\nu_t,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right)\leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
Outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass, the conditional sum need not be binomial.
semantic_closure.justification: This lemma supplies the conditional selected-sample law, random-count likelihood, bounded variance, and explicit point-anchor bias under the unknown bivariate design.
semantic_closure.gap: Exact-radius and scalar-running-variable analyses do not state the conditional iid selected-outcome law after retaining only side and quantized radius under an unknown bivariate design.
semantic_closure.consumer: The count and selected-average laws are the implementation contract for the bin-aware estimator and total conditional-Hoeffding interval.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Let \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) satisfy \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:sharp\text{-}boundary\text{-}assignment}\), \(T\) is a measurable function of \(X\), and the definitions of \(R\) and \(Q_\Delta\) make \(Q_\Delta(R)\) a measurable function of \(X\).  Thus \(B\in\sigma(X)\), up to a \(P\)-null set.  By \(\mathrm{ass:consistency}\), \(Y=Y(t)\) on \(B\).  The bounded-outcome conditional-mean condition \(\mathrm{ass:radial\text{-}bernoulli}\) then gives \(0\leq Y\leq1\) on \(B\), and iterated conditioning gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid B]
 =\mathbb E_P[Y(t)\mid B]
 =\mathbb E_P\!\left[\mathbb E_P[Y(t)\mid X]\,\middle|\,B\right]
 =\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
This proves the first assertion without imposing a Bernoulli law on a general member of \(\mathcal P_L\).

Put \(h=h_n\), \(H=H_{n,\Delta}\), and \(K=K_{n,\Delta}\).  By definition, \(H=K\Delta\) with integer \(K\geq1\).  Hence, pointwise for \(R\in[0,1]\),
\[
 Q_\Delta(R)<H
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \Delta\lfloor R/\Delta\rfloor<K\Delta
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 R<K\Delta=H.
\]
Moreover, \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\leq1/4\), and the ceiling inequality imply
\[
 0<h=n^{-1/4}\leq\frac14,
 \qquad
 h\leq H=\Delta\left\lceil\frac h\Delta\right\rceil<h+\Delta\leq\frac12.
\]
Thus the local-mass condition applies to
\[
 A_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)<H\}=\{T=t,R<H\}
\]
and yields
\[
 q_t:=\mathbb P_P(A_t)\geq c_0H^2>0.
\]
The first part, with \(B=A_t\), defines
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A_t]
      =\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t].
\]
On \(A_t\), one has \(R<H\leq1/2\).  The point-anchor envelope \(\mathrm{ass:radial\text{-}lipschitz}\), the identity \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\), and the triangle inequality for conditional expectation give
\[
 \left|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)\right|
 =\left|\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)-\theta_t\mid A_t]\right|
 \leq\mathbb E_P[|\mu_t(X)-\theta_t|\mid A_t]
 \leq L\mathbb E_P[R\mid A_t]
 \leq LH.
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:boundary\text{-}anchor\text{-}uniqueness}\) ensures that the declared anchor is a well-defined functional of \(P\).

For sample unit \(i\), set \(I_i=\mathbf1\{A_{t,i}\}\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) makes the pairs \((I_i,Y_i)\) independent and identically distributed, with \(\mathbb P_P(I_i=1)=q_t\).  Therefore
\[
 N_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{i=1}^n I_i\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t).
\]
Fix \(k\geq1\) with \(\mathbb P_P(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k)>0\).  Conditional on any indicator configuration \((I_1,\ldots,I_n)\) having exactly \(k\) ones, independence across units implies that the outcomes at the selected indices are independent, while identical sampling makes every selected outcome have law \(\mathcal L_P(Y\mid A_t)\).  This product law is the same for every such indicator configuration.  Mixing over the configurations conditional on their sum therefore leaves that product law unchanged.  Hence \(Y_{t,1}^{\star},\ldots,Y_{t,k}^{\star}\) are conditionally independent and identically distributed, are supported on \([0,1]\), and have common mean \(\nu_t\).  By the definition of the localized outcome sum,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{j=1}^kY_{t,j}^{\star}
 \quad\text{on }\{N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\},
\]
and consequently
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right]=\nu_t.
\]
Finally, if \(0\leq W\leq1\) and \(\mathbb E[W]=\nu\), then \(W^2\leq W\), so
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(W)=\mathbb E[W^2]-\nu^2
 \leq\nu-\nu^2\leq\frac14.
\]
Conditional independence now gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right)
 =\frac1{k^2}\sum_{j=1}^k
 \operatorname{Var}_P(Y_{t,j}^{\star}\mid N_{t,n,\Delta}=k)
 \leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
This proves all assertions.

semantic_closure.statement:
For every \(n\ge256\) and \(0<\Delta\le\Delta_0\), the handle \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}\) admits one same-class baseline--alternative realization with both difficulties present.  Specifically, put \(\kappa=c_L/4\), \(b_h(r)=(h_n-r)_+\),
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf 1\{0\le r<\Delta\},
 \qquad
 g_{n,\Delta}(r)=\kappa\{b_h(r)+a_\Delta(r)\}.
\]
There are \(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta}\in\mathcal P_L\) with \(m_{0,0}=m_{0,1}=1/2\), \(m_{1,0}=1/2\), and \(m_{1,1}=1/2+g_{n,\Delta}\), for which
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\!\left(\mathcal L_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n),
 \mathcal L_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n)\right)
 \le\frac14<1-2\alpha
\]
and
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)
 =\kappa(h_n+\Delta).
\]
semantic_closure.justification: One legal uniform-half-disc pair combines the sampling bump and exact first-bin alias while charging released divergence only for the sampling component.
semantic_closure.gap: No cited comparator supplies a single pair for the latent annular experiment with both order-\(n^{-1/4}\) and order-\(\Delta\) displacement.
semantic_closure.consumer: The pair is the common lower certificate for absolute risk, squared risk, and honest expected interval length over the point-anchored superclass.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\geq256\) and \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and abbreviate \(h=h_n\) and \(\kappa=c_L/4\).  Then \(h\leq1/4\) and \(\Delta\leq1/4\).  From \(\phi(u)=1-3u+2u^2\), one has \(\phi(1)=0\) and \(\sup_{u\in[0,1]}|\phi'(u)|=3\).  Consequently
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf1\{0\leq r<\Delta\}
\]
is \(3\)-Lipschitz, satisfies \(a_\Delta(0)=\Delta\), and, by \(\mathrm{lem:first\text{-}bin\text{-}alias}\), has the exact null moment
\[
 \int_0^\Delta ra_\Delta(r)\,dr
 =\Delta^3\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du=0.
\]
The function \(b_h(r)=(h-r)_+\) is \(1\)-Lipschitz and satisfies \(b_h(0)=h\).  Therefore
\[
 g_{n,\Delta}(r)=\kappa\{b_h(r)+a_\Delta(r)\}
\]
is \(4\kappa=c_L\leq L\)-Lipschitz, and
\[
 |g_{n,\Delta}(r)|
 \leq\kappa(h+\Delta)
 \leq\frac{c_L}{8}
 \leq\frac1{128}<\frac12.
\]

Take the laws named in \(\mathrm{def:joint\text{-}lower\text{-}handle}\), and abbreviate them by \(P_0=P_{0,n,\Delta}\) and \(P_1=P_{1,n,\Delta}\).  Under \(P_0\), choose both anchors equal to \(1/2\).  Under \(P_1\), choose \(\theta_0=1/2\) and
\[
 \theta_1=\frac12+g_{n,\Delta}(0)
 =\frac12+\kappa(h+\Delta).
\]
The range bound puts every conditional Bernoulli mean in \([0,1]\).  For every treated point of radius \(r\leq1/2\),
\[
 |\mu_1(x)-\theta_1|
 =|g_{n,\Delta}(r)-g_{n,\Delta}(0)|
 \leq c_Lr\leq Lr,
\]
and all other point-anchor deviations vanish.  The construction supplies the known sharp half-plane partition, consistency, and conditional Bernoulli laws.  Uniform polar integration gives, for each side and every \(0<H\leq1/2\),
\[
 \mathbb P(T=t,R<H)=\frac{H^2}{2}\geq c_0H^2,
\]
because \(c_0\leq1/2\).  Thus both laws belong to the bounded-outcome superclass \(\mathcal P_L\).  Their target separation is
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)
 =g_{n,\Delta}(0)=\kappa(h+\Delta).
\]

It remains to bound the distance between the released laws.  Partition \([0,1]\) into the positive-mass quantizer cells
\[
 A_j=[j\Delta,\min\{(j+1)\Delta,1\}),
\]
with the immaterial radius-one endpoint assigned arbitrarily, and define
\[
 w_j=\int_{A_j}r\,dr,
 \qquad
 \overline b_j=w_j^{-1}\int_{A_j}rb_h(r)\,dr.
\]
For the uniform disc cut into half-discs,
\[
 w_j=\mathbb P(T=1,Q_\Delta(R)=j\Delta).
\]
The alias term is supported in the complete first cell and has zero \(r\)-weighted integral there; it vanishes in all other cells.  Hence, cell by cell, the treated conditional success probability is \(1/2\) under \(P_0\) and \(1/2+\kappa\overline b_j\) under \(P_1\), while all control cells agree.

Let \(Q_k=\mathcal L_{P_k}(Z_\Delta)\).  Direct summation over the two Bernoulli outcomes gives
\[
 \chi^2\!\left(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2+x),
                    \operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\right)=4x^2.
\]
Consequently, Jensen's inequality within each quantizer cell yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 d:=\chi^2(Q_1,Q_0)
 &=4\kappa^2\sum_jw_j\overline b_j^2\\
 &\leq4\kappa^2\int_0^1rb_h(r)^2\,dr\\
 &=4\kappa^2\int_0^h r(h-r)^2\,dr
 =\frac{\kappa^2h^4}{3}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) makes the likelihood ratio a product.  Expanding its second moment and using \(nh^4=1\) gives
\[
 1+\chi^2(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 =(1+d)^n
 \leq\exp(nd)
 \leq\exp(\kappa^2/3).
\]
Since \(\kappa=c_L/4\leq1/64\), the elementary inequality \(e^x-1\leq2x\) for \(0\leq x\leq1\) implies
\[
 \chi^2(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \leq\frac{2\kappa^2}{3}.
\]
Writing \(M=dQ_1^{\otimes n}/dQ_0^{\otimes n}\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 =\frac12\mathbb E_{Q_0^{\otimes n}}|M-1|
 \leq\frac12\{\mathbb E_{Q_0^{\otimes n}}(M-1)^2\}^{1/2}
 \leq\frac{\kappa}{\sqrt6}<\frac14.
\]
Finally, \(0<\alpha<1/4\) implies \(1/4<1-2\alpha\).  This proves the same-class realization, separation, and asserted total-variation bound.
