semantic_closure.name: Unknown-design bivariate bounded-outcome point-anchored boundary class
semantic_closure.construction:
\(\mathcal P_L\) is the set of one-unit laws \(P\) such that \(P_X(\mathcal D)=1\); for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(H\in(0,1/2]\), \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\); \((\mathcal X_{0,P},\mathcal X_{1,P})\) is a known Borel partition of \(\mathcal D\) and \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\) almost surely; \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\) almost surely; for each \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the conditional law of \(Y(t)\) given \(X=x\) is supported on \([0,1]\) and has mean \(\mu_t(x)\); and the point-anchored envelope
\[
 |\mu_t(x)-\theta_t|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
\]
holds for every \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every side-\(t\) point \(x\) of radius at most \(1/2\), where \(\theta_t\in[0,1]\) and \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\).  The sampling condition \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) is imposed on the sample and is not a member property of a one-unit law.

semantic_closure.name: Rounded-radius observation experiment
semantic_closure.construction: \(\mathcal E_{n,\Delta}(P)=\mathcal L_P(Z_{\Delta,1},\ldots,Z_{\Delta,n}),\quad Z_{\Delta,i}=(Y_i,T_i,\Delta\lfloor R_i/\Delta\rfloor)\). The observation \(\sigma\)-field is exactly \(\sigma(Z_{\Delta,1},\ldots,Z_{\Delta,n})\); it excludes \(X_i\), angle, and raw \(R_i\).

semantic_closure.name: Total bin-aware local-constant estimator
semantic_closure.construction:
For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), let \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{T_i=t,Q_\Delta(R_i)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Define
\[
 \widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}=
 \begin{cases}
 \Pi_{[0,1]}\!\left(S_{t,n,\Delta}/N_{t,n,\Delta}\right),&N_{t,n,\Delta}>0,\\
 1/2,&N_{t,n,\Delta}=0,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 H_{n,\Delta}=\Delta\left\lceil n^{-1/4}/\Delta\right\rceil,
\]
where \(\Pi_{[0,1]}\) is Euclidean clipping, and set \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}=\widehat m_{1,n,\Delta}-\widehat m_{0,n,\Delta}\).

semantic_closure.name: Rounded-radius minimax risks
semantic_closure.construction: \(\mathfrak R^{(1)}_{n,\Delta}=\inf_{\widetilde\tau\in\mathcal T_{n,\Delta}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P|\widetilde\tau-\tau_P(b)|\) and \(\mathfrak R^{(2)}_{n,\Delta}=\inf_{\widetilde\tau\in\mathcal T_{n,\Delta}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau_P(b))^2]\).

semantic_closure.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  For every event \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) with \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\), the conditional outcome is supported on \([0,1]\) and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid B]=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
In particular, put \(A_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Then \(A_t=\{T=t,R<H_{n,\Delta}\}\), its probability \(q_t\) is at least \(c_0H_{n,\Delta}^2>0\), and, with
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t],
\]
one has \(|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|\leq LH_{n,\Delta}\) and \(N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\).  Conditional on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\geq1\), list the selected outcomes in increasing sample-index order as \(Y_{t,1}^{\star},\ldots,Y_{t,k}^{\star}\).  They are independent and identically distributed, supported on \([0,1]\), and have common mean \(\nu_t\); moreover,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{j=1}^kY_{t,j}^{\star},\qquad
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right]=\nu_t,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right)\leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
Outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass, the conditional sum need not be binomial.
semantic_closure.justification: This lemma supplies the conditional selected-sample law, random-count likelihood, bounded variance, and explicit point-anchor bias under the unknown bivariate design.
semantic_closure.gap: Exact-radius and scalar-running-variable analyses do not state the conditional iid selected-outcome law after retaining only side and quantized radius under an unknown bivariate design.
semantic_closure.consumer: The count and selected-average laws are the implementation contract for the bin-aware estimator and total conditional-Hoeffding interval.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Let \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) satisfy \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:sharp\text{-}boundary\text{-}assignment}\), \(T\) is a measurable function of \(X\), and the definitions of \(R\) and \(Q_\Delta\) make \(Q_\Delta(R)\) a measurable function of \(X\).  Thus \(B\in\sigma(X)\), up to a \(P\)-null set.  By \(\mathrm{ass:consistency}\), \(Y=Y(t)\) on \(B\).  The bounded-outcome conditional-mean condition \(\mathrm{ass:radial\text{-}bernoulli}\) then gives \(0\leq Y\leq1\) on \(B\), and iterated conditioning gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid B]
 =\mathbb E_P[Y(t)\mid B]
 =\mathbb E_P\!\left[\mathbb E_P[Y(t)\mid X]\,\middle|\,B\right]
 =\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
This proves the first assertion without imposing a Bernoulli law on a general member of \(\mathcal P_L\).

Put \(h=h_n\), \(H=H_{n,\Delta}\), and \(K=K_{n,\Delta}\).  By definition, \(H=K\Delta\) with integer \(K\geq1\).  Hence, pointwise for \(R\in[0,1]\),
\[
 Q_\Delta(R)<H
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \Delta\lfloor R/\Delta\rfloor<K\Delta
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 R<K\Delta=H.
\]
Moreover, \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\leq1/4\), and the ceiling inequality imply
\[
 0<h=n^{-1/4}\leq\frac14,
 \qquad
 h\leq H=\Delta\left\lceil\frac h\Delta\right\rceil<h+\Delta\leq\frac12.
\]
Thus the local-mass condition applies to
\[
 A_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)<H\}=\{T=t,R<H\}
\]
and yields
\[
 q_t:=\mathbb P_P(A_t)\geq c_0H^2>0.
\]
The first part, with \(B=A_t\), defines
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A_t]
      =\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t].
\]
On \(A_t\), one has \(R<H\leq1/2\).  The point-anchor envelope \(\mathrm{ass:radial\text{-}lipschitz}\), the identity \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\), and the triangle inequality for conditional expectation give
\[
 \left|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)\right|
 =\left|\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)-\theta_t\mid A_t]\right|
 \leq\mathbb E_P[|\mu_t(X)-\theta_t|\mid A_t]
 \leq L\mathbb E_P[R\mid A_t]
 \leq LH.
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:boundary\text{-}anchor\text{-}uniqueness}\) ensures that the declared anchor is a well-defined functional of \(P\).

For sample unit \(i\), set \(I_i=\mathbf1\{A_{t,i}\}\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) makes the pairs \((I_i,Y_i)\) independent and identically distributed, with \(\mathbb P_P(I_i=1)=q_t\).  Therefore
\[
 N_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{i=1}^n I_i\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t).
\]
Fix \(k\geq1\) with \(\mathbb P_P(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k)>0\).  Conditional on any indicator configuration \((I_1,\ldots,I_n)\) having exactly \(k\) ones, independence across units implies that the outcomes at the selected indices are independent, while identical sampling makes every selected outcome have law \(\mathcal L_P(Y\mid A_t)\).  This product law is the same for every such indicator configuration.  Mixing over the configurations conditional on their sum therefore leaves that product law unchanged.  Hence \(Y_{t,1}^{\star},\ldots,Y_{t,k}^{\star}\) are conditionally independent and identically distributed, are supported on \([0,1]\), and have common mean \(\nu_t\).  By the definition of the localized outcome sum,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{j=1}^kY_{t,j}^{\star}
 \quad\text{on }\{N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\},
\]
and consequently
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right]=\nu_t.
\]
Finally, if \(0\leq W\leq1\) and \(\mathbb E[W]=\nu\), then \(W^2\leq W\), so
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(W)=\mathbb E[W^2]-\nu^2
 \leq\nu-\nu^2\leq\frac14.
\]
Conditional independence now gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right)
 =\frac1{k^2}\sum_{j=1}^k
 \operatorname{Var}_P(Y_{t,j}^{\star}\mid N_{t,n,\Delta}=k)
 \leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
This proves all assertions.

semantic_closure.statement:
For every \(n\ge256\) and \(0<\Delta\le\Delta_0\), the handle \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}\) admits one same-class baseline--alternative realization with both difficulties present.  Specifically, put \(\kappa=c_L/4\), \(b_h(r)=(h_n-r)_+\),
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf 1\{0\le r<\Delta\},
 \qquad
 g_{n,\Delta}(r)=\kappa\{b_h(r)+a_\Delta(r)\}.
\]
There are \(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta}\in\mathcal P_L\) with \(m_{0,0}=m_{0,1}=1/2\), \(m_{1,0}=1/2\), and \(m_{1,1}=1/2+g_{n,\Delta}\), for which
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\!\left(\mathcal L_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n),
 \mathcal L_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n)\right)
 \le\frac14<1-2\alpha
\]
and
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)
 =\kappa(h_n+\Delta).
\]
semantic_closure.justification: One legal uniform-half-disc pair combines the sampling bump and exact first-bin alias while charging released divergence only for the sampling component.
semantic_closure.gap: No cited comparator supplies a single pair for the latent annular experiment with both order-\(n^{-1/4}\) and order-\(\Delta\) displacement.
semantic_closure.consumer: The pair is the common lower certificate for absolute risk, squared risk, and honest expected interval length over the point-anchored superclass.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\geq256\) and \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and abbreviate \(h=h_n\) and \(\kappa=c_L/4\).  Then \(h\leq1/4\) and \(\Delta\leq1/4\).  From \(\phi(u)=1-3u+2u^2\), one has \(\phi(1)=0\) and \(\sup_{u\in[0,1]}|\phi'(u)|=3\).  Consequently
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf1\{0\leq r<\Delta\}
\]
is \(3\)-Lipschitz, satisfies \(a_\Delta(0)=\Delta\), and, by \(\mathrm{lem:first\text{-}bin\text{-}alias}\), has the exact null moment
\[
 \int_0^\Delta ra_\Delta(r)\,dr
 =\Delta^3\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du=0.
\]
The function \(b_h(r)=(h-r)_+\) is \(1\)-Lipschitz and satisfies \(b_h(0)=h\).  Therefore
\[
 g_{n,\Delta}(r)=\kappa\{b_h(r)+a_\Delta(r)\}
\]
is \(4\kappa=c_L\leq L\)-Lipschitz, and
\[
 |g_{n,\Delta}(r)|
 \leq\kappa(h+\Delta)
 \leq\frac{c_L}{8}
 \leq\frac1{128}<\frac12.
\]

Take the laws named in \(\mathrm{def:joint\text{-}lower\text{-}handle}\), and abbreviate them by \(P_0=P_{0,n,\Delta}\) and \(P_1=P_{1,n,\Delta}\).  Under \(P_0\), choose both anchors equal to \(1/2\).  Under \(P_1\), choose \(\theta_0=1/2\) and
\[
 \theta_1=\frac12+g_{n,\Delta}(0)
 =\frac12+\kappa(h+\Delta).
\]
The range bound puts every conditional Bernoulli mean in \([0,1]\).  For every treated point of radius \(r\leq1/2\),
\[
 |\mu_1(x)-\theta_1|
 =|g_{n,\Delta}(r)-g_{n,\Delta}(0)|
 \leq c_Lr\leq Lr,
\]
and all other point-anchor deviations vanish.  The construction supplies the known sharp half-plane partition, consistency, and conditional Bernoulli laws.  Uniform polar integration gives, for each side and every \(0<H\leq1/2\),
\[
 \mathbb P(T=t,R<H)=\frac{H^2}{2}\geq c_0H^2,
\]
because \(c_0\leq1/2\).  Thus both laws belong to the bounded-outcome superclass \(\mathcal P_L\).  Their target separation is
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)
 =g_{n,\Delta}(0)=\kappa(h+\Delta).
\]

It remains to bound the distance between the released laws.  Partition \([0,1]\) into the positive-mass quantizer cells
\[
 A_j=[j\Delta,\min\{(j+1)\Delta,1\}),
\]
with the immaterial radius-one endpoint assigned arbitrarily, and define
\[
 w_j=\int_{A_j}r\,dr,
 \qquad
 \overline b_j=w_j^{-1}\int_{A_j}rb_h(r)\,dr.
\]
For the uniform disc cut into half-discs,
\[
 w_j=\mathbb P(T=1,Q_\Delta(R)=j\Delta).
\]
The alias term is supported in the complete first cell and has zero \(r\)-weighted integral there; it vanishes in all other cells.  Hence, cell by cell, the treated conditional success probability is \(1/2\) under \(P_0\) and \(1/2+\kappa\overline b_j\) under \(P_1\), while all control cells agree.

Let \(Q_k=\mathcal L_{P_k}(Z_\Delta)\).  Direct summation over the two Bernoulli outcomes gives
\[
 \chi^2\!\left(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2+x),
                    \operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\right)=4x^2.
\]
Consequently, Jensen's inequality within each quantizer cell yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 d:=\chi^2(Q_1,Q_0)
 &=4\kappa^2\sum_jw_j\overline b_j^2\\
 &\leq4\kappa^2\int_0^1rb_h(r)^2\,dr\\
 &=4\kappa^2\int_0^h r(h-r)^2\,dr
 =\frac{\kappa^2h^4}{3}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) makes the likelihood ratio a product.  Expanding its second moment and using \(nh^4=1\) gives
\[
 1+\chi^2(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 =(1+d)^n
 \leq\exp(nd)
 \leq\exp(\kappa^2/3).
\]
Since \(\kappa=c_L/4\leq1/64\), the elementary inequality \(e^x-1\leq2x\) for \(0\leq x\leq1\) implies
\[
 \chi^2(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \leq\frac{2\kappa^2}{3}.
\]
Writing \(M=dQ_1^{\otimes n}/dQ_0^{\otimes n}\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 =\frac12\mathbb E_{Q_0^{\otimes n}}|M-1|
 \leq\frac12\{\mathbb E_{Q_0^{\otimes n}}(M-1)^2\}^{1/2}
 \leq\frac{\kappa}{\sqrt6}<\frac14.
\]
Finally, \(0<\alpha<1/4\) implies \(1/4<1-2\alpha\).  This proves the same-class realization, separation, and asserted total-variation bound.

semantic_closure.statement:
For every \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), every release law \(Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta\) has positive probability on each first-bin side event \(\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)=0\}\), and
\[
 2c_L\Delta\leq\omega_\Delta\leq4L\Delta.
\]
Consequently, the full-data causal functional \(\tau_P(b)\) is generally not point identified from a fixed-\(\Delta\) released law, and its worst release-fiber diameter is of order \(\Delta\).
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Fix \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\) and \(Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta\).  By \(\mathrm{def:released\text{-}identified\text{-}set}\), there is at least one \(P\in\mathcal P_L\) such that \(Q=\mathcal L_P(Z_\Delta)\).  For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), define the released first-bin side event
\[
 B_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)=0\}.
\]
Because \(R\in[0,1]\) and \(Q_\Delta(r)=\Delta\lfloor r/\Delta\rfloor\),
\[
 B_t=\{T=t,0\leq R<\Delta\}=\{T=t,R<\Delta\}.
\]
The inequalities \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\leq1/4<1/2\) permit use of the two-sided local-mass condition in \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}disc\text{-}design}\) and \(\mathrm{def:half\text{-}disc\text{-}class}\), giving
\[
 Q(B_t)=\mathbb P_P(B_t)\geq c_0\Delta^2>0.
\]
This proves the first assertion for every attainable \(Q\).

Since \(B_t\) has positive \(Q\)-probability, the released law determines the number
\[
 \zeta_t(Q)=\mathbb E_Q[Y\mid B_t]
 =\frac{\int y\mathbf1_{B_t}(y,t',q)\,dQ(y,t',q)}{Q(B_t)}.
\]
For any \(P'\in\mathcal P_L\) satisfying \(\mathcal L_{P'}(Z_\Delta)=Q\), the general event assertion of \(\mathrm{lem:conditional\text{-}local\text{-}binomial\text{-}law}\), which follows from sharp assignment, consistency, and the declared conditional means, yields
\[
 \zeta_t(Q)=\mathbb E_{P'}[Y\mid B_t]
 =\mathbb E_{P'}[\mu_t(X)\mid B_t].
\]
On \(B_t\), one has \(R<\Delta\leq1/2\).  The point-anchor envelope in \(\mathrm{ass:radial\text{-}lipschitz}\) therefore gives, using conditional Jensen's inequality for the absolute value,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\zeta_t(Q)-\theta_{t,P'}|
 &\leq \mathbb E_{P'}[|\mu_t(X)-\theta_{t,P'}|\mid B_t]\\
 &\leq L\mathbb E_{P'}[R\mid B_t]
 \leq L\Delta.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The anchor \(\theta_{t,P'}\) is unambiguous by \(\mathrm{lem:boundary\text{-}anchor\text{-}uniqueness}\).  Hence, if \(P',P''\in\mathcal P_L\) induce the same \(Q\), then
\[
 |\theta_{t,P'}-\theta_{t,P''}|
 \leq |\theta_{t,P'}-\zeta_t(Q)|+|\zeta_t(Q)-\theta_{t,P''}|
 \leq2L\Delta.
\]
Using \(\tau_P(b)=\theta_{1,P}-\theta_{0,P}\) and the triangle inequality,
\[
 |\tau_{P'}(b)-\tau_{P''}(b)|
 \leq |\theta_{1,P'}-\theta_{1,P''}|+|\theta_{0,P'}-\theta_{0,P''}|
 \leq4L\Delta.
\]
Taking the supremum first over all \(P',P''\) in a fixed release fiber and then over \(Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta\), as prescribed by \(\mathrm{def:released\text{-}identified\text{-}set}\), proves \(\omega_\Delta\leq4L\Delta\).

For the converse, \(\mathrm{lem:first\text{-}bin\text{-}alias}\) supplies \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta},P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}\in\mathcal P_L\) having a common released law, say \(Q^{\mathrm{alias}}\), and satisfying
\[
 \tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}}(b)
 -\tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}}(b)=2c_L\Delta.
\]
Both displayed target values consequently belong to \(I_\Delta(Q^{\mathrm{alias}})\), so
\[
 \omega_\Delta
 \geq\operatorname{diam}I_\Delta(Q^{\mathrm{alias}})
 \geq2c_L\Delta.
\]
Here \(c_L>0\) by its definition and \(L\geq1\).  Thus a fixed-width release has at least one fiber containing two distinct values of the structural causal target, which proves general failure of point identification.  The two positive finite constants \(2c_L\) and \(4L\) give the asserted order in \(\Delta\).

semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  Suppose that \(a,a'\in[0,1]\) both satisfy the point-anchor envelope in the statement.  For every \(H\in(0,1/2]\), the local-mass condition in \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}disc\text{-}design}\) gives
\[
 \mathbb P_P(T=t,R<H)\geq c_0H^2>0.
\]
Each candidate envelope holds outside a \(P_X\)-null subset of the side-\(t\), radius-at-most-\(1/2\) region.  Removing the union of these two null sets from \(\{T=t,R<H\}\) leaves a set of positive probability.  At every \(x\) in that remaining set,
\[
 |a-a'|
 \leq |a-\mu_t(x)|+|\mu_t(x)-a'|
 \leq 2L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
 <2LH.
\]
The left side is deterministic, and this inequality holds for every \(H\in(0,1/2]\).  Letting \(H\downarrow0\) yields \(|a-a'|=0\), hence \(a=a'\).  Existence of the declared anchor \(\theta_t\) is a member condition in \(\mathrm{def:half\text{-}disc\text{-}class}\), so the anchor is unique.  Consequently \(\theta_t\), and therefore \(\tau_P(b)=\theta_1-\theta_0\), is a well-defined functional of \(P\).

semantic_closure.name: Embedded uniform-half-disc joint lower handle
semantic_closure.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}=(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta})\) denote the following pair.  Under both laws, \(X\) is uniform on \(\mathcal D\), \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assignment is sharp, and the control mean is \(1/2\).  Under \(P_{0,n,\Delta}\) the treated mean is \(1/2\); under \(P_{1,n,\Delta}\) it is
\[
 \frac12+\frac{c_L}{4}\left\{(h_n-\lVert x-b\rVert_2)_+
 +\Delta\phi\!\left(\frac{\lVert x-b\rVert_2}{\Delta}\right)
 \mathbf1\{\lVert x-b\rVert_2<\Delta\}\right\}.
\]
Given \(X\), the potential outcomes are conditionally independent Bernoulli variables with these means, and \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\).

semantic_closure.statement: For every \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), \(\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du=0\), both \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}\) and \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}\) belong to \(\mathcal P_L\), their released one-unit laws of \(Z_\Delta\) are identical, and \(\tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}}(b)=2c_L\Delta\).

semantic_closure.proof_tex:
The polynomial in \(\mathrm{def:first\text{-}bin\text{-}alias}\) is
\[
 \phi(u)=1-3u+2u^2,
 \qquad
 \int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du
 =\int_0^1(u-3u^2+2u^3)\,du
 =\frac12-1+\frac12=0.
\]
Furthermore, \(\phi(1)=0\), \(|\phi(u)|\leq1\) for \(u\in[0,1]\), and \(\phi'(u)=-3+4u\), whence \(\sup_{u\in[0,1]}|\phi'(u)|=3\).  Define
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf1\{0\leq r<\Delta\}.
\]
The two pieces agree at \(r=\Delta\), and the derivative bound shows that \(a_\Delta\) is continuous and \(3\)-Lipschitz on \([0,1]\).  The radius map is \(1\)-Lipschitz because
\[
 \bigl|\lVert x-b\rVert_2-\lVert x'-b\rVert_2\bigr|
 \leq\lVert x-x'\rVert_2.
\]

Consider either law in \(\mathrm{def:first\text{-}bin\text{-}alias}\).  Choose the control anchor \(\theta_0=1/2\) and the treated anchor
\[
 \theta_{1,\pm}=\frac12\pm c_L\Delta
 =\frac12\pm c_La_\Delta(0).
\]
For every treated point \(x\) with radius \(r\leq1/2\),
\[
 |\mu_{1,\pm}(x)-\theta_{1,\pm}|
 =c_L|a_\Delta(r)-a_\Delta(0)|
 \leq3c_Lr\leq Lr,
\]
where the last inequality uses \(c_L\leq L/8\).  The control deviation is zero.  Also
\[
 |c_La_\Delta(r)|\leq c_L\Delta
 \leq\frac1{16}\frac14=\frac1{64},
\]
using \(c_L\leq1/16\) and \(\Delta\leq\Delta_0\leq1/4\); therefore the constructed Bernoulli means lie in \([0,1]\).

The construction supplies the known half-plane partition, sharp assignment, consistency, and conditionally Bernoulli potential outcomes, which in particular satisfy the bounded-outcome conditional-mean requirement.  Uniformity of \(X\) on the unit disc and polar integration give, for each \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(0<H\leq1/2\),
\[
 \mathbb P(T=t,R<H)
 =\frac1\pi\int_{\Theta_t}\int_0^H r\,dr\,d\vartheta
 =\frac{H^2}{2}
 \geq c_0H^2,
 \qquad |\Theta_t|=\pi,
\]
by \(c_0\leq1/2\).  Thus both laws belong to \(\mathcal P_L\).  This is membership through an embedded uniform-half-disc subclass, not an assertion of design-wide orthogonality.

The distribution of \((T,Q_\Delta(R))\) is common to the two signs.  Within the treated first bin, the difference of their joint success masses is
\[
 \frac1\pi\int_{\Theta_1}\int_0^\Delta
 2c_L\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)r\,dr\,d\vartheta
 =2c_L\Delta^3\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du=0.
\]
Outside this bin the perturbation vanishes, and every control cell is unchanged.  Because the released outcome is binary under these two constructed laws, equality of a released cell's total mass and success mass also gives equality of its failure mass.  Hence the entire one-unit laws of \(Z_\Delta=(Y,T,Q_\Delta(R))\) coincide.  Finally, \(\phi(0)=1\) and the declared boundary anchors give
\[
 \tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}}(b)=c_L\Delta,
 \qquad
 \tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}}(b)=-c_L\Delta.
\]
Their difference is \(2c_L\Delta\), as claimed.

semantic_closure.construction:
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), set \([\ell_t,u_t]=[0,1]\) when \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=0\).  When \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k>0\), put
\[
 \overline Y_t=\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k,
 \qquad

 \qquad

\]
With \(B_{n,\Delta}=LH_{n,\Delta}\), define the closed bounded interval
\[
 C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}
 =\bigl[\ell_1-u_0-2B_{n,\Delta},\ u_1-\ell_0+2B_{n,\Delta}\bigr].
\]

semantic_closure.construction:

\[

payload.justification: This corollary reads the two limiting regimes directly from the proved frontier without equating the experiment to an exact-score model.
payload.gap: An exact-score rate is only a sanity check and does not imply the coarsened radial result.
payload.consumer: Users can determine whether increasing sample size or improving release precision changes the leading error order.

payload.tldr: An analyst observes only \(Z_\Delta=(Y,T,Q_\Delta(R))\): bounded outcome, sharp-treatment side, and floor-rounded distance from one fixed boundary point; raw location, polar angle, and raw radius are unavailable.  Over an unknown-design bivariate class with two-sided quadratic local mass and sidewise point-anchored \(L\)-Lipschitz means, an observed-count bin-aligned estimator has minimax absolute-error order \(\max\{n^{-1/4},\Delta\}\) and squared-risk order \(\max\{n^{-1/4},\Delta\}^2\).  A conditional-Hoeffding interval, enlarged by explicit spatial bias and defined even at zero counts, has honest expected length of the same first order.  One uniform-half-disc Bernoulli pair combines the sampling bump with an exact first-bin alias, proving all converse rates.  The \(\Delta\) term is also a population ambiguity cost: fixed-width release fibers have worst diameter between \(2c_L\Delta\) and \(4L\Delta\).

project_justification.gap: Exact-coordinate boundary methods do not cover a release field that removes both angle and within-bin radius, while ordinary discrete or rounded scalar-running-variable methods do not evaluate the radial first-bin fiber together with quadratic local mass.  The resulting causal boundary target is generally only partially identified at fixed release precision, and its sampling and resolution costs must be analyzed jointly.
project_justification.niche: The model allows an unknown score design subject only to two-sided quadratic local mass and allows general outcomes in \([0,1]\).  Radial localization has effective mass of order \(H^2\), whereas the uniform-half-disc least-favorable subclass has an exact first-bin direction orthogonal under the radial Jacobian.  These mechanisms yield the transition between \(n^{-1/4}\) sampling error and order-\(\Delta\) release ambiguity.
project_justification.fill: The note fixes the analyst's observation \(\sigma\)-field, uses observed local side counts in an explicit bin-aligned estimator, and constructs a total conditional-Hoeffding interval with sidewise Lipschitz bias enlargement.  It proves one same-class pair carrying the sampling bump and alias simultaneously, derives matching minimax absolute and squared risks and honest expected length, and quantifies the population release-fiber diameter without redefining the structural causal target.

sampling_model.design: For each \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), the latent score \(X\) is supported on the unit disc centered at \(b\).  Its distribution need not be uniform or known; each treatment side has probability at least \(c_0H^2\) inside every radius \(H\leq1/2\).
sampling_model.units: The primitive observations \((X_i,Y_i(0),Y_i(1))_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed.  The analyst receives only \((Y_i,T_i,Q_\Delta(R_i))\); neither \(X_i\), angle, nor raw \(R_i\) is released.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is assigned sharply by the known Borel side partition, \(T_i=\mathbf1\{X_i\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\), and consistency gives \(Y_i=T_iY_i(1)+(1-T_i)Y_i(0)\).
sampling_model.overlap: No propensity overlap is imposed because assignment is deterministic.  The required boundary support condition is geometric: both sides have at least \(c_0H^2\) probability within every radius \(H\leq1/2\), which also makes each first-bin side event have positive probability.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No design density or known local-bin probability is used.  The estimator divides each localized outcome sum by its observed localized side count and uses a fixed \(1/2\) fallback at zero count.  The confidence interval conditions on those observed counts, applies bounded-outcome Hoeffding tails, and adds the known point-anchor bias envelope \(LH_{n,\Delta}\) on each side.

payload.related_work: CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance motivates point-distance compression and supplies an exact-coordinate radial benchmark, but no class-inclusion or transfer claim is made: the experiment here with unknown design and quantized radius is different.  Dong2015Rounding and KolesarRothe2018Discrete are the closest scalar-score coarsening and discrete-support references; neither evaluates a two-dimensional radial release fiber with quadratic local mass.  ArmstrongKolesar2018Optimal provides general modulus perspective, and ArmstrongKolesar2020Honest motivates explicit smoothness-bias enlargement.  The present note derives its own joint least-favorable pair, release-fiber bounds, observed-count estimator, and conditional-Hoeffding coverage argument.  The uniform half-disc and Bernoulli outcomes are used only for the least-favorable subclass; Clopper--Pearson inversion, when desired, is likewise only a Bernoulli-subclass specialization.  CattaneoTitiunikYu2025Rd2d documents relevant \(\texttt{rd2d}\) workflows, but the theorem applies to a workflow or replication only after verifying that the analyst truly lacks raw coordinates, angle, and within-bin radius.
payload.interpretation: The causal estimand remains the full-data boundary contrast \(\tau_P(b)=\theta_1-\theta_0\).  At fixed \(\Delta>0\), the released population law need not determine it uniquely: \(I_\Delta(Q)\) records compatible values and \(\omega_\Delta\asymp\Delta\) measures worst release ambiguity.  Finite sampling adds the \(n^{-1/4}\) boundary-regression scale, and the proved joint pair shows that one cannot evade either cost by switching procedures.  Thus \(\Delta\leq n^{-1/4}\) is sample-limited, while \(n^{-1/4}=o(\Delta)\) is release-precision-limited.
payload.technical_internal_limitation: The upper bounds cover the full unknown-design, \([0,1]\)-bounded-outcome class, but they require the declared quadratic local-mass constant, known side partition, fixed boundary point, and point-anchored Lipschitz envelope.  The matching converse embeds a uniform half-disc with Bernoulli potential outcomes; this is a legal subclass certificate, not a claim that the main class has uniform design or Bernoulli outcomes.  The results establish rate order rather than sharp constants.  They do not cover data releases retaining raw coordinates, angle, or within-bin radius, and they do not by themselves validate every geographic-boundary workflow or establish inclusion in the exact-coordinate comparison class.
payload.honest_scope: The structural target and the observed-law functional are kept distinct: \(\tau_P(b)\) is causal, whereas \(I_\Delta(Q)\) is the set compatible with one attainable rounded release.  The main theorem gives matching minimax risk and honest expected-length orders uniformly over \(n\geq256\) and \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\); it does not claim a sharp leading constant.  Main-class inference uses conditional Hoeffding concentration for general bounded outcomes, observed random counts, explicit sidewise bias enlargement, and a total zero-count definition.  Exact binomial or Clopper--Pearson calculations are confined to the embedded Bernoulli subclass.  Applicability requires that only outcome, treatment side, and quantized radius are observed; availability of raw \(X\), polar angle, or raw \(R\) defines a different experiment.

payload.statement:
Let \(k\geq1\), and let \(W_1,\ldots,W_k\) be independent random variables satisfying \(0\leq W_j\leq1\) almost surely and \(\mathbb E[W_j]=p\) for every \(j\).  Then, for every \(r\) satisfying \(0<r<1-p\),
\[
 \mathbb P\!\left(\frac1k\sum_{j=1}^kW_j-p\geq r\right)\leq\exp(-2kr^2).
\]

source.verbatim_statement: If X₁,…,Xₙ are independent and 0≤Xᵢ≤1, then for 0<t<1−μ, Pr{X̄−μ≥t}≤e^(−2nt²).

carrier.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and suppose that \(a,a'\in[0,1]\) both satisfy the displayed point-anchor envelope.  This proof uses the shrinking-support argument.  For every \(H\in(0,1/2]\), assumption \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}disc\text{-}design}\) gives
\[
 P_X\{x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}:\lVert x-b\rVert_2<H\}
 =\mathbb P_P(T=t,R<H)\ge c_0H^2>0.
\]
The two envelope inequalities fail only on the union of two \(P_X\)-null sets.  Hence the positive-probability set above contains a point \(x_H\) at which both hold.  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:radial\text{-}lipschitz}\) and the triangle inequality then yield
\[
 |a-a'|
 \le |a-\mu_t(x_H)|+|\mu_t(x_H)-a'|
 \le 2L\lVert x_H-b\rVert_2
 <2LH.
\]
Because this inequality holds for every \(H\in(0,1/2]\), letting \(H\downarrow0\) gives \(|a-a'|=0\), hence \(a=a'\).  The member properties in \(\mathrm{def:half\text{-}disc\text{-}class}\) assert existence of the declared anchor \(\theta_t\); the argument proves its uniqueness.  Therefore \(\theta_1-\theta_0\), and thus \(\tau_P(b)\), is a well-defined functional of the full-data law rather than a choice of conditional-mean version.

target_declaration.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_L\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), there is at most one \(a\in[0,1]\) such that \(|\mu_t(x)-a|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) with \(\lVert x-b\rVert_2\leq1/2\). Consequently, the declared \(\theta_t\) and \(\tau_P(b)=\theta_1-\theta_0\) are well-defined functionals of \(P\).
target_declaration.justification: The point anchor must be a functional of the law, not an arbitrary version choice, for the boundary contrast to be a well-defined causal estimand.
target_declaration.gap: The uniqueness step is specific to combining an almost-everywhere point envelope with positive side mass at every shrinking radius.
target_declaration.consumer: The identified set, risk, and coverage statements use the uniquely determined boundary anchor contrast.

semantic_closure.name: Unknown-design bivariate bounded-outcome point-anchored boundary class
semantic_closure.construction:
\(\mathcal P_L\) is the set of one-unit laws \(P\) such that \(P_X(\mathcal D)=1\); for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(H\in(0,1/2]\), \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\); \((\mathcal X_{0,P},\mathcal X_{1,P})\) is a known Borel partition of \(\mathcal D\) and \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\) almost surely; \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\) almost surely; for each \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the conditional law of \(Y(t)\) given \(X=x\) is supported on \([0,1]\) and has mean \(\mu_t(x)\); and the point-anchored envelope
\[
 |\mu_t(x)-\theta_t|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
\]
holds for every \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every side-\(t\) point \(x\) of radius at most \(1/2\), where \(\theta_t\in[0,1]\) and \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\).  The sampling condition \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) is imposed on the sample and is not a member property of a one-unit law.

semantic_closure.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  For every event \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) with \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\), the conditional outcome is supported on \([0,1]\) and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid B]=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
In particular, put \(A_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Then \(A_t=\{T=t,R<H_{n,\Delta}\}\), its probability \(q_t\) is at least \(c_0H_{n,\Delta}^2>0\), and, with
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t],
\]
one has \(|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|\leq LH_{n,\Delta}\) and \(N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\).  Conditional on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\geq1\), list the selected outcomes in increasing sample-index order as \(Y_{t,1}^{\star},\ldots,Y_{t,k}^{\star}\).  They are independent and identically distributed, supported on \([0,1]\), and have common mean \(\nu_t\); moreover,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{j=1}^kY_{t,j}^{\star},\qquad
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right]=\nu_t,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right)\leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
Outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass, the conditional sum need not be binomial.
semantic_closure.justification: The lemma supplies the conditional iid selected-outcome law, random-count distribution, bounded variance, and point-anchor bias for the bounded-outcome superclass.
semantic_closure.gap: The selected sum is not binomial outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass; the usable general statement is conditional iid bounded sampling with a common mean.
semantic_closure.consumer: The local estimator uses its variance bound, and the total interval uses its conditional product law.

semantic_closure.statement: For every \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), \(\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du=0\), both \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}\) and \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}\) belong to \(\mathcal P_L\), their released one-unit laws of \(Z_\Delta\) are identical, and \(\tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}}(b)=2c_L\Delta\).
semantic_closure.justification: This certifies an exact order-\(\Delta\) alias in a legal uniform-half-disc subclass of the unknown-design point-anchored model, without asserting design-wide orthogonality.
semantic_closure.gap: Scalar rounding results do not furnish the radial-Jacobian null direction for a release that hides bivariate coordinates within annuli.
semantic_closure.consumer: Data stewards using released radial bins can see that no sample size removes the first-bin resolution floor.

semantic_closure.statement:
For every \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), every release law \(Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta\) has positive probability on each first-bin side event \(\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)=0\}\), and
\[
 2c_L\Delta\leq\omega_\Delta\leq4L\Delta.
\]
Consequently, the full-data causal functional \(\tau_P(b)\) is generally not point identified from a fixed-\(\Delta\) released law, and its worst release-fiber diameter is of order \(\Delta\).
semantic_closure.justification: This is the headline partial-identification result: it quantifies the population ambiguity created by the rounded release before finite-sample error is considered.
semantic_closure.gap: DaveziesLeBarbanchon2017 restores scalar-RD identification using auxiliary discrepancy data, and GerardRokkanenRothe2020 sharply bounds effects under latent manipulation types; neither evaluates the release fiber generated by a known annular map with no auxiliary true-score sample over the stated bivariate point-anchored class.
semantic_closure.consumer: It tells analysts and data stewards how much fixed-precision radial release alone can vary the latent point boundary effect before sampling error is considered.

semantic_closure.statement:
For every \(n\ge256\) and \(0<\Delta\le\Delta_0\), the handle \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}\) admits one same-class baseline--alternative realization with both difficulties present.  Specifically, put \(\kappa=c_L/4\), \(b_h(r)=(h_n-r)_+\),
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf 1\{0\le r<\Delta\},
 \qquad
 g_{n,\Delta}(r)=\kappa\{b_h(r)+a_\Delta(r)\}.
\]
There are \(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta}\in\mathcal P_L\) with \(m_{0,0}=m_{0,1}=1/2\), \(m_{1,0}=1/2\), and \(m_{1,1}=1/2+g_{n,\Delta}\), for which
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\!\left(\mathcal L_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n),
 \mathcal L_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n)\right)
 \le\frac14<1-2\alpha
\]
and
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)
 =\kappa(h_n+\Delta).
\]
semantic_closure.justification: One uniform-half-disc Bernoulli pair combines a localized sampling bump and the exact first-bin alias while charging released divergence only for the sampling component.
semantic_closure.gap: No cited comparator supplies this single pair for the latent-annular experiment with both order-\(n^{-1/4}\) and order-\(\Delta\) target displacement.
semantic_closure.consumer: The pair is the common same-class lower certificate for absolute risk, squared risk, and honest expected interval length.

semantic_closure.name: Embedded uniform-half-disc exact first-bin alias pair
semantic_closure.construction:
For each sign, construct \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{\pm,\Delta}\) by drawing \(X\) uniformly on \(\mathcal D\), taking \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assigning \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\), and drawing conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes given \(X\) with
\[
 \mu_{0,\pm}(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mu_{1,\pm}(x)=\frac12\pm c_L\Delta\phi\!\left(\frac{\lVert x-b\rVert_2}{\Delta}\right)
 \mathbf1\{\lVert x-b\rVert_2<\Delta\}.
\]
Finally set \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\), where \(\phi(u)=(1-u)(1-2u)\) and \(c_L=\min\{L/8,1/16\}\).

semantic_closure.name: P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{\pm,\Delta}
semantic_closure.def: The two bivariate laws constructed in \(\mathrm{def:first\text{-}bin\text{-}alias}\).
semantic_closure.role: exact nonidentification witness in a least-favorable subclass

semantic_closure.name: Z_\Delta
semantic_closure.def: \(Z_\Delta=(Y,T,Q_\Delta(R))\); neither \(X\), the polar angle, nor raw \(R\) is observed.

semantic_closure.name: Released-law identified set and maximal fiber diameter
semantic_closure.construction:
For \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), let
\[
 \mathcal Q_\Delta=\{\mathcal L_P(Z_\Delta):P\in\mathcal P_L\}.
\]
For every \(Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta\), define the nonempty release-fiber identified set and its diameter by
\[
 I_\Delta(Q)=\{\tau_P(b):P\in\mathcal P_L\ \text{and}\ \mathcal L_P(Z_\Delta)=Q\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{diam} I_\Delta(Q)=\sup_{a,a'\in I_\Delta(Q)}|a-a'|.
\]
The maximal population ambiguity of the rounded release is
\[
 \omega_\Delta=\sup_{Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta}\operatorname{diam} I_\Delta(Q).
\]

semantic_closure.space: sets of probability laws on the released observation space
semantic_closure.def: The image \(\{\mathcal L_P(Z_\Delta):P\in\mathcal P_L\}\) defined in \(\mathrm{def:released\text{-}identified\text{-}set}\).

semantic_closure.name: \omega_\Delta
semantic_closure.def: The supremum over attainable released laws of the diameter of \(I_\Delta\), defined in \(\mathrm{def:released\text{-}identified\text{-}set}\).

semantic_closure.name: Embedded uniform-half-disc joint lower handle
semantic_closure.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}=(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta})\) denote the following pair.  Under both laws, \(X\) is uniform on \(\mathcal D\), \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assignment is sharp, and the control mean is \(1/2\).  Under \(P_{0,n,\Delta}\) the treated mean is \(1/2\); under \(P_{1,n,\Delta}\) it is
\[
 \frac12+\frac{c_L}{4}\left\{(h_n-\lVert x-b\rVert_2)_+
 +\Delta\phi\!\left(\frac{\lVert x-b\rVert_2}{\Delta}\right)
 \mathbf1\{\lVert x-b\rVert_2<\Delta\}\right\}.
\]
Given \(X\), the potential outcomes are conditionally independent Bernoulli variables with these means, and \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\).

semantic_closure.def: The explicit embedded uniform-half-disc pair constructed in \(\mathrm{def:joint\text{-}lower\text{-}handle}\).

semantic_closure.name: Total bin-aware local-constant estimator
semantic_closure.construction:
For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), let \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{T_i=t,Q_\Delta(R_i)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Define
\[
 \widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}=
 \begin{cases}
 \Pi_{[0,1]}\!\left(S_{t,n,\Delta}/N_{t,n,\Delta}\right),&N_{t,n,\Delta}>0,\\
 1/2,&N_{t,n,\Delta}=0,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 H_{n,\Delta}=\Delta\left\lceil n^{-1/4}/\Delta\right\rceil,
\]
where \(\Pi_{[0,1]}\) is Euclidean clipping, and set \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}=\widehat m_{1,n,\Delta}-\widehat m_{0,n,\Delta}\).

carrier.proof_tex:
Fix the objects in the statement.  First use conditioning and consistency.  If \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\), \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\), and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\), then \(B\in\sigma(X)\), because both \(T\) and \(Q_\Delta(R)\) are functions of \(X\) by \(\mathrm{ass:sharp\text{-}boundary\text{-}assignment}\) and \(\mathrm{def:rounded\text{-}experiment}\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:consistency}\) gives \(Y=Y(t)\) on \(B\).  The conditional-mean member property in \(\mathrm{def:half\text{-}disc\text{-}class}\) therefore implies
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mathbf1_B]
 =\mathbb E_P[Y(t)\mathbf1_B]
 =\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mathbf1_B].
\]
Division by the positive number \(\mathbb P_P(B)\) proves
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid B]=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
The same member property and consistency show that \(Y\mid B\) is supported on \([0,1]\).

Next use bin alignment.  Write \(H_{n,\Delta}=K_{n,\Delta}\Delta\), where \(K_{n,\Delta}=\lceil h_n/\Delta\rceil\) is a positive integer.  For every \(r\in[0,1]\),
\[
 Q_\Delta(r)<H_{n,\Delta}
 \iff \Delta\lfloor r/\Delta\rfloor<K_{n,\Delta}\Delta
 \iff r<K_{n,\Delta}\Delta.
\]
Thus \(A_t=\{T=t,R<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Moreover,
\[
 h_n\le H_{n,\Delta}<h_n+\Delta\le\frac12,
\]
because \(n\ge256\) gives \(h_n=n^{-1/4}\le1/4\) and \(\Delta\le\Delta_0\le1/4\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}disc\text{-}design}\) consequently gives
\[
 q_t:=\mathbb P_P(A_t)\ge c_0H_{n,\Delta}^2>0.
\]
By the first part and \(\mathrm{ass:radial\text{-}lipschitz}\),
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A_t]
 =\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t],
 \qquad
 |\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|
 \le \mathbb E_P[|\mu_t(X)-\theta_t|\mid A_t]
 \le LH_{n,\Delta},
\]
where \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\) and its uniqueness is supplied by \(\mathrm{lem:boundary\text{-}anchor\text{-}uniqueness}\).

Finally use the conditional thinning law, derived directly from \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\).  The indicators \(\mathbf1_{A_t}(X_i)\) are independent Bernoulli variables of common success probability \(q_t\), so
\[
 N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t).
\]
Conditional on any specified set of \(k\) successful indices, independence makes the corresponding outcomes independent with common law \(\mathcal L_P(Y\mid A_t)\); this conditional law does not depend on the specified index set.  Mixing over the index sets conditional on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\) therefore leaves the ordered selected outcomes independent and identically distributed with that same law.  Hence, for \(k\ge1\),
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{j=1}^kY_{t,j}^{\star},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right]=\nu_t.
\]
If \(W\in[0,1]\) has mean \(p\), then \(W^2\le W\), and therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(W)=\mathbb E[W^2]-p^2\le p(1-p)\le\frac14.
\]
Independence of the selected outcomes now gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right)
 =\frac1{k^2}\sum_{j=1}^k\operatorname{Var}_P(Y_{t,j}^{\star}\mid N_{t,n,\Delta}=k)
 \le\frac1{4k}.
\]
Nothing in this argument makes a general bounded outcome Bernoulli, which proves the final qualification.

target_declaration.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  For every event \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) with \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\), the conditional outcome is supported on \([0,1]\) and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid B]=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
In particular, put \(A_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Then \(A_t=\{T=t,R<H_{n,\Delta}\}\), its probability \(q_t\) is at least \(c_0H_{n,\Delta}^2>0\), and, with
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t],
\]
one has \(|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|\leq LH_{n,\Delta}\) and \(N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\).  Conditional on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\geq1\), list the selected outcomes in increasing sample-index order as \(Y_{t,1}^{\star},\ldots,Y_{t,k}^{\star}\).  They are independent and identically distributed, supported on \([0,1]\), and have common mean \(\nu_t\); moreover,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{j=1}^kY_{t,j}^{\star},\qquad
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right]=\nu_t,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right)\leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
Outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass, the conditional sum need not be binomial.
target_declaration.justification: The lemma supplies the conditional iid selected-outcome law, random-count distribution, bounded variance, and point-anchor bias for the bounded-outcome superclass.
target_declaration.gap: The selected sum is not binomial outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass; the usable general statement is conditional iid bounded sampling with a common mean.
target_declaration.consumer: The local estimator uses its variance bound, and the total interval uses its conditional product law.

semantic_closure.condition: \(Y=T Y(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\) almost surely under \(P\).
\((X_i,Y_i(0),Y_i(1))_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed under \(P\).
For the fixed class constant \(c_0\in(0,1/2]\), \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\) for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and every \(H\in(0,1/2]\).

standard.name: sharp assignment across a known bivariate boundary

semantic_closure.condition:
For every \(t\in\{0,1\}\), for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) satisfying \(\lVert x-b\rVert_2\leq1/2\),
\[
 |\mu_t(x)-\theta_t|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2.
\]

semantic_closure.name: Unknown-design bivariate bounded-outcome point-anchored boundary class
semantic_closure.construction:
\(\mathcal P_L\) is the set of one-unit laws \(P\) such that \(P_X(\mathcal D)=1\); for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(H\in(0,1/2]\), \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\); \((\mathcal X_{0,P},\mathcal X_{1,P})\) is a known Borel partition of \(\mathcal D\) and \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\) almost surely; \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\) almost surely; for each \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the conditional law of \(Y(t)\) given \(X=x\) is supported on \([0,1]\) and has mean \(\mu_t(x)\); and the point-anchored envelope
\[
 |\mu_t(x)-\theta_t|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
\]
holds for every \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every side-\(t\) point \(x\) of radius at most \(1/2\), where \(\theta_t\in[0,1]\) and \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\).  The sampling condition \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) is imposed on the sample and is not a member property of a one-unit law.

semantic_closure.name: Rounded-radius observation experiment
semantic_closure.construction: \(\mathcal E_{n,\Delta}(P)=\mathcal L_P(Z_{\Delta,1},\ldots,Z_{\Delta,n}),\quad Z_{\Delta,i}=(Y_i,T_i,\Delta\lfloor R_i/\Delta\rfloor)\). The observation \(\sigma\)-field is exactly \(\sigma(Z_{\Delta,1},\ldots,Z_{\Delta,n})\); it excludes \(X_i\), angle, and raw \(R_i\).

semantic_closure.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_L\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), there is at most one \(a\in[0,1]\) such that \(|\mu_t(x)-a|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) with \(\lVert x-b\rVert_2\leq1/2\). Consequently, the declared \(\theta_t\) and \(\tau_P(b)=\theta_1-\theta_0\) are well-defined functionals of \(P\).
semantic_closure.justification: The point anchor must be a functional of the law, not an arbitrary version choice, for the boundary contrast to be a well-defined causal estimand.
semantic_closure.gap: The uniqueness step is specific to combining an almost-everywhere point envelope with positive side mass at every shrinking radius.
semantic_closure.consumer: The identified set, risk, and coverage statements use the uniquely determined boundary anchor contrast.

semantic_closure.statement:
For every \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), every release law \(Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta\) has positive probability on each first-bin side event \(\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)=0\}\), and
\[
 2c_L\Delta\leq\omega_\Delta\leq4L\Delta.
\]
Consequently, the full-data causal functional \(\tau_P(b)\) is generally not point identified from a fixed-\(\Delta\) released law, and its worst release-fiber diameter is of order \(\Delta\).
semantic_closure.justification: This is the headline partial-identification result: it quantifies the population ambiguity created by the rounded release before finite-sample error is considered.
semantic_closure.gap: DaveziesLeBarbanchon2017 restores scalar-RD identification using auxiliary discrepancy data, and GerardRokkanenRothe2020 sharply bounds effects under latent manipulation types; neither evaluates the release fiber generated by a known annular map with no auxiliary true-score sample over the stated bivariate point-anchored class.
semantic_closure.consumer: It tells analysts and data stewards how much fixed-precision radial release alone can vary the latent point boundary effect before sampling error is considered.

semantic_closure.statement:
For every \(n\ge256\) and \(0<\Delta\le\Delta_0\), the handle \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}\) admits one same-class baseline--alternative realization with both difficulties present.  Specifically, put \(\kappa=c_L/4\), \(b_h(r)=(h_n-r)_+\),
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf 1\{0\le r<\Delta\},
 \qquad
 g_{n,\Delta}(r)=\kappa\{b_h(r)+a_\Delta(r)\}.
\]
There are \(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta}\in\mathcal P_L\) with \(m_{0,0}=m_{0,1}=1/2\), \(m_{1,0}=1/2\), and \(m_{1,1}=1/2+g_{n,\Delta}\), for which
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\!\left(\mathcal L_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n),
 \mathcal L_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n)\right)
 \le\frac14<1-2\alpha
\]
and
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)
 =\kappa(h_n+\Delta).
\]
semantic_closure.justification: One uniform-half-disc Bernoulli pair combines a localized sampling bump and the exact first-bin alias while charging released divergence only for the sampling component.
semantic_closure.gap: No cited comparator supplies this single pair for the latent-annular experiment with both order-\(n^{-1/4}\) and order-\(\Delta\) target displacement.
semantic_closure.consumer: The pair is the common same-class lower certificate for absolute risk, squared risk, and honest expected interval length.

semantic_closure.name: Embedded uniform-half-disc exact first-bin alias pair
semantic_closure.construction:
For each sign, construct \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{\pm,\Delta}\) by drawing \(X\) uniformly on \(\mathcal D\), taking \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assigning \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\), and drawing conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes given \(X\) with
\[
 \mu_{0,\pm}(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mu_{1,\pm}(x)=\frac12\pm c_L\Delta\phi\!\left(\frac{\lVert x-b\rVert_2}{\Delta}\right)
 \mathbf1\{\lVert x-b\rVert_2<\Delta\}.
\]
Finally set \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\), where \(\phi(u)=(1-u)(1-2u)\) and \(c_L=\min\{L/8,1/16\}\).

semantic_closure.name: Released-law identified set and maximal fiber diameter
semantic_closure.construction:
For \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), let
\[
 \mathcal Q_\Delta=\{\mathcal L_P(Z_\Delta):P\in\mathcal P_L\}.
\]
For every \(Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta\), define the nonempty release-fiber identified set and its diameter by
\[
 I_\Delta(Q)=\{\tau_P(b):P\in\mathcal P_L\ \text{and}\ \mathcal L_P(Z_\Delta)=Q\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{diam} I_\Delta(Q)=\sup_{a,a'\in I_\Delta(Q)}|a-a'|.
\]
The maximal population ambiguity of the rounded release is
\[
 \omega_\Delta=\sup_{Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta}\operatorname{diam} I_\Delta(Q).
\]

carrier.proof_tex:
The algebraic null direction is exact:
\[
 \int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du
 =\int_0^1(u-3u^2+2u^3)\,du
 =\frac12-1+\frac12=0.
\]
We next verify class membership rather than taking it from the construction.  Under either law in \(\mathrm{def:first\text{-}bin\text{-}alias}\), uniformity on the unit disc and the half-disc assignment imply, for \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(0<H\le1/2\),
\[
 \mathbb P(T=t,R<H)=\frac{H^2}{2}\ge c_0H^2,
\]
where the last inequality uses \(c_0\le1/2\).  Sharp assignment and consistency hold by construction.  On \([0,1]\), \(|\phi(u)|\le1\); hence, since \(c_L\Delta\le(1/16)(1/4)=1/64\), all constructed Bernoulli means lie in \([1/4,3/4]\subset[0,1]\).

For the treated side the boundary anchor is
\[
 \theta_{1,\pm}=\mu_{1,\pm}(b)=\frac12\pm c_L\Delta,
\]
and the control anchor is \(1/2\).  If \(0\le r<\Delta\), then
\[
 |\phi(r/\Delta)-1|
 =3(r/\Delta)-2(r/\Delta)^2
 \le3r/\Delta,
\]
whereas if \(r\ge\Delta\), the perturbation is zero and \(\Delta\le r\).  Thus at every side point of radius at most \(1/2\),
\[
 |\mu_{1,\pm}(x)-\theta_{1,\pm}|
 \le3c_Lr\le Lr,
\]
using \(c_L\le L/8\); the control envelope is immediate.  This verifies every member property of \(\mathrm{def:half\text{-}disc\text{-}class}\), so both laws belong to \(\mathcal P_L\).

It remains to prove observational equivalence.  The laws of \((T,Q_\Delta(R))\) agree.  Conditional on the treated first-bin event, the uniform-disc radial density is \(2r/\Delta^2\) on \([0,\Delta)\).  The two conditional Bernoulli success probabilities after mixing over the latent radius are therefore
\[
 \frac12\pm c_L\Delta\int_0^\Delta\frac{2r}{\Delta^2}\phi(r/\Delta)\,dr
 =\frac12\pm2c_L\Delta\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du
 =\frac12.
\]
A mixture of Bernoulli variables is Bernoulli with its averaged success probability.  On the control side and on every other radial bin the conditional outcome laws already coincide.  Hence the full released one-unit laws of \(Z_\Delta\) are identical.  Finally,
\[
 \tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}}(b)
 -\tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}}(b)
 =\theta_{1,+}-\theta_{1,-}=2c_L\Delta,
\]
because the control anchors agree.

target_declaration.statement: For every \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), \(\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du=0\), both \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}\) and \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}\) belong to \(\mathcal P_L\), their released one-unit laws of \(Z_\Delta\) are identical, and \(\tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}}(b)=2c_L\Delta\).
target_declaration.justification: This certifies an exact order-\(\Delta\) alias in a legal uniform-half-disc subclass of the unknown-design point-anchored model, without asserting design-wide orthogonality.
target_declaration.gap: Scalar rounding results do not furnish the radial-Jacobian null direction for a release that hides bivariate coordinates within annuli.
target_declaration.consumer: Data stewards using released radial bins can see that no sample size removes the first-bin resolution floor.

semantic_closure.name: Unknown-design bivariate bounded-outcome point-anchored boundary class
semantic_closure.construction:
\(\mathcal P_L\) is the set of one-unit laws \(P\) such that \(P_X(\mathcal D)=1\); for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(H\in(0,1/2]\), \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\); \((\mathcal X_{0,P},\mathcal X_{1,P})\) is a known Borel partition of \(\mathcal D\) and \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\) almost surely; \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\) almost surely; for each \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the conditional law of \(Y(t)\) given \(X=x\) is supported on \([0,1]\) and has mean \(\mu_t(x)\); and the point-anchored envelope
\[
 |\mu_t(x)-\theta_t|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
\]
holds for every \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every side-\(t\) point \(x\) of radius at most \(1/2\), where \(\theta_t\in[0,1]\) and \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\).  The sampling condition \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) is imposed on the sample and is not a member property of a one-unit law.

The observation \(\sigma\)-field is exactly \(\sigma(Z_{\Delta,1},\ldots,Z_{\Delta,n})\); it excludes \(X_i\), angle, and raw \(R_i\).

semantic_closure.name: Embedded uniform-half-disc exact first-bin alias pair
semantic_closure.construction:
For each sign, construct \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{\pm,\Delta}\) by drawing \(X\) uniformly on \(\mathcal D\), taking \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assigning \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\), and drawing conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes given \(X\) with
\[
 \mu_{0,\pm}(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mu_{1,\pm}(x)=\frac12\pm c_L\Delta\phi\!\left(\frac{\lVert x-b\rVert_2}{\Delta}\right)
 \mathbf1\{\lVert x-b\rVert_2<\Delta\}.
\]
Finally set \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\), where \(\phi(u)=(1-u)(1-2u)\) and \(c_L=\min\{L/8,1/16\}\).

semantic_closure.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  For every event \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) with \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\), the conditional outcome is supported on \([0,1]\) and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid B]=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
In particular, put \(A_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Then \(A_t=\{T=t,R<H_{n,\Delta}\}\), its probability \(q_t\) is at least \(c_0H_{n,\Delta}^2>0\), and, with
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t],
\]
one has \(|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|\leq LH_{n,\Delta}\) and \(N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\).  Conditional on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\geq1\), list the selected outcomes in increasing sample-index order as \(Y_{t,1}^{\star},\ldots,Y_{t,k}^{\star}\).  They are independent and identically distributed, supported on \([0,1]\), and have common mean \(\nu_t\); moreover,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{j=1}^kY_{t,j}^{\star},\qquad
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right]=\nu_t,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right)\leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
Outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass, the conditional sum need not be binomial.
semantic_closure.justification: The lemma supplies the conditional iid selected-outcome law, random-count distribution, bounded variance, and point-anchor bias for the bounded-outcome superclass.
semantic_closure.gap: The selected sum is not binomial outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass; the usable general statement is conditional iid bounded sampling with a common mean.
semantic_closure.consumer: The local estimator uses its variance bound, and the total interval uses its conditional product law.

semantic_closure.statement:
For every \(n\ge256\) and \(0<\Delta\le\Delta_0\), the handle \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}\) admits one same-class baseline--alternative realization with both difficulties present.  Specifically, put \(\kappa=c_L/4\), \(b_h(r)=(h_n-r)_+\),
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf 1\{0\le r<\Delta\},
 \qquad
 g_{n,\Delta}(r)=\kappa\{b_h(r)+a_\Delta(r)\}.
\]
There are \(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta}\in\mathcal P_L\) with \(m_{0,0}=m_{0,1}=1/2\), \(m_{1,0}=1/2\), and \(m_{1,1}=1/2+g_{n,\Delta}\), for which
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\!\left(\mathcal L_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n),
 \mathcal L_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n)\right)
 \le\frac14<1-2\alpha
\]
and
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)
 =\kappa(h_n+\Delta).
\]
semantic_closure.justification: One uniform-half-disc Bernoulli pair combines a localized sampling bump and the exact first-bin alias while charging released divergence only for the sampling component.
semantic_closure.gap: No cited comparator supplies this single pair for the latent-annular experiment with both order-\(n^{-1/4}\) and order-\(\Delta\) target displacement.
semantic_closure.consumer: The pair is the common same-class lower certificate for absolute risk, squared risk, and honest expected interval length.

semantic_closure.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}=(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta})\) denote the following pair.  Under both laws, \(X\) is uniform on \(\mathcal D\), \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assignment is sharp, and the control mean is \(1/2\).  Under \(P_{0,n,\Delta}\) the treated mean is \(1/2\); under \(P_{1,n,\Delta}\) it is
\[
 \frac12+\frac{c_L}{4}\left\{(h_n-\lVert x-b\rVert_2)_+
 +\Delta\phi\!\left(\frac{\lVert x-b\rVert_2}{\Delta}\right)
 \mathbf1\{\lVert x-b\rVert_2<\Delta\}\right\}.
\]
Given \(X\), the potential outcomes are conditionally independent Bernoulli variables with these means, and \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\).

semantic_closure.name: Total bin-aware local-constant estimator
semantic_closure.construction:
For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), let \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{T_i=t,Q_\Delta(R_i)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Define
\[
 \widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}=
 \begin{cases}
 \Pi_{[0,1]}\!\left(S_{t,n,\Delta}/N_{t,n,\Delta}\right),&N_{t,n,\Delta}>0,\\
 1/2,&N_{t,n,\Delta}=0,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 H_{n,\Delta}=\Delta\left\lceil n^{-1/4}/\Delta\right\rceil,
\]
where \(\Pi_{[0,1]}\) is Euclidean clipping, and set \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}=\widehat m_{1,n,\Delta}-\widehat m_{0,n,\Delta}\).

semantic_closure.name: Bias-enlarged conditional-Hoeffding interval
semantic_closure.construction:
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), set \([\ell_t,u_t]=[0,1]\) when \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=0\).  When \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k>0\), put
\[
 \overline Y_t=\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k,
 \qquad
 r_{k,\alpha}=\sqrt{\frac{\log(4/\alpha)}{2k}},
 \qquad
 [\ell_t,u_t]=\bigl[\max\{0,\overline Y_t-r_{k,\alpha}\},\min\{1,\overline Y_t+r_{k,\alpha}\}\bigr].
\]
With \(B_{n,\Delta}=LH_{n,\Delta}\), define the closed bounded interval
\[
 C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}
 =\bigl[\ell_1-u_0-2B_{n,\Delta},\ u_1-\ell_0+2B_{n,\Delta}\bigr].
\]

semantic_closure.statement:

carrier.proof_tex:
Fix \(0<\Delta\le\Delta_0\) and \(Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta\).  By \(\mathrm{def:released\text{-}identified\text{-}set}\), choose any compatible \(P\in\mathcal P_L\) with \(\mathcal L_P(Z_\Delta)=Q\).  For
\[
 B_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)=0\}=\{T=t,R<\Delta\},
\]
assumption \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}disc\text{-}design}\), together with \(\Delta\le\Delta_0\le1/4\), gives
\[
 Q(B_t)=\mathbb P_P(B_t)\ge c_0\Delta^2>0.
\]
Thus the observable first-bin conditional means
\[
 \eta_t(Q):=\mathbb E_Q[Y\mid B_t]
\]
are well defined.  The conditional-mean identity in \(\mathrm{lem:conditional\text{-}local\text{-}binomial\text{-}law}\), which follows from sharp assignment and consistency, and the point-anchor envelope give
\[
 |\eta_t(Q)-\theta_t(P)|
 =\left|\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)-\theta_t(P)\mid B_t]\right|
 \le L\mathbb E_P[R\mid B_t]
 \le L\Delta.
\]
Consequently every compatible anchor satisfies the computable outer restriction
\[
 \theta_t(P)\in[\underline\theta_t(Q),\overline\theta_t(Q)],
 \quad
 \underline\theta_t(Q)=\max\{0,\eta_t(Q)-L\Delta\},
 \quad
 \overline\theta_t(Q)=\min\{1,\eta_t(Q)+L\Delta\}.
\]
In particular, this proves the release-law-specific outer bound
\[
 I_\Delta(Q)\subseteq
 [\underline\theta_1(Q)-\overline\theta_0(Q),
   \overline\theta_1(Q)-\underline\theta_0(Q)].
\]
For any two laws \(P,P'\) in the same release fiber, the same observable \(\eta_t(Q)\) appears in both inequalities, so
\[
 |\theta_t(P)-\theta_t(P')|\le2L\Delta
\]
and therefore
\[
 |\tau_P(b)-\tau_{P'}(b)|
 \le |\theta_1(P)-\theta_1(P')|+|\theta_0(P)-\theta_0(P')|
 \le4L\Delta.
\]
Taking first the diameter of each fiber and then the supremum over \(Q\) proves \(\omega_\Delta\le4L\Delta\).  Conversely, \(\mathrm{lem:first\text{-}bin\text{-}alias}\) supplies two members of \(\mathcal P_L\) with the same released law and target separation \(2c_L\Delta\).  Their common release law is an element of \(\mathcal Q_\Delta\), hence
\[
 \omega_\Delta\ge2c_L\Delta.
\]
Because \(c_L>0\) and \(\Delta>0\), this fiber is non-singleton.  The conclusion is therefore partial identification of the full-data causal target from the released law, not a redefinition of that target.

target_declaration.statement:
For every \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), every release law \(Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta\) has positive probability on each first-bin side event \(\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)=0\}\), and
\[
 2c_L\Delta\leq\omega_\Delta\leq4L\Delta.
\]
Consequently, the full-data causal functional \(\tau_P(b)\) is generally not point identified from a fixed-\(\Delta\) released law, and its worst release-fiber diameter is of order \(\Delta\).
target_declaration.justification: This is the headline partial-identification result: it quantifies the population ambiguity created by the rounded release before finite-sample error is considered.
target_declaration.gap: DaveziesLeBarbanchon2017 restores scalar-RD identification using auxiliary discrepancy data, and GerardRokkanenRothe2020 sharply bounds effects under latent manipulation types; neither evaluates the release fiber generated by a known annular map with no auxiliary true-score sample over the stated bivariate point-anchored class.
target_declaration.consumer: It tells analysts and data stewards how much fixed-precision radial release alone can vary the latent point boundary effect before sampling error is considered.

semantic_closure.name: Unknown-design bivariate bounded-outcome point-anchored boundary class
semantic_closure.construction:
\(\mathcal P_L\) is the set of one-unit laws \(P\) such that \(P_X(\mathcal D)=1\); for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(H\in(0,1/2]\), \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\); \((\mathcal X_{0,P},\mathcal X_{1,P})\) is a known Borel partition of \(\mathcal D\) and \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\) almost surely; \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\) almost surely; for each \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the conditional law of \(Y(t)\) given \(X=x\) is supported on \([0,1]\) and has mean \(\mu_t(x)\); and the point-anchored envelope
\[
 |\mu_t(x)-\theta_t|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
\]
holds for every \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every side-\(t\) point \(x\) of radius at most \(1/2\), where \(\theta_t\in[0,1]\) and \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\).  The sampling condition \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) is imposed on the sample and is not a member property of a one-unit law.

semantic_closure.construction: \(\mathcal E_{n,\Delta}(P)=\mathcal L_P(Z_{\Delta,1},\ldots,Z_{\Delta,n}),\quad Z_{\Delta,i}=(Y_i,T_i,\Delta\lfloor R_i/\Delta\rfloor)\). The observation \(\sigma\)-field is exactly \(\sigma(Z_{\Delta,1},\ldots,Z_{\Delta,n})\); it excludes \(X_i\), angle, and raw \(R_i\).

semantic_closure.name: Released-law identified set and maximal fiber diameter
semantic_closure.construction:
For \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), let
\[
 \mathcal Q_\Delta=\{\mathcal L_P(Z_\Delta):P\in\mathcal P_L\}.
\]
For every \(Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta\), define the nonempty release-fiber identified set and its diameter by
\[
 I_\Delta(Q)=\{\tau_P(b):P\in\mathcal P_L\ \text{and}\ \mathcal L_P(Z_\Delta)=Q\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{diam} I_\Delta(Q)=\sup_{a,a'\in I_\Delta(Q)}|a-a'|.
\]
The maximal population ambiguity of the rounded release is
\[
 \omega_\Delta=\sup_{Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta}\operatorname{diam} I_\Delta(Q).
\]

semantic_closure.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_L\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), there is at most one \(a\in[0,1]\) such that \(|\mu_t(x)-a|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) with \(\lVert x-b\rVert_2\leq1/2\). Consequently, the declared \(\theta_t\) and \(\tau_P(b)=\theta_1-\theta_0\) are well-defined functionals of \(P\).
semantic_closure.justification: The point anchor must be a functional of the law, not an arbitrary version choice, for the boundary contrast to be a well-defined causal estimand.
semantic_closure.gap: The uniqueness step is specific to combining an almost-everywhere point envelope with positive side mass at every shrinking radius.
semantic_closure.consumer: The identified set, risk, and coverage statements use the uniquely determined boundary anchor contrast.

semantic_closure.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  For every event \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) with \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\), the conditional outcome is supported on \([0,1]\) and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid B]=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
In particular, put \(A_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Then \(A_t=\{T=t,R<H_{n,\Delta}\}\), its probability \(q_t\) is at least \(c_0H_{n,\Delta}^2>0\), and, with
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t],
\]
one has \(|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|\leq LH_{n,\Delta}\) and \(N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\).  Conditional on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\geq1\), list the selected outcomes in increasing sample-index order as \(Y_{t,1}^{\star},\ldots,Y_{t,k}^{\star}\).  They are independent and identically distributed, supported on \([0,1]\), and have common mean \(\nu_t\); moreover,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{j=1}^kY_{t,j}^{\star},\qquad
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right]=\nu_t,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right)\leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
Outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass, the conditional sum need not be binomial.
semantic_closure.justification: The lemma supplies the conditional iid selected-outcome law, random-count distribution, bounded variance, and point-anchor bias for the bounded-outcome superclass.
semantic_closure.gap: The selected sum is not binomial outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass; the usable general statement is conditional iid bounded sampling with a common mean.
semantic_closure.consumer: The local estimator uses its variance bound, and the total interval uses its conditional product law.

semantic_closure.statement: For every \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), \(\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du=0\), both \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}\) and \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}\) belong to \(\mathcal P_L\), their released one-unit laws of \(Z_\Delta\) are identical, and \(\tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}}(b)=2c_L\Delta\).

semantic_closure.gap: Scalar rounding results do not furnish the radial-Jacobian null direction for a release that hides bivariate coordinates within annuli.
semantic_closure.consumer: Data stewards using released radial bins can see that no sample size removes the first-bin resolution floor.

\]

\]

carrier.proof_tex:
Set \(h=h_n=n^{-1/4}\), \(\kappa=c_L/4\), \(b_h(r)=(h-r)_+\), and \(a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf1\{0\le r<\Delta\}\), as in the statement.  We first verify that the pair named by \(\mathrm{def:joint\text{-}lower\text{-}handle}\) is legal.  The uniform half-disc design has
\[
 \mathbb P(T=t,R<H)=H^2/2\ge c_0H^2
\]
for \(0<H\le1/2\).  The assignment and consistency restrictions hold by construction.  Also \(|a_\Delta(r)|\le\Delta\), \(0\le b_h(r)\le h\), and \(h+\Delta\le1/2\).  Since \(\kappa\le1/64\),
\[
 |g_{n,\Delta}(r)|\le\kappa(h+\Delta)\le\frac1{128},
\]
so the alternative treated Bernoulli mean lies in \([1/4,3/4]\).

The treated alternative anchor is \(1/2+g_{n,\Delta}(0)\), where
\[
 g_{n,\Delta}(0)=\kappa(h+\Delta).
\]
The map \(b_h\) satisfies \(|b_h(r)-b_h(0)|\le r\).  Since \(\phi'(u)=-3+4u\), one has \(|a_\Delta(r)-a_\Delta(0)|\le3r\) for \(r<\Delta\), while for \(r\ge\Delta\) the same difference equals \(\Delta\le r\).  It follows that
\[
 |g_{n,\Delta}(r)-g_{n,\Delta}(0)|
 \le4\kappa r=c_Lr\le Lr.
\]
All other mean functions are constant.  Hence both laws satisfy \(\mathrm{ass:radial\text{-}lipschitz}\) and belong to \(\mathcal P_L\).

We now use an explicit chi-square calculation to show that the alias adds target separation without adding released divergence.  Let \(Q_0,Q_1\) be the one-unit released laws, define
\[
 \chi^2(Q_1,Q_0)=\int\left(\frac{dQ_1}{dQ_0}-1\right)^2dQ_0,
\]
and let \(J=Q_\Delta(R)/\Delta\).  Absolute continuity holds because every released Bernoulli cell having positive probability under \(Q_1\) has both outcome atoms positive under the baseline \(Q_0\).  Put \(p_j=Q_0(T=1,J=j)\), and, when \(p_j>0\),
\[
 \overline b_j=\mathbb E[b_h(R)\mid T=1,J=j].
\]
The radial density on a treated half-disc, before normalization by its side probability, is \(r\,dr\).  The null identity proved in \(\mathrm{lem:first\text{-}bin\text{-}alias}\) gives
\[
 \int_0^\Delta r a_\Delta(r)\,dr
 =\Delta^3\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du=0.
\]
The alias vanishes outside the first bin, so under \(Q_1\) the Bernoulli success probability conditional on \((T=1,J=j)\) differs from \(1/2\) by exactly
\[
 \delta_j=\kappa\overline b_j.
\]
Under \(Q_0\), each of the two outcome atoms in that cell has probability \(p_j/2\); under \(Q_1\), their probabilities are \(p_j(1/2+\delta_j)\) and \(p_j(1/2-\delta_j)\).  All control cells agree.  Therefore, with zero-mass cells omitted,
\[
 \chi^2(Q_1,Q_0)
 =4\sum_jp_j\delta_j^2
 \le4\kappa^2\sum_jp_j\mathbb E[b_h(R)^2\mid T=1,J=j]
 =4\kappa^2\int_0^h r(h-r)^2\,dr
 =\frac{\kappa^2h^4}{3},
\]
where the inequality is conditional Jensen and the last integral equals \(h^4/12\).

Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) makes the released sample laws \(Q_0^{\otimes n}\) and \(Q_1^{\otimes n}\).  Direct multiplication of likelihood ratios gives
\[
 1+\chi^2(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 =(1+\chi^2(Q_1,Q_0))^n
 \le\exp\!\left(\frac{n\kappa^2h^4}{3}\right)
 =\exp(\kappa^2/3).
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz applied to the likelihood ratio gives
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_0^{\otimes n},Q_1^{\otimes n})
 \le\frac12\sqrt{\chi^2(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})}.
\]
Because \(\kappa\le1/64\) and \(e^x-1\le2x\) for \(0\le x\le1\),
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_0^{\otimes n},Q_1^{\otimes n})
 \le\frac12\sqrt{2/12288}<\frac14.
\]
Since \(\alpha<1/4\), also \(1/4<1-2\alpha\).  Finally the control anchors agree, while the treated anchors differ by \(g_{n,\Delta}(0)\); hence
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)
 =\kappa(h_n+\Delta).
\]
Thus this single same-class pair contains both the sampling displacement \(\kappa h_n\) and the exactly aliased displacement \(\kappa\Delta\), while only the sampling bump enters the divergence.

target_declaration.statement:
For every \(n\ge256\) and \(0<\Delta\le\Delta_0\), the handle \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}\) admits one same-class baseline--alternative realization with both difficulties present.  Specifically, put \(\kappa=c_L/4\), \(b_h(r)=(h_n-r)_+\),
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf 1\{0\le r<\Delta\},
 \qquad
 g_{n,\Delta}(r)=\kappa\{b_h(r)+a_\Delta(r)\}.
\]
There are \(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta}\in\mathcal P_L\) with \(m_{0,0}=m_{0,1}=1/2\), \(m_{1,0}=1/2\), and \(m_{1,1}=1/2+g_{n,\Delta}\), for which
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\!\left(\mathcal L_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n),
 \mathcal L_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n)\right)
 \le\frac14<1-2\alpha
\]
and
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)
 =\kappa(h_n+\Delta).
\]
target_declaration.justification: One uniform-half-disc Bernoulli pair combines a localized sampling bump and the exact first-bin alias while charging released divergence only for the sampling component.
target_declaration.gap: No cited comparator supplies this single pair for the latent-annular experiment with both order-\(n^{-1/4}\) and order-\(\Delta\) target displacement.
target_declaration.consumer: The pair is the common same-class lower certificate for absolute risk, squared risk, and honest expected interval length.

semantic_closure.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  For every event \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) with \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\), the conditional outcome is supported on \([0,1]\) and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid B]=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
In particular, put \(A_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Then \(A_t=\{T=t,R<H_{n,\Delta}\}\), its probability \(q_t\) is at least \(c_0H_{n,\Delta}^2>0\), and, with
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t],
\]
one has \(|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|\leq LH_{n,\Delta}\) and \(N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\).  Conditional on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\geq1\), list the selected outcomes in increasing sample-index order as \(Y_{t,1}^{\star},\ldots,Y_{t,k}^{\star}\).  They are independent and identically distributed, supported on \([0,1]\), and have common mean \(\nu_t\); moreover,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{j=1}^kY_{t,j}^{\star},\qquad
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right]=\nu_t,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right)\leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
Outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass, the conditional sum need not be binomial.
semantic_closure.justification: The lemma supplies the conditional iid selected-outcome law, random-count distribution, bounded variance, and point-anchor bias for the bounded-outcome superclass.
semantic_closure.gap: The selected sum is not binomial outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass; the usable general statement is conditional iid bounded sampling with a common mean.
semantic_closure.consumer: The local estimator uses its variance bound, and the total interval uses its conditional product law.

semantic_closure.name: Embedded uniform-half-disc exact first-bin alias pair
semantic_closure.construction:
For each sign, construct \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{\pm,\Delta}\) by drawing \(X\) uniformly on \(\mathcal D\), taking \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assigning \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\), and drawing conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes given \(X\) with
\[
 \mu_{0,\pm}(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mu_{1,\pm}(x)=\frac12\pm c_L\Delta\phi\!\left(\frac{\lVert x-b\rVert_2}{\Delta}\right)
 \mathbf1\{\lVert x-b\rVert_2<\Delta\}.
\]
Finally set \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\), where \(\phi(u)=(1-u)(1-2u)\) and \(c_L=\min\{L/8,1/16\}\).

semantic_closure.name: Released-law identified set and maximal fiber diameter
semantic_closure.construction:
For \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), let
\[
 \mathcal Q_\Delta=\{\mathcal L_P(Z_\Delta):P\in\mathcal P_L\}.
\]
For every \(Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta\), define the nonempty release-fiber identified set and its diameter by
\[
 I_\Delta(Q)=\{\tau_P(b):P\in\mathcal P_L\ \text{and}\ \mathcal L_P(Z_\Delta)=Q\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{diam} I_\Delta(Q)=\sup_{a,a'\in I_\Delta(Q)}|a-a'|.
\]
The maximal population ambiguity of the rounded release is
\[
 \omega_\Delta=\sup_{Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta}\operatorname{diam} I_\Delta(Q).
\]

For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), let \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{T_i=t,Q_\Delta(R_i)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Define

 \widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}=

 \Pi_{[0,1]}\!\left(S_{t,n,\Delta}/N_{t,n,\Delta}\right),&N_{t,n,\Delta}>0,\\

 \end{cases}
 \qquad

\]
where \(\Pi_{[0,1]}\) is Euclidean clipping, and set \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}=\widehat m_{1,n,\Delta}-\widehat m_{0,n,\Delta}\).
