semantic_closure.name: Bias-enlarged conditional-Hoeffding interval
semantic_closure.construction:
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), set \([\ell_t,u_t]=[0,1]\) when \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=0\).  When \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k>0\), put
\[
 \overline Y_t=\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k,
 \qquad

\]
With \(B_{n,\Delta}=LH_{n,\Delta}\), define the closed bounded interval
\[

 =\bigl[\ell_1-u_0-2B_{n,\Delta},\ u_1-\ell_0+2B_{n,\Delta}\bigr].
\]

carrier.proof_tex:
Write \(h=h_n\), \(H=H_{n,\Delta}\), and \(\rho=\rho_{n,\Delta}\).  The ceiling definition gives
\[
 h\le H<h+\Delta\le2\rho,
 \qquad
 \frac1{\sqrt n\,H}\le\frac1{\sqrt n\,h}=h\le\rho,
 \qquad
 \frac1{nH^2}\le h^2\le\rho^2.
\]

We first prove the estimator upper bounds from the conditional selected-sample law.  Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\) and a side \(t\), and abbreviate \(N=N_{t,n,\Delta}\), \(q=q_t\), \(\nu=\nu_t\), and \(\theta=\theta_t\).  By \(\mathrm{lem:conditional\text{-}local\text{-}binomial\text{-}law}\),
\[
 q\ge c_0H^2,
 \qquad |\nu-\theta|\le LH,
 \qquad N\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q).
\]
For a binomial variable with \(q>0\), direct summation gives
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac1{N+1}\right]
 =\frac{1-(1-q)^{n+1}}{(n+1)q}
 \le\frac1{(n+1)q}.
\]
Since \(1/k\le2/(k+1)\) for \(k\ge1\), and since \((1-q)^n\le e^{-nq}\le\min\{1,(nq)^{-1}\}\),
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{N>0\}}N\right]\le\frac2{nq},
 \quad
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{N>0\}}{\sqrt N}\right]\le\sqrt{\frac2{nq}},
 \quad
 \mathbb P(N=0)\le\min\{1,(nq)^{-1}\}.
\]
Here the middle inequality is Cauchy--Schwarz.

When \(N=k>0\), the sample mean already lies in \([0,1]\), and its conditional variance is at most \(1/(4k)\).  The fixed zero-count fallback differs from \(\theta\in[0,1]\) by at most \(1/2\).  Conditional Jensen and the preceding display yield, for a numerical constant \(A\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}-\theta_t|
 \le LH+\frac12\mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{N>0\}}{\sqrt N}\right]
       +\frac12\mathbb P(N=0)
 \le LH+\frac{A}{\sqrt{nq}}
 \le LH+\frac{A}{\sqrt{c_0}\sqrt n\,H},
\]
and, using the conditional mean \(\nu\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P[(\widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}-\theta_t)^2]
 \le L^2H^2+\frac14\mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{N>0\}}N\right]
       +\frac14\mathbb P(N=0)
 \le L^2H^2+\frac{3}{4nq}
 \le L^2H^2+\frac{3}{4c_0nH^2}.
\]
The triangle inequality and \((x-y)^2\le2x^2+2y^2\), applied to the two side errors, therefore give constants \(C_1,C_2<\infty\), depending only on \(L\) and \(c_0\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P|\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}-\tau_P(b)|
 \le C_1\rho,
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}-\tau_P(b))^2]
 \le C_2\rho^2.
\]
The estimator is measurable with respect to \(Z_\Delta^n\) by \(\mathrm{def:bin\text{-}aware\text{-}estimator}\), so it belongs to \(\mathcal T_{n,\Delta}\).  Taking the infima in \(\mathrm{def:minimax\text{-}risks}\) proves both upper bounds.

For the lower bounds, use the two-point testing argument and the single pair from \(\mathrm{thm:single\text{-}joint\text{-}pair}\).  Let its target gap be
\[
 d=\kappa(h+\Delta)\ge\kappa\rho
\]
and its released-sample total variation be \(v\le1/4\).  For any released-data estimator \(\widetilde\tau\), classify it according to which of the two target values is closer.  On every classification error its absolute error is at least \(d/2\), and its squared error is at least \(d^2/4\).  The sum of the two classification-error probabilities is at least \(1-v\), by the defining variational inequality for total variation.  Hence
\[
 \max_{j\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_{P_j}|\widetilde\tau-\tau_{P_j}(b)|
 \ge\frac d4(1-v)\ge\frac{3d}{16},
\]
and
\[
 \max_{j\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_{P_j}[(\widetilde\tau-\tau_{P_j}(b))^2]
 \ge\frac{d^2}{8}(1-v)\ge\frac{3d^2}{32}.
\]
Both laws lie in \(\mathcal P_L\); taking the supremum over that class and then the infimum over \(\mathcal T_{n,\Delta}\) gives lower bounds by fixed positive multiples of \(\rho\) and \(\rho^2\).  Choosing the smaller lower constant and the larger upper constant proves the theorem.  The target throughout is the full-data functional \(\tau_P(b)\); measurability only restricts the decision rule to the released experiment.

semantic_closure.name: Unknown-design bivariate bounded-outcome point-anchored boundary class
semantic_closure.construction:
\(\mathcal P_L\) is the set of one-unit laws \(P\) such that \(P_X(\mathcal D)=1\); for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(H\in(0,1/2]\), \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\); \((\mathcal X_{0,P},\mathcal X_{1,P})\) is a known Borel partition of \(\mathcal D\) and \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\) almost surely; \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\) almost surely; for each \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the conditional law of \(Y(t)\) given \(X=x\) is supported on \([0,1]\) and has mean \(\mu_t(x)\); and the point-anchored envelope
\[
 |\mu_t(x)-\theta_t|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
\]
holds for every \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every side-\(t\) point \(x\) of radius at most \(1/2\), where \(\theta_t\in[0,1]\) and \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\).  The sampling condition \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) is imposed on the sample and is not a member property of a one-unit law.

semantic_closure.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  For every event \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) with \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\), the conditional outcome is supported on \([0,1]\) and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid B]=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
In particular, put \(A_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Then \(A_t=\{T=t,R<H_{n,\Delta}\}\), its probability \(q_t\) is at least \(c_0H_{n,\Delta}^2>0\), and, with
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t],
\]
one has \(|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|\leq LH_{n,\Delta}\) and \(N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\).  Conditional on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\geq1\), list the selected outcomes in increasing sample-index order as \(Y_{t,1}^{\star},\ldots,Y_{t,k}^{\star}\).  They are independent and identically distributed, supported on \([0,1]\), and have common mean \(\nu_t\); moreover,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{j=1}^kY_{t,j}^{\star},\qquad
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right]=\nu_t,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right)\leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
Outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass, the conditional sum need not be binomial.
semantic_closure.justification: The lemma supplies the conditional iid selected-outcome law, random-count distribution, bounded variance, and point-anchor bias for the bounded-outcome superclass.

semantic_closure.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}=(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta})\) denote the following pair.  Under both laws, \(X\) is uniform on \(\mathcal D\), \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assignment is sharp, and the control mean is \(1/2\).  Under \(P_{0,n,\Delta}\) the treated mean is \(1/2\); under \(P_{1,n,\Delta}\) it is
\[

 +\Delta\phi\!\left(\frac{\lVert x-b\rVert_2}{\Delta}\right)
 \mathbf1\{\lVert x-b\rVert_2<\Delta\}\right\}.
\]
Given \(X\), the potential outcomes are conditionally independent Bernoulli variables with these means, and \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\).

semantic_closure.construction:

\[

semantic_closure.name: Bias-enlarged conditional-Hoeffding interval
semantic_closure.construction:
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), set \([\ell_t,u_t]=[0,1]\) when \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=0\).  When \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k>0\), put
\[
 \overline Y_t=\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k,
 \qquad

 \qquad
 [\ell_t,u_t]=\bigl[\max\{0,\overline Y_t-r_{k,\alpha}\},\min\{1,\overline Y_t+r_{k,\alpha}\}\bigr].
\]
With \(B_{n,\Delta}=LH_{n,\Delta}\), define the closed bounded interval
\[
 C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}
 =\bigl[\ell_1-u_0-2B_{n,\Delta},\ u_1-\ell_0+2B_{n,\Delta}\bigr].
\]

carrier.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\).  The construction in \(\mathrm{def:total\text{-}honest\text{-}interval}\) specifies an interval for every possible count, including \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=0\), and its endpoints are measurable functions of the released counts and sums.  Its lower endpoint does not exceed its upper endpoint because their difference is the sum of two nonnegative sidewise widths and \(4LH_{n,\Delta}\).  Thus it is always a closed bounded released-data interval.

For coverage, condition on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k>0\).  By \(\mathrm{lem:conditional\text{-}local\text{-}binomial\text{-}law}\), the selected outcomes are independent, supported on \([0,1]\), and have common mean \(\nu_t\).  Put
\[
 r=r_{k,\alpha}=\sqrt{\frac{\log(4/\alpha)}{2k}}.
\]
If \(\nu_t<\ell_t\), then necessarily \(\overline Y_t-\nu_t>r\); if \(\nu_t>u_t\), then \(\nu_t-\overline Y_t>r\).  Apply \(\mathrm{lem:hoeffding\text{-}bounded\text{-}average}\) to the selected outcomes for the first event and to their complements for the second.  Whenever its displayed range condition on \(r\) is not met, the corresponding strict event is empty; otherwise the cited inequality gives
\[
 \mathbb P_P(\overline Y_t-\nu_t>r\mid N_t=k)\le e^{-2kr^2}=\frac\alpha4,
\]
and the same bound for \(\nu_t-\overline Y_t>r\).  Therefore
\[
 \mathbb P_P(\nu_t\notin[\ell_t,u_t]\mid N_t=k)\le\frac\alpha2.
\]
For \(k=0\), the interval is \([0,1]\) and contains \(\nu_t\) surely.  Averaging over the count proves sidewise failure probability at most \(\alpha/2\).

Let \(B=LH_{n,\Delta}\).  The bias conclusion of \(\mathrm{lem:conditional\text{-}local\text{-}binomial\text{-}law}\) gives \(|\nu_t-\theta_t|\le B\).  Hence, on the event that both side intervals contain their respective \(\nu_t\),
\[
 \theta_t\in[\ell_t-B,u_t+B],\qquad t=0,1,
\]
and subtraction gives
\[
 \tau_P(b)=\theta_1-\theta_0
 \in[\ell_1-u_0-2B,u_1-\ell_0+2B]
 =C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}.
\]
The union bound over the two sides proves coverage at least \(1-\alpha\), uniformly over \(P\).

For expected length, let \(w_t=u_t-\ell_t\).  Clipping can only reduce width, so
\[
 w_t\le\mathbf1\{N_t=0\}
 +2\sqrt{\frac{\log(4/\alpha)}2}\,
   \frac{\mathbf1\{N_t>0\}}{\sqrt{N_t}}.
\]
For \(N_t\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\), direct summation and \(1/k\le2/(k+1)\) for \(k\ge1\) give
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac1{N_t+1}\right]
 =\frac{1-(1-q_t)^{n+1}}{(n+1)q_t}
 \le\frac1{nq_t},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{N_t>0\}}{\sqrt{N_t}}\right]
 \le\sqrt{\frac2{nq_t}}.
\]
Also \(\mathbb P(N_t=0)=(1-q_t)^n\le\min\{1,(nq_t)^{-1}\}\le(nq_t)^{-1/2}\).  Combining these inequalities with \(q_t\ge c_0H_{n,\Delta}^2\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[w_t]
 \le \frac{C_\alpha}{\sqrt{nq_t}}
 \le\frac{C_\alpha}{\sqrt{c_0}\sqrt n\,H_{n,\Delta}}
 \le\frac{C_\alpha}{\sqrt{c_0}}h_n.
\]
Finally,
\[
 \operatorname{length}(C_{n,\Delta,\alpha})=w_1+w_0+4LH_{n,\Delta},
\]
and \(H_{n,\Delta}<h_n+\Delta\le2\rho_{n,\Delta}\).  Taking the supremum over \(P\) proves the asserted expected-length bound with a constant depending only on \(L,c_0,\alpha\), and hence admissibly on \(\Delta_0\) as well.

semantic_closure.name: Unknown-design bivariate bounded-outcome point-anchored boundary class
semantic_closure.construction:
\(\mathcal P_L\) is the set of one-unit laws \(P\) such that \(P_X(\mathcal D)=1\); for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(H\in(0,1/2]\), \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\); \((\mathcal X_{0,P},\mathcal X_{1,P})\) is a known Borel partition of \(\mathcal D\) and \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\) almost surely; \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\) almost surely; for each \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the conditional law of \(Y(t)\) given \(X=x\) is supported on \([0,1]\) and has mean \(\mu_t(x)\); and the point-anchored envelope
\[
 |\mu_t(x)-\theta_t|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
\]
holds for every \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every side-\(t\) point \(x\) of radius at most \(1/2\), where \(\theta_t\in[0,1]\) and \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\).  The sampling condition \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) is imposed on the sample and is not a member property of a one-unit law.

semantic_closure.name: Bias-enlarged conditional-Hoeffding interval
semantic_closure.construction:
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), set \([\ell_t,u_t]=[0,1]\) when \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=0\).  When \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k>0\), put
\[
 \overline Y_t=\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k,
 \qquad
 r_{k,\alpha}=\sqrt{\frac{\log(4/\alpha)}{2k}},
 \qquad
 [\ell_t,u_t]=\bigl[\max\{0,\overline Y_t-r_{k,\alpha}\},\min\{1,\overline Y_t+r_{k,\alpha}\}\bigr].
\]
With \(B_{n,\Delta}=LH_{n,\Delta}\), define the closed bounded interval
\[
 C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}
 =\bigl[\ell_1-u_0-2B_{n,\Delta},\ u_1-\ell_0+2B_{n,\Delta}\bigr].
\]

semantic_closure.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  For every event \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) with \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\), the conditional outcome is supported on \([0,1]\) and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid B]=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
In particular, put \(A_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Then \(A_t=\{T=t,R<H_{n,\Delta}\}\), its probability \(q_t\) is at least \(c_0H_{n,\Delta}^2>0\), and, with
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t],
\]
one has \(|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|\leq LH_{n,\Delta}\) and \(N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\).  Conditional on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\geq1\), list the selected outcomes in increasing sample-index order as \(Y_{t,1}^{\star},\ldots,Y_{t,k}^{\star}\).  They are independent and identically distributed, supported on \([0,1]\), and have common mean \(\nu_t\); moreover,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{j=1}^kY_{t,j}^{\star},\qquad
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right]=\nu_t,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right)\leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
Outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass, the conditional sum need not be binomial.
semantic_closure.justification: The lemma supplies the conditional iid selected-outcome law, random-count distribution, bounded variance, and point-anchor bias for the bounded-outcome superclass.
semantic_closure.gap: The selected sum is not binomial outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass; the usable general statement is conditional iid bounded sampling with a common mean.
semantic_closure.consumer: The local estimator uses its variance bound, and the total interval uses its conditional product law.

semantic_closure.statement:
Let \(k\geq1\), and let \(W_1,\ldots,W_k\) be independent random variables satisfying \(0\leq W_j\leq1\) almost surely and \(\mathbb E[W_j]=p\) for every \(j\).  Then, for every \(r\) satisfying \(0<r<1-p\),
\[
 \mathbb P\!\left(\frac1k\sum_{j=1}^kW_j-p\geq r\right)\leq\exp(-2kr^2).
\]

semantic_closure.statement:
For every \(n\ge256\) and \(0<\Delta\le\Delta_0\), the handle \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}\) admits one same-class baseline--alternative realization with both difficulties present.  Specifically, put \(\kappa=c_L/4\), \(b_h(r)=(h_n-r)_+\),
\[

 \qquad

\]
There are \(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta}\in\mathcal P_L\) with \(m_{0,0}=m_{0,1}=1/2\), \(m_{1,0}=1/2\), and \(m_{1,1}=1/2+g_{n,\Delta}\), for which

 \operatorname{TV}\!\left(\mathcal L_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n),
 \mathcal L_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n)\right)
 \le\frac14<1-2\alpha
\]
and
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)

semantic_closure.name: Released-law identified set and maximal fiber diameter
semantic_closure.construction:
For \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), let
\[
 \mathcal Q_\Delta=\{\mathcal L_P(Z_\Delta):P\in\mathcal P_L\}.
\]
For every \(Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta\), define the nonempty release-fiber identified set and its diameter by
\[
 I_\Delta(Q)=\{\tau_P(b):P\in\mathcal P_L\ \text{and}\ \mathcal L_P(Z_\Delta)=Q\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{diam} I_\Delta(Q)=\sup_{a,a'\in I_\Delta(Q)}|a-a'|.
\]
The maximal population ambiguity of the rounded release is
\[
 \omega_\Delta=\sup_{Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta}\operatorname{diam} I_\Delta(Q).
\]

For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), let \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{T_i=t,Q_\Delta(R_i)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Define
\[
 \widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}=
 \begin{cases}
 \Pi_{[0,1]}\!\left(S_{t,n,\Delta}/N_{t,n,\Delta}\right),&N_{t,n,\Delta}>0,\\
 1/2,&N_{t,n,\Delta}=0,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad

where \(\Pi_{[0,1]}\) is Euclidean clipping, and set \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}=\widehat m_{1,n,\Delta}-\widehat m_{0,n,\Delta}\).

semantic_closure.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}=(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta})\) denote the following pair.  Under both laws, \(X\) is uniform on \(\mathcal D\), \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assignment is sharp, and the control mean is \(1/2\). carrier.proof_tex:
Let \(C\in\mathcal C_{n,\Delta}(\alpha)\), and use the pair \((P_0,P_1)\) from \(\mathrm{thm:single\text{-}joint\text{-}pair}\).  Write \(\vartheta_j=\tau_{P_j}(b)\),
\[
 d=|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=\kappa(h_n+\Delta),
 \qquad
 v=\operatorname{TV}(\mathcal L_{P_0}(Z_\Delta^n),\mathcal L_{P_1}(Z_\Delta^n))\le\frac14.
\]
Honesty as defined in \(\mathrm{def:honest\text{-}class}\) implies
\[
 \mathbb P_{P_0}(\vartheta_0\in C)\ge1-\alpha,
 \qquad
 \mathbb P_{P_1}(\vartheta_1\in C)\ge1-\alpha.
\]
The total-variation inequality transfers the second event to \(P_0\):
\[
 \mathbb P_{P_0}(\vartheta_1\in C)
 \ge\mathbb P_{P_1}(\vartheta_1\in C)-v
 \ge1-\alpha-v.
\]
Therefore, under \(P_0\),
\[
 \mathbb P_{P_0}(\{\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1\}\subseteq C)
 \ge1-2\alpha-v
 \ge\frac34-2\alpha>0.
\]
Because \(C\) is an interval, its length is at least \(d\) on this event.  It follows that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C)]
 \ge\mathbb E_{P_0}[\operatorname{length}(C)]
 \ge d\left(\frac34-2\alpha\right)
 \ge\kappa\left(\frac34-2\alpha\right)\rho_{n,\Delta}.
\]
Taking the infimum over honest intervals proves the claimed lower bound.  Conversely, \(\mathrm{thm:total\text{-}honest\text{-}interval}\) puts \(C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}\) in the honest class and bounds its worst expected length by a constant multiple of \(\rho_{n,\Delta}\).  Using \(\mathrm{def:honest\text{-}width}\) gives
\[
 c_{L,\alpha,\Delta_0}\rho_{n,\Delta}
 \le\mathfrak W_{n,\Delta}(\alpha)
 \le C_{L,c_0,\alpha,\Delta_0}\rho_{n,\Delta},
\]
which is the asserted order statement.

semantic_closure.statement:
For every \(n\ge256\) and \(0<\Delta\le\Delta_0\), the handle \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}\) admits one same-class baseline--alternative realization with both difficulties present.  Specifically, put \(\kappa=c_L/4\), \(b_h(r)=(h_n-r)_+\),
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf 1\{0\le r<\Delta\},
 \qquad
 g_{n,\Delta}(r)=\kappa\{b_h(r)+a_\Delta(r)\}.
\]
There are \(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta}\in\mathcal P_L\) with \(m_{0,0}=m_{0,1}=1/2\), \(m_{1,0}=1/2\), and \(m_{1,1}=1/2+g_{n,\Delta}\), for which
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\!\left(\mathcal L_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n),
 \mathcal L_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n)\right)
 \le\frac14<1-2\alpha
\]
and
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)
 =\kappa(h_n+\Delta).
\]
semantic_closure.justification: One uniform-half-disc Bernoulli pair combines a localized sampling bump and the exact first-bin alias while charging released divergence only for the sampling component.
semantic_closure.gap: No cited comparator supplies this single pair for the latent-annular experiment with both order-\(n^{-1/4}\) and order-\(\Delta\) target displacement.
semantic_closure.consumer: The pair is the common same-class lower certificate for absolute risk, squared risk, and honest expected interval length.

semantic_closure.statement: For every \(n\geq256\) and \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), the interval \(C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}\) is defined for every released sample, satisfies \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb P_P(\tau_P(b)\in C_{n,\Delta,\alpha})\geq1-\alpha\), and obeys \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_{n,\Delta,\alpha})]\leq C_{L,c_0,\alpha,\Delta_0}\rho_{n,\Delta}\).
semantic_closure.justification: Conditional Hoeffding concentration plus sidewise Euclidean Lipschitz enlargement yields a total honest interval for bounded outcomes under unknown design.
semantic_closure.gap: Existing ordinary-running-variable intervals do not handle latent annuli, quadratic local mass, empty random side counts, and general bounded outcomes in this release field.
semantic_closure.consumer: The interval is directly implementable when an analyst truly receives only outcome, treatment side, and quantized radial distance.

semantic_closure.name: Unknown-design bivariate bounded-outcome point-anchored boundary class
semantic_closure.construction:
\(\mathcal P_L\) is the set of one-unit laws \(P\) such that \(P_X(\mathcal D)=1\); for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(H\in(0,1/2]\), \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\); \((\mathcal X_{0,P},\mathcal X_{1,P})\) is a known Borel partition of \(\mathcal D\) and \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\) almost surely; \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\) almost surely; for each \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the conditional law of \(Y(t)\) given \(X=x\) is supported on \([0,1]\) and has mean \(\mu_t(x)\); and the point-anchored envelope
\[
 |\mu_t(x)-\theta_t|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
\]
holds for every \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every side-\(t\) point \(x\) of radius at most \(1/2\), where \(\theta_t\in[0,1]\) and \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\).  The sampling condition \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) is imposed on the sample and is not a member property of a one-unit law.

semantic_closure.construction: \(\mathcal E_{n,\Delta}(P)=\mathcal L_P(Z_{\Delta,1},\ldots,Z_{\Delta,n}),\quad Z_{\Delta,i}=(Y_i,T_i,\Delta\lfloor R_i/\Delta\rfloor)\). The observation \(\sigma\)-field is exactly \(\sigma(Z_{\Delta,1},\ldots,Z_{\Delta,n})\); it excludes \(X_i\), angle, and raw \(R_i\).

semantic_closure.name: Embedded uniform-half-disc joint lower handle
semantic_closure.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}=(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta})\) denote the following pair.  Under both laws, \(X\) is uniform on \(\mathcal D\), \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assignment is sharp, and the control mean is \(1/2\).  Under \(P_{0,n,\Delta}\) the treated mean is \(1/2\); under \(P_{1,n,\Delta}\) it is
\[
 \frac12+\frac{c_L}{4}\left\{(h_n-\lVert x-b\rVert_2)_+
 +\Delta\phi\!\left(\frac{\lVert x-b\rVert_2}{\Delta}\right)
 \mathbf1\{\lVert x-b\rVert_2<\Delta\}\right\}.
\]
Given \(X\), the potential outcomes are conditionally independent Bernoulli variables with these means, and \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\).

semantic_closure.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  For every event \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) with \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\), the conditional outcome is supported on \([0,1]\) and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid B]=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
In particular, put \(A_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Then \(A_t=\{T=t,R<H_{n,\Delta}\}\), its probability \(q_t\) is at least \(c_0H_{n,\Delta}^2>0\), and, with
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t],
\]
one has \(|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|\leq LH_{n,\Delta}\) and \(N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\).  Conditional on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\geq1\), list the selected outcomes in increasing sample-index order as \(Y_{t,1}^{\star},\ldots,Y_{t,k}^{\star}\).  They are independent and identically distributed, supported on \([0,1]\), and have common mean \(\nu_t\); moreover,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{j=1}^kY_{t,j}^{\star},\qquad
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right]=\nu_t,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right)\leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
Outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass, the conditional sum need not be binomial.
semantic_closure.justification: The lemma supplies the conditional iid selected-outcome law, random-count distribution, bounded variance, and point-anchor bias for the bounded-outcome superclass.
semantic_closure.gap: The selected sum is not binomial outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass; the usable general statement is conditional iid bounded sampling with a common mean.
semantic_closure.consumer: The local estimator uses its variance bound, and the total interval uses its conditional product law.

semantic_closure.statement: For every \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), \(\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du=0\), both \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}\) and \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}\) belong to \(\mathcal P_L\), their released one-unit laws of \(Z_\Delta\) are identical, and \(\tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}}(b)=2c_L\Delta\).
semantic_closure.justification: This certifies an exact order-\(\Delta\) alias in a legal uniform-half-disc subclass of the unknown-design point-anchored model, without asserting design-wide orthogonality.
semantic_closure.gap: Scalar rounding results do not furnish the radial-Jacobian null direction for a release that hides bivariate coordinates within annuli.
semantic_closure.consumer: Data stewards using released radial bins can see that no sample size removes the first-bin resolution floor.

semantic_closure.name: Bias-enlarged conditional-Hoeffding interval
semantic_closure.construction:
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), set \([\ell_t,u_t]=[0,1]\) when \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=0\).  When \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k>0\), put
\[
 \overline Y_t=\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k,
 \qquad

 \qquad
 [\ell_t,u_t]=\bigl[\max\{0,\overline Y_t-r_{k,\alpha}\},\min\{1,\overline Y_t+r_{k,\alpha}\}\bigr].
\]
With \(B_{n,\Delta}=LH_{n,\Delta}\), define the closed bounded interval
\[
 C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}
 =\bigl[\ell_1-u_0-2B_{n,\Delta},\ u_1-\ell_0+2B_{n,\Delta}\bigr].
\]

semantic_closure.statement:
Let \(k\geq1\), and let \(W_1,\ldots,W_k\) be independent random variables satisfying \(0\leq W_j\leq1\) almost surely and \(\mathbb E[W_j]=p\) for every \(j\).  Then, for every \(r\) satisfying \(0<r<1-p\),
\[
 \mathbb P\!\left(\frac1k\sum_{j=1}^kW_j-p\geq r\right)\leq\exp(-2kr^2).
\]

semantic_closure.construction:
For each sign, construct \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{\pm,\Delta}\) by drawing \(X\) uniformly on \(\mathcal D\), taking \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assigning \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\), and drawing conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes given \(X\) with

\]
Finally set \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\), where \(\phi(u)=(1-u)(1-2u)\) and \(c_L=\min\{L/8,1/16\}\).

semantic_closure.name: Released-law identified set and maximal fiber diameter
semantic_closure.construction:
For \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), let
\[
 \mathcal Q_\Delta=\{\mathcal L_P(Z_\Delta):P\in\mathcal P_L\}.
\]
For every \(Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta\), define the nonempty release-fiber identified set and its diameter by
\[
 I_\Delta(Q)=\{\tau_P(b):P\in\mathcal P_L\ \text{and}\ \mathcal L_P(Z_\Delta)=Q\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{diam} I_\Delta(Q)=\sup_{a,a'\in I_\Delta(Q)}|a-a'|.
\]
The maximal population ambiguity of the rounded release is
\[
 \omega_\Delta=\sup_{Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta}\operatorname{diam} I_\Delta(Q).
\]

For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), let \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{T_i=t,Q_\Delta(R_i)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Define
\[
 \widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}=
 \begin{cases}
 \Pi_{[0,1]}\!\left(S_{t,n,\Delta}/N_{t,n,\Delta}\right),&N_{t,n,\Delta}>0,\\
 1/2,&N_{t,n,\Delta}=0,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad

\]
where \(\Pi_{[0,1]}\) is Euclidean clipping, and set \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}=\widehat m_{1,n,\Delta}-\widehat m_{0,n,\Delta}\).

carrier.proof_tex:
This is an algebraic specialization of the proved frontiers.  If \(0<\Delta\le n^{-1/4}=h_n\), then
\[
 \rho_{n,\Delta}=\max\{h_n,\Delta\}=h_n=n^{-1/4}.
\]
Substitution into \(\mathrm{thm:minimax\text{-}frontier}\) gives absolute-risk order \(n^{-1/4}\) and squared-risk order \(n^{-1/2}\); substitution into \(\mathrm{thm:honest\text{-}length\text{-}lower}\), including its upper bound from \(\mathrm{thm:total\text{-}honest\text{-}interval}\), gives honest expected-length order \(n^{-1/4}\).

If instead \(n^{-1/4}=o(\Delta)\) along a sequence, then \(h_n/\Delta\to0\), so eventually \(h_n<\Delta\) and
\[
 \rho_{n,\Delta}=\Delta.
\]
The same two frontier results then give absolute-risk and honest-length order \(\Delta\), and squared-risk order \(\Delta^2\).  The constants are uniform over the stated ranges because the parent theorems' constants are.

target_declaration.statement: Along every sequence with \(0<\Delta\leq n^{-1/4}\), the unknown-design frontier has minimax absolute-error and honest expected-length order \(n^{-1/4}\) and squared-risk order \(n^{-1/2}\).  Along every sequence with \(n^{-1/4}=o(\Delta)\), the corresponding orders are \(\Delta\) and \(\Delta^2\), respectively.
target_declaration.justification: This proposition separates the fine-quantization sampling regime from the coarsening-dominated population-ambiguity regime.

semantic_closure.name: Unknown-design bivariate bounded-outcome point-anchored boundary class
semantic_closure.construction:
\(\mathcal P_L\) is the set of one-unit laws \(P\) such that \(P_X(\mathcal D)=1\); for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(H\in(0,1/2]\), \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\); \((\mathcal X_{0,P},\mathcal X_{1,P})\) is a known Borel partition of \(\mathcal D\) and \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\) almost surely; \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\) almost surely; for each \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the conditional law of \(Y(t)\) given \(X=x\) is supported on \([0,1]\) and has mean \(\mu_t(x)\); and the point-anchored envelope
\[
 |\mu_t(x)-\theta_t|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
\]
holds for every \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every side-\(t\) point \(x\) of radius at most \(1/2\), where \(\theta_t\in[0,1]\) and \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\).  The sampling condition \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) is imposed on the sample and is not a member property of a one-unit law.

semantic_closure.name: Rounded-radius observation experiment
semantic_closure.construction: \(\mathcal E_{n,\Delta}(P)=\mathcal L_P(Z_{\Delta,1},\ldots,Z_{\Delta,n}),\quad Z_{\Delta,i}=(Y_i,T_i,\Delta\lfloor R_i/\Delta\rfloor)\). The observation \(\sigma\)-field is exactly \(\sigma(Z_{\Delta,1},\ldots,Z_{\Delta,n})\); it excludes \(X_i\), angle, and raw \(R_i\).

semantic_closure.name: Total bin-aware local-constant estimator
semantic_closure.construction:
For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), let \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{T_i=t,Q_\Delta(R_i)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Define
\[
 \widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}=
 \begin{cases}
 \Pi_{[0,1]}\!\left(S_{t,n,\Delta}/N_{t,n,\Delta}\right),&N_{t,n,\Delta}>0,\\
 1/2,&N_{t,n,\Delta}=0,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 H_{n,\Delta}=\Delta\left\lceil n^{-1/4}/\Delta\right\rceil,
\]
where \(\Pi_{[0,1]}\) is Euclidean clipping, and set \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}=\widehat m_{1,n,\Delta}-\widehat m_{0,n,\Delta}\).

semantic_closure.name: Rounded-radius minimax risks
semantic_closure.construction: \(\mathfrak R^{(1)}_{n,\Delta}=\inf_{\widetilde\tau\in\mathcal T_{n,\Delta}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P|\widetilde\tau-\tau_P(b)|\) and \(\mathfrak R^{(2)}_{n,\Delta}=\inf_{\widetilde\tau\in\mathcal T_{n,\Delta}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau_P(b))^2]\).

semantic_closure.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  For every event \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) with \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\), the conditional outcome is supported on \([0,1]\) and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid B]=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
In particular, put \(A_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Then \(A_t=\{T=t,R<H_{n,\Delta}\}\), its probability \(q_t\) is at least \(c_0H_{n,\Delta}^2>0\), and, with
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t],
\]
one has \(|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|\leq LH_{n,\Delta}\) and \(N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\).  Conditional on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\geq1\), list the selected outcomes in increasing sample-index order as \(Y_{t,1}^{\star},\ldots,Y_{t,k}^{\star}\).  They are independent and identically distributed, supported on \([0,1]\), and have common mean \(\nu_t\); moreover,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{j=1}^kY_{t,j}^{\star},\qquad
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right]=\nu_t,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right)\leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
Outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass, the conditional sum need not be binomial.
semantic_closure.justification: The lemma supplies the conditional iid selected-outcome law, random-count distribution, bounded variance, and point-anchor bias for the bounded-outcome superclass.
semantic_closure.gap: The selected sum is not binomial outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass; the usable general statement is conditional iid bounded sampling with a common mean.
semantic_closure.consumer: The local estimator uses its variance bound, and the total interval uses its conditional product law.

semantic_closure.statement:
For every \(n\ge256\) and \(0<\Delta\le\Delta_0\), the handle \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}\) admits one same-class baseline--alternative realization with both difficulties present.  Specifically, put \(\kappa=c_L/4\), \(b_h(r)=(h_n-r)_+\),
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf 1\{0\le r<\Delta\},
 \qquad
 g_{n,\Delta}(r)=\kappa\{b_h(r)+a_\Delta(r)\}.
\]
There are \(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta}\in\mathcal P_L\) with \(m_{0,0}=m_{0,1}=1/2\), \(m_{1,0}=1/2\), and \(m_{1,1}=1/2+g_{n,\Delta}\), for which
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\!\left(\mathcal L_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n),
 \mathcal L_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n)\right)
 \le\frac14<1-2\alpha
\]
and
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)
 =\kappa(h_n+\Delta).
\]
semantic_closure.justification: One uniform-half-disc Bernoulli pair combines a localized sampling bump and the exact first-bin alias while charging released divergence only for the sampling component.
semantic_closure.gap: No cited comparator supplies this single pair for the latent-annular experiment with both order-\(n^{-1/4}\) and order-\(\Delta\) target displacement.
semantic_closure.consumer: The pair is the common same-class lower certificate for absolute risk, squared risk, and honest expected interval length.

semantic_closure.statement:

semantic_closure.name: Embedded uniform-half-disc joint lower handle
semantic_closure.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}=(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta})\) denote the following pair.  Under both laws, \(X\) is uniform on \(\mathcal D\), \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assignment is sharp, and the control mean is \(1/2\).  Under \(P_{0,n,\Delta}\) the treated mean is \(1/2\); under \(P_{1,n,\Delta}\) it is
\[
 \frac12+\frac{c_L}{4}\left\{(h_n-\lVert x-b\rVert_2)_+
 +\Delta\phi\!\left(\frac{\lVert x-b\rVert_2}{\Delta}\right)
 \mathbf1\{\lVert x-b\rVert_2<\Delta\}\right\}.
\]
Given \(X\), the potential outcomes are conditionally independent Bernoulli variables with these means, and \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\).

semantic_closure.name: Bias-enlarged conditional-Hoeffding interval
semantic_closure.construction:
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), set \([\ell_t,u_t]=[0,1]\) when \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=0\).  When \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k>0\), put
\[
 \overline Y_t=\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k,
 \qquad
 r_{k,\alpha}=\sqrt{\frac{\log(4/\alpha)}{2k}},
 \qquad
 [\ell_t,u_t]=\bigl[\max\{0,\overline Y_t-r_{k,\alpha}\},\min\{1,\overline Y_t+r_{k,\alpha}\}\bigr].
\]
With \(B_{n,\Delta}=LH_{n,\Delta}\), define the closed bounded interval
\[
 C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}
 =\bigl[\ell_1-u_0-2B_{n,\Delta},\ u_1-\ell_0+2B_{n,\Delta}\bigr].
\]

semantic_closure.statement:
Let \(k\geq1\), and let \(W_1,\ldots,W_k\) be independent random variables satisfying \(0\leq W_j\leq1\) almost surely and \(\mathbb E[W_j]=p\) for every \(j\).  Then, for every \(r\) satisfying \(0<r<1-p\),
\[
 \mathbb P\!\left(\frac1k\sum_{j=1}^kW_j-p\geq r\right)\leq\exp(-2kr^2).
\]

semantic_closure.name: Released-law identified set and maximal fiber diameter
semantic_closure.construction:
For \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), let
\[
 \mathcal Q_\Delta=\{\mathcal L_P(Z_\Delta):P\in\mathcal P_L\}.
\]
For every \(Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta\), define the nonempty release-fiber identified set and its diameter by
\[
 I_\Delta(Q)=\{\tau_P(b):P\in\mathcal P_L\ \text{and}\ \mathcal L_P(Z_\Delta)=Q\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{diam} I_\Delta(Q)=\sup_{a,a'\in I_\Delta(Q)}|a-a'|.
\]
The maximal population ambiguity of the rounded release is
\[
 \omega_\Delta=\sup_{Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta}\operatorname{diam} I_\Delta(Q).
\]

semantic_closure.name: Embedded uniform-half-disc exact first-bin alias pair
semantic_closure.construction:
For each sign, construct \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{\pm,\Delta}\) by drawing \(X\) uniformly on \(\mathcal D\), taking \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assigning \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\), and drawing conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes given \(X\) with
\[
 \mu_{0,\pm}(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mu_{1,\pm}(x)=\frac12\pm c_L\Delta\phi\!\left(\frac{\lVert x-b\rVert_2}{\Delta}\right)
 \mathbf1\{\lVert x-b\rVert_2<\Delta\}.
\]
Finally set \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\), where \(\phi(u)=(1-u)(1-2u)\) and \(c_L=\min\{L/8,1/16\}\).

semantic_closure.name: I_\Delta
semantic_closure.def: The set of structural point boundary effects compatible with a fixed one-unit released law, defined in \(\mathrm{def:released\text{-}identified\text{-}set}\).

payload.what_is_open: Equality in the release-law-specific endpoint map and the exact value, rather than order, of \(\omega_\Delta\) over the full unknown-design class remain open.
payload.obstruction: The released law fixes the distribution of \((Y,T,Q_\Delta(R))\) but not the latent within-bin score disintegrations.  The frozen endpoint handle does not specify the joint kernel variables and full outcome-distribution constraints needed to prove that every candidate endpoint is attainable; the local-mass inequalities also couple feasible disintegrations across all shrinking radii.  The first-bin mean restriction alone therefore proves an outer interval but not sharpness.
payload.attempted: The proof projects each compatible law onto the observable first-bin means, optimizes the point-anchor envelope to obtain explicit endpoint bounds, and uses the exact uniform-half-disc alias for an attainable diameter lower witness.  Extending that construction to arbitrary \(Q\) fails because matching a general released outcome law requires a feasible latent outcome kernel, not merely matching its mean.
payload.partial_result:
For every attainable release law \(Q\), the first-bin side probabilities are positive and the observable conditional means \(\eta_t(Q)=\mathbb E_Q[Y\mid T=t,Q_\Delta(R)=0]\) are defined.  The proved, computable outer endpoint map is
\[
 I_\Delta(Q)\subseteq
 [\underline\theta_1(Q)-\overline\theta_0(Q),
   \overline\theta_1(Q)-\underline\theta_0(Q)],
\]
where
\[
 \underline\theta_t(Q)=\max\{0,\eta_t(Q)-L\Delta\},
 \qquad
 \overline\theta_t(Q)=\min\{1,\eta_t(Q)+L\Delta\}.
\]
Moreover, \(2c_L\Delta\le\omega_\Delta\le4L\Delta\).  This is an outer bound, not a sharp endpoint characterization.

payload.justification: Exact endpoints would upgrade the computable first-bin outer interval to a sharp release-law-specific partial-identification procedure.
payload.gap: The full latent-disintegration program, including the released outcome-distribution and all-radius local-mass constraints, is not yet solved.
payload.consumer: A future solution would let data stewards report the narrowest compatible population interval rather than the present certified outer interval.

payload.tldr: An analyst observes only \(Z_\Delta=(Y,T,Q_\Delta(R))\): bounded outcome, sharp-treatment side, and floor-rounded distance from one fixed boundary point; raw location, polar angle, and raw radius are unavailable.  The structural boundary effect is generally only partially identified at fixed release precision.  Its release-fiber identified set is \(I_\Delta(Q)\), and its maximal diameter satisfies \(2c_L\Delta\leq\omega_\Delta\leq4L\Delta\).  A computable first-bin envelope gives release-law-specific outer endpoints, while exact sharp endpoints remain open.  Supporting statistical results show that minimax absolute error and honest expected length have order \(\max\{n^{-1/4},\Delta\}\), with squared risk of the corresponding squared order.

project_justification.gap: Exact-coordinate boundary methods do not describe the identified set after angle and within-bin radius are removed.  Scalar measurement-error methods require auxiliary discrepancy information to restore identification, and manipulation-based partial-identification methods address latent assignment types rather than a known deterministic annular release; neither evaluates the release fiber of a fixed bivariate point-boundary effect.
project_justification.niche: The released population law fixes annular outcome distributions but not the latent boundary anchors.  The radial Jacobian admits an exact first-bin null direction, creating order-\(\Delta\) causal ambiguity even with an infinite sample.
project_justification.fill: The paper fixes the analyst's observation \(\sigma\)-field, defines the release-fiber identified set \(I_\Delta(Q)\), gives a computable first-bin outer endpoint map, and bounds the worst fiber diameter between \(2c_L\Delta\) and \(4L\Delta\).  Supporting minimax-risk and honest-length frontiers then separate this population ambiguity from the additional \(n^{-1/4}\) sampling cost.

sampling_model.design: For each law \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), the latent score \(X\) is supported on the unit disc centered at \(b\), with each known assignment side having probability at least \(c_0H^2\) inside every radius \(H\in(0,1/2]\).  The design distribution is otherwise unknown; the uniform two-sided half-disc is used only as an embedded lower-bound subclass.
sampling_model.units: The primitive observations \((X_i,Y_i(0),Y_i(1))_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed, but the analyst receives only \(Z_{\Delta,i}=(Y_i,T_i,Q_\Delta(R_i))\).  Raw locations, polar angles, and raw radii are excluded from the observation \(\sigma\)-field.
sampling_model.overlap: No unit-level treatment-overlap condition is imposed because assignment is deterministic.  Instead, the two-sided quadratic local-mass condition requires \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\) for each \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and every \(H\in(0,1/2]\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No design density is estimated.  The estimator and interval use only released local counts and outcome sums, the known bin-aligned bandwidth \(H_{n,\Delta}=\Delta\lceil n^{-1/4}/\Delta\rceil\), and the known point-anchor envelope constant \(L\); they do not use raw coordinates or a known local side probability.

payload.related_work: DaveziesLeBarbanchon2017 shows that continuous measurement error can destroy ordinary scalar regression-discontinuity identification and recovers a local effect using auxiliary discrepancy information under additional conditions.  No such auxiliary sample exists here.  GerardRokkanenRothe2020 derives sharp bounds under latent manipulation types, whereas the ambiguity here is induced by a known annular release.  DongKolesar2023Measurement studies causal targets compatible with correctly classified coarsened scores, and Dong2015Rounding inverts scalar within-cell moment structure; neither recovers this fixed latent boundary anchor from side and rounded radius alone.  KolesarRothe2018Discrete addresses inference with a discrete scalar running score but does not calculate a bivariate annular release fiber.  CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance is an exact-distance comparator only: its exact-coordinate results do not transfer to a release that suppresses angle and within-bin radius.  ArmstrongKolesar2018Optimal informs the two-point modulus logic, and ArmstrongKolesar2020Honest informs explicit smoothness-bias enlargement; the joint pair and conditional random-count argument are derived here.  CattaneoTitiunikYu2025Rd2d documents the R, Python, and Stata workflows that can consume these conclusions only after verifying the stated coarsening field.
payload.interpretation: The causal estimand remains the full-data boundary contrast \(\tau_P(b)=\theta_1-\theta_0\).  The observed-law object \(I_\Delta(Q)\) is the set of causal values compatible with one released population law; it is not the estimand by definition.  At fixed \(\Delta>0\), the release need not determine the target uniquely, and \(\omega_\Delta\asymp\Delta\) measures the worst ambiguity.  Finite sampling adds the \(n^{-1/4}\) boundary-regression scale, so \(\Delta\leq n^{-1/4}\) is sample-limited while \(n^{-1/4}=o(\Delta)\) is release-precision-limited.
payload.technical_internal_limitation: The outer fiber map and statistical upper bounds cover the full unknown-design, \([0,1]\)-bounded-outcome class, but they require the declared quadratic local-mass constant, known side partition, fixed boundary point, and point-anchored Lipschitz envelope.  The matching lower bounds embed a uniform half-disc with Bernoulli potential outcomes; this is a legal subclass certificate, not a restriction of the main class.  The release-law-specific endpoint interval is proved only as an outer bound, and the exact maximal-diameter constant remains open.  The results do not apply when raw coordinates, polar angle, or within-bin radius remain available.
payload.honest_scope: The headline partial-identification result is the release-fiber map with a computable first-bin outer interval and worst diameter satisfying \(2c_L\Delta\leq\omega_\Delta\leq4L\Delta\); exact release-law-specific endpoints and the sharp maximal-diameter constant remain open.  The minimax-risk and honest-length theorems are supporting statistical results, uniform over \(n\geq256\) and \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and do not claim sharp leading constants.  Applicability requires that the observation field be exactly \(\sigma(Z_{\Delta,1},\ldots,Z_{\Delta,n})\).

statement_notes.justification: This is the headline partial-identification result: it separates the full-data causal target from the released-law identified set and quantifies fixed-precision population ambiguity.
statement_notes.gap: Exact-coordinate and scalar discrete-score results do not calculate the radial two-sided release-fiber diameter over this point-anchored class.
statement_notes.consumer: Data stewards can report a release-law-specific outer interval and the worst order of causal information lost by publishing only side and rounded radius.

statement_notes.justification: This supporting statistical theorem matches an observed-count estimator with one same-class lower pair and separates sampling error from the order-\(\Delta\) population ambiguity.
statement_notes.gap: Exact-radius boundary methods and scalar rounding methods do not derive the unknown-design latent-annular frontier \(\max\{n^{-1/4},\Delta\}\).
statement_notes.consumer: Users can diagnose sample-limited and release-precision-limited regimes only when no within-bin coordinates are available.

statement_notes.justification: Conditional Hoeffding concentration and explicit sidewise point-anchor bias enlargement yield a total interval, including at zero local counts.
statement_notes.gap: Ordinary-running-variable intervals do not directly handle latent annuli, unknown bivariate design, quadratic local mass, bounded non-Bernoulli outcomes, and no within-bin coordinate.
statement_notes.consumer: The interval is implementable from outcome, treatment side, rounded radius, the smoothness envelope, and observed local counts.

statement_notes.justification: The same sampling-plus-aliasing pair forces every uniformly honest interval to cover two separated causal values with positive probability under one released law.
statement_notes.gap: General modulus and discrete-score results do not evaluate this radial \(n^{-1/4}\)-to-\(\Delta\) transition.
statement_notes.consumer: The result certifies the conditional-Hoeffding interval's rate without using unavailable within-bin information.
